items.statement: The plat is the single spatial truth: every area (sea, river, district, block, plot, yard, footprint) is a face and every line (street, alley, wall, shore, plot line) an edge, in integer centimetres, refined in five coarse-to-fine levels so a change at one level touches only what lies under it. Plain-words restatement of §2.2.
Every record carries provenance (which rule, which random stream) and a lifecycle history (generated, edited, pinned, built, converted, demolished). Plain-words restatement of §2.8.
Three model layers exist from the start (underground, ground, sky), so the owner-staged sewers and floating islands need no change of the model.
Every model length is an integer number of centimetres (i32); world centred on (0,0), +x east, +y north (as FTG, _critic-ftg.md F1), inside the arena frame of §3.2 (9).
Twice-areas and ring orientation are §3.2 (6)'s exact integer predicates; directions are §3.2 (5)'s (reference, not restated).
Heights are centimetres; angles, where stored, are i32 centidegrees, named ...Cdeg or typed Cdeg (§2.8 type list).
A length field carries its unit either in its name (...Cm, ...M) or in a unit-branded type (Cm, M, CmArray, ChainProfile of Cm); a schema lint refuses any length field with neither (O6 (a), G-R14).

layer ∈ {underground, ground, sky} is a field on every geometric entity and every display-list item, with z: i32 (order inside the layer) and elevationCm: i32 (base elevation: an island's altitude; a sewer's negative depth).
Each layer has its own arena or its own parts (G-R11): the ground; one per underground system (the sewer network's is part 0; item 65); one per sky island; keyed by PlatKey (§2.2 rule 2).

items.owner: model (LayerSpec and setLayer referenced: rendering §8.4, determinism §7.1)
items.statement: Per-layer toggles, shadows and export hang off the one layer field; a layer's drawing and export settings are its LayerSpec (§8.4), edited by setLayer (§7.1).
The base populates only the ground layer; underground and sky are schema-complete and empty until their staged stages run.

Layer (unqualified) means one of the three model layers; the toggleable drawing groups of §8-§9 (labels, cadastral outlines, trees, annotations, thematic style overrides) are display-list groups selected by `semantic`, never a fourth model layer.
names: (distinct concept) display-list group selected by semantic

items.statement: Address id `kind:token`, prefixed with its arena outside the ground layer (sky2/plot:..., under/tunnel:..., under3/chamber:...): underground part 0 keeps under/, a further underground part n takes under<n>/, a sky island's part n takes sky<n>/. Edits, locks, assignments, pins, labels, households, exports and hosts point at it.
The lineage key (keying random streams), the anchor rule with its hysteresis radii, survival and succession, the JOIN rule and the one collision rule are §6.3's (LC-1, LC-29, GEO-34) — referenced.
In memory addresses are interned u32 handles, held by the kernel's owner and role tables; in the document they are strings.
The parent is a field (Identity.parent, §2.8), never parsed from the id; no record outside the kernel stores an arena slot (§2.2 rule 5).

The underground layer holds a family of systems, each in its own arena part (PlatKey; J-A65.31): part 0 = the sewer network's tunnels and, along its navigable runs, the underground neighbourhoods' blocks, plots and buildings (II.7.3); each further part = one system of II.7.6 (catacombs, caverns, quarries and mine voids, vaults, buried old town, or dug private passages) as an UndergroundSystem record with galleries, chambers and links (§2.7); the undercity's neighbourhoods in the part of the void they occupy (II.7.5).
An underground part number is allocated once and never reused (Document.nextUndergroundPart, §2.9).

Underground records live on under/ and under<n>/ prefixes and are populated only when the owner-staged network and underground stages run, or, for a dug system, when an access edit or an undercity lifeline's closure makes one once those stages exist (§7.3 item 9 (d), II.7.4; item 66).
Underground level mapping is §2.2 rule 1's; depth is elevationCm (negative below the ground datum, II.7.3, II.7.6).

Whether a layer exists is decided by what the model holds, never by a layer's visibility (item 14): Features.sewers for the network at a rung and Features.underground for the layer as a whole (§2.9, II.7.4).
Cm = integer centimetres (number); a number becomes an arena coordinate only through snap() (§3.2 (7)), in every build.
Level = 0|1|2|3|4: L0 land/water; L1 way skeleton; L2 kerbs, corridors, blocks; L3 plots + residue; L4 footprints + yard parts.

PlatKey = { layer, part }: part 0 = the ground, or the underground layer's sewer network; underground parts >= 1 = one arena per further system (catacombs, caverns, quarries and mine voids, vaults, buried old town, dug passages — II.7.6), each number allocated once at creation and never reused (§3.4; counter nextUndergroundPart §2.9); sky parts 1-3 = one arena per sky island (§4.2, II.1).
items.note: Sky parts 1-3 caps sky islands at three per map (agreement subject with II.6 and V05). The II.1 citation resolves: II.1's neighbourhood input carries the sky island's arena (the unit run on an island).

items.statement: VertexId, HalfEdgeId, FaceId = arena slots: kernel-internal, valid within one batch (rule 5).
Plat { key; frame; lattice; vertices; halfEdges; roles; faces[5]; index[5]; indexHome; version } — the per-arena planar structure.
Plat.frame is set at creation and replaced only by the frame growth of an epoch's upward rung crossing (§3.2 (9), §4.11; J-A81.41), which only grows it.

Plat.lattice is fixed for the arena's life; §3.2 (1)'s range bound is taken at the population cap and the extreme aspect so a grown frame keeps every old lattice point. LatticeSpec { unitCm 1; minEdgeCm 25; attractCm 26; minFaceAngleCdeg 500; rangeCm 8,388,608 (2^23) } — meaning in §3.2 (2), classes in §3.10.
vertices: x, y (Int32Array), out (one outgoing half-edge), level (Uint8: birth level; lowered by promotion, raised by demotion — rule 3), flags (Uint8: pinned | steiner | split | free slot).

Vertex flag `pinned` is set only by pinVertices (§3.4) and cleared when a batch strips the vertex's last vertex role row other than knot rows (rule 3 (b)); `split` is rule 3's, its clearing under moves is §3.6's.
halfEdges: origin, next, prev (Int32Array); twin(h) = h ^ 1 (allocated in pairs); level per pair (h >> 1) = the edge's birth level, always the lowest level among its role rows (rule 3).
roles: RoleTable — (role, entity, level, ordinal) sets on edge pairs and vertices, with a reverse index (rule 7).

faces: one LevelFaces per level; index: one LevelIndex per level (§3.3); indexHome: per slot the static index partition (numbered across the levels) whose build holds it, -1 if none, written by every build, read to tombstone (§3.3); version: bumped by every committed batch.

LevelFaces { outer; holesStart; holes; kind (Uint16); owner (interned entity handle); parent (level-1 face containing it; -1 at L0); stage (Uint8: rank in §4.1 order of the stage whose batch created or last re-owned the face — the kept-content rule, §3.3); nextOfOwner; ownerHead: OwnerTable }.

RoleTable { edgeFirst; vertexFirst (first slot of each set, -1 if none); kind (Uint16 interned RoleName); entity; level (batch level that added it); ordinal (Uint16; 0 unless registry declares role indexed, rule 7); nextInSet; nextSameKey; head: RoleHeadTable }.

RoleHeadTable and OwnerTable are typed-array hash tables (J-K22): open addressing, linear probing, capacity a power of two kept at load <= 0.5 (doubled and re-inserted in slot order when exceeded), fixed integer hash of the key words, deletion by backward shift (no tombstones); lookups only — nothing iterates a table — so its layout never reaches an output.
RoleHeadTable { k0 entity handle; k1 = role << 16 | ordinal; first (first role-row slot, -1 empty); count }; OwnerTable { owner (interned handle); head (first FaceId, -1 empty); count }.

LevelIndex { static: PackedIndex[] (one per arena at L0-L1; one per district plus one outside districts at L2-L4); dynamic: UniformGrid; tombstones: Set per static partition of keys (kind * 2^32 + slot; kind = vertex, route edge or face) tombstoned since its build, filtering that partition's hits only; when a set empties is §3.3's }.

RoleRow = { role; entity; ordinal? } — a row a writer adds; its level is always the adding batch's (rules 3, 7); an `anchor` contact name is given without ordinal, the kernel allocates it (§3.3 rule 2). RoleKey = { role; entity; ordinal } — a row's identity without level.

Geometry references (the only forms by which an entity, seam contract, edit event or API scope refers to geometry, rule 5): FaceRef {owner, level} = faces whose owner at that level is the entity; ChainRef {role, entity} = ordered edge chain carrying (role, entity) (way spine, wall trace, tunnel); EdgeSetRef {role, entity, ordinal?} = unordered edges (frontage, access, party walls, one gate opening); VertexRef {role, entity, ordinal?} = the vertex (junction, tower, gate, entrance, portal, deck end, water gate's bank end, weld end); StretchRef {chain, from, to: VertexRef|LatticePoint} = chain edges between two vertices, batch-local, never stored in an entity record.
LatticePoint = { x: Cm; y: Cm } — a position in an arena; which records may hold a vertex's position is rule 5's.
VertexSig { v: the vertex's own (role, entity, ordinal) rows sorted; e: the structural (role, entity) rows of its incident edges sorted, deduplicated }.

ChainProfile<T number|string> { knotRole (registry knot role: width_knot, base_knot, invert_knot, bank_knot, shore_class_knot ...); values[i] belongs to the chain vertex carrying (knotRole, entity, i): an authored value in the attribute's unit or a cut knot's exact sample; interp 'linear'|'step' } — never an array indexed by chain vertices.
Rule 1: everything with a boundary is a face; everything linear is an edge chain.
L0 faces are land and water only: land components, sea, lakes, river reaches, islets, ponds, moats.
Terrain contours and drainage lines are raster products (§2.3), never plat edges or faces, so no L1 face straddles two L0 parents and no drainage antenna enters a face ring.

The arena's outer ring (frame plus context margin, §3.2 (9)) is one L0 chain carrying the structural `margin` role on the arena's Terrain entity, written first by S1 before any water, so every L0 face has a boundary; a sea or river reaching it shares its stretch (§4.1).

L1 faces: coarse blocks (regions between way spines) and the wall strips S7 cuts beside each trace (§4.8). L1 edges: way spines (centrelines), wall lines, the wall strips' setback and glacis lines (role `setback`), shorelines inherited from L0, the map border, the settlement perimeter (a district_bound chain, §4.5) and district boundaries.
The map border is the frame rectangle, role `border` on the arena's Terrain entity, written first by S3's L1 batch after S3's L0 batch (§4.1).
District boundaries are always L1 edges — a spine, a wall line, a reservation boundary, a shore or the perimeter — so every finer face lies inside one district.

L2 refines each L1 face into one half-corridor strip along each spine edge (road reserve on that side, width = the way's half-width), one junction wedge at each corner and the remaining built block(s), built by corridorUnion (§3.7), so every L2 face nests in exactly one L1 face.

A Corridor entity is the FaceRef of the half-corridor faces on both sides of its spine; a Junction is the FaceRef of the wedges around its vertex; a Square is a corridor face of class `square` (G-R11).

L3 faces: plots, courts, yards, greens, alleys-as-faces and passage faces (a covered alley-as-face under a front building's wing — §2.5's Passage record, cut by S10 on §4.6's reach; item 30); the wall-band, setback and glacis parts (per side of the L1 wall chain, built by bandUnion inside the wall strips after S9, §3.7, §4.8; Enceinte.band = FaceRef of both sides); margin-band parts along the settlement perimeter and other shared non-spine district boundaries (§3.3 pool step 3); the hinterland's furlongs, lots, woods, driveways and trails, whose boundaries are L3 edges carrying field_bound.
A hedgerow is the green_line role on a field_bound edge; a track along one is the same edge with both roles (§4.9).
L4 faces: building footprints (and wing sub-faces when stage 3 exists) plus yard sub-areas.
Districts, blocks, merged plots and water bodies are multi-face FaceRefs, never single face ids.

Sewer network part (underground part 0) levels: L0 one land face — the rock — bounded by the arena's outer ring, a chain with structural `margin` role on the underground pseudo-district's record (II.7.3), written by the network stage before any tunnel; L1 tunnel centrelines (`tunnel` chains, never `way`: no street skeleton, U2); L2 tunnel bands — bore plus wall (Tunnel.widthCm, profile row's wall thickness, II.7.2) — as half-corridor strips and junction wedges built by corridorUnion (band's outer ring = the tunnel's external wall, the kerb frontage plots end on), the rock between as built blocks; L3 frontage plots, each fronting exactly one navigable open tunnel run (U1), and residue typed `rock`; L4 buildings flush against the kerb (U3).
The underground and the ground never share topology (rule 2): every surface constraint the underground reads is a query on the ground's key (§3.4; J-A12.32).

Further underground parts take the same five views: L0 rock face bounded by the part's outer ring (the ground's frame plus context margin, so every part grows with the frame by §3.2 (9), J-A65.22), a chain with structural `margin` role on its UndergroundSystem record, written by the system's stage before any gallery; L1 gallery centrelines (`gallery` chains, a system's passages and an undercity's walkways alike) and each chamber's closed outline chain with structural `chamber_wall` role (inside = the chamber floor, an L1 face); L2 gallery bands — bore plus wall (Gallery.widthCm, wallCm) — built by corridorUnion, and inside an undercity-settled chamber (II.7.5) walkway bands and built blocks; L3 frontage plots on a gallery's kerb, plots that may end on the chamber_wall, residue typed `rock`; L4 buildings under the chamber's ceiling (Chamber.ceilingCm).

Two arena parts never share a vertex: a link between elements of two parts names one vertex in each (UndergroundLink, §2.7, ends carrying `link_end` role); two systems crossing in plan without meeting are two parts, drawn over and under (§8.4).

Rule 2: one arena per PlatKey; the five levels are views of it (J-K1). All levels live in one vertex-and-half-edge arena and every edge carries its birth level; the level-n subdivision = edges of level <= n, so each level-n face is exactly the union of the level-(n+1) faces inside it; nesting holds by construction and is checked by index (§3.10).
A face walk at level n follows `next` and around each vertex skips edges of level > n (O(degree)).
A level's face records inside a parent face are materialised when the first edge of that level is inserted there; until then the parent face is its own child.
A shared boundary is one edge seen by every finer level (kerb, plot line, party wall), so a warp moves it once and two row houses share literally one wall edge.

The ground, each underground part and each sky island are separate arenas and never share topology: sky and underground geometry never cut ground faces; two underground parts never cut each other's; cross-arena links (island shadow footprint, sewer outfall, access point, underground link) are entity ids naming at most one vertex in each arena.

Rule 3: finer levels never move coarser geometry, with one bounded exception. A level-n batch creates vertices and edges of level n only (E_LEVEL otherwise; clearing finer content, promotion, demotion and warp moves excepted, §3.3, §3.6).

splitThrough: where a level-n batch needs a vertex on a coarser edge (plot line ending on a kerb, footprint corner on a plot line, band cross edge on its wall), it inserts a level-n Steiner vertex at the lattice point §3.6's placement rule chooses near the exact foot and routes the coarser edge through it, moving the route by at most half a lattice diagonal, 0.71 cm (61 % of 5-60 m edges have no interior lattice point, GEO-1).
The coarser edge's endpoints, birth level, faces and own-level roles never change under splitThrough; a finer batch may add roles of its own level (a plot's frontage on a kerb).

Level-n route of an edge: the chain through its vertices of level <= n; every level-n query, digest (§6.2) and stage reads it, so no level-n result depends on whether or when a finer level was derived (lazy per-district stages included).

A same-level split, a promotion, a demotion or a dissolution adds a vertex to a route or removes one and moves nothing (J-K32), so the hot pixel bounds placement, not a standing distance (§3.6, §3.10), and the index boxes each route edge over the vertices on its run (§3.3).

Promotion (J-K11): a coarser batch ending a chain on a route that already carries a finer vertex kept beside it (a neighbour's plot-line end where II.1 (3)'s neighbour step lands its corridor_split edge; a close-up's kept fabric beside a new L1 junction) attracts onto that vertex and promotes it: its birth level drops to the batch's level, adding it to the coarser route (it lies within the route's hot pixel, §3.6) without moving it or touching finer faces. It keeps its split flag (removing the promoting chain restores the edge by demotion).
The commit record lists every promotion and the undo record restores the birth levels (§3.6).

A coarse batch inserted into finished fabric (carve, re-carved reach, outer moat) clears finer content only inside its declared clear region and meets finer geometry only at the vertices prepared for that contact, which it promotes (§3.3 clear-region rules).
A kept way's straight L1 edge between its two promoted bank vertices becomes the deck span over the new water (rule 7; J-I12).

Dissolution: clearFiner (regeneration, undo) and removeEdges remove edges and roles, then dissolve each vertex left with degree 2 that carries the split flag, no vertex role and no pin, and whose two remaining edges carry identical role sets and one birth level.

The split flag marks a vertex whose dissolution restores exactly the edge it was created on. Set when a vertex is created on an existing edge (split foot, crossing, every Steiner vertex); cleared (a) by a promotion making it a coarse chain's own vertex (prepared contact §3.3 rule 3, or stretch end §3.4); (b) by a move of it or of the nearest vertex beside it on a run it split (§3.6 "split flag under moves"); (c) by a removal breaking the run it split (demotion (b)). A promotion onto the route it already lies on (§3.6 candidate (b)) keeps it. A chain's own shape vertices never carry it.

Levels follow the rows — demotion (J-K28): a row is added at the adding batch's level, never coarser than its edge or vertex (a coarser chain never shares a finer edge, §3.6; promotion is the only way a vertex becomes coarser), so an edge's birth level is the lowest level among its rows; removeEdges, clearFiner and retypeEdges' remove (§3.4) end, after stripping rows and deleting edges left with none, with three steps (a) edges, (b) flags, (c) vertices.

Demotion (a) edges: an edge whose remaining rows are all above its birth level takes the lowest of them (a quay on an old shore stretch left with its way row when a moved river takes shore and bank rows becomes L1, as does a wall on an old bank), so the L0 view stays land and water only.

Demotion (b) flags: a split vertex keeps its flag only while a run it split survives the batch whole — a pair of its incident edges of its lowest incident level that carried identical rows of that level before the batch still exists after it, at one level, with identical rows (a crossing has two such pairs, a T-junction one); otherwise cleared (where a quay left the old shore stretch it shared, that point becomes a shape vertex of the quay; a quay sharing the whole stretch on both sides of a street end keeps that end restorable).

Demotion (b) pins: a vertex from which the batch strips its last vertex role row other than knot rows loses its kernel pinned flag (a pin guards the feature its role names — gate, junction, portal, deck, gate, weld or anchor end; §3.4 pinVertices); so a deck's bank vertices that F-REDERIVE removes become plain way vertices keeping any knot row, and a water gate's bank vertex left on an unchanged shore can dissolve.

Demotion (c) vertices, in canonical order (y, then x), each reading levels the earlier left: a vertex with no incident edge and no vertex role row of its level or coarser takes the lowest level among its incident edges and vertex role rows (with neither it is freed), as an old shore stretch's L0 vertices do.

A deck's bank vertex left over land by moved water takes its way's level at once when its deck_end rows are L1 (placed by a preparation batch), and keeps L0 with no L0 edge at it while they are L0 (placed by an L0 batch; which batch places them at which level is §4.2 S1 (5)'s), until F-REDERIVE removes the deck's deck and deck_end rows (§7.3 (b) 9).

Split restoration (after dissolution): a split vertex whose incident edges of its level or coarser are exactly two, of one level, with identical rows of its level or coarser, carrying no vertex role row of its level or coarser and no pin, but still meeting finer edges or carrying finer vertex role rows, takes the lowest level among those finer edges and rows and keeps its flag. The flag is the whole guard: it stands only while neither the vertex nor its run neighbours moved since it split the run, so restoring gives the run's route before its promotion, changed only by same-level vertices added/removed since.

Split restoration bar: a plot-line end or footprint corner promoted to L2 by II.1 (3)'s neighbour step returns to its level when the street is removed (undo, district reroll, later edit) and the kerb's L2 route, index and digest equal those before the step — restored vertex for vertex on 100,000 of 100,000 random routes (docs/validation/bench/fixall_kernel_r4_checks.out A), and by construction for any number of later same-level vertices.
A promoted vertex that a move has unflagged stays in the coarser route, which is then its true shape.

Each demotion re-indexes the items it changes (§3.3 "No item changes in place") and re-walks faces beside a demoted edge at the levels it no longer bounds (§3.6 step 5); per-level digests read current levels (§6.2); the commit record lists the demotions and cleared flags, which the undo record restores (§3.3, §7.4); §3.10's level-consistency row checks the result on every batch.

Rule 4: edges enter only through insertChain — one door for generated chains, user strokes, boolean and buffer outputs, offsets and smoothing results (§3.4; snapping, attraction, shared stretches, placement, crossings and local re-walk are §3.6's).
Faces are never re-walked globally; a split face's two parts both inherit its owner and stage rank until the stage re-owns one (§3.6 step 5).

Rule 5: topology by index, references by role (J-K3, J-K9). Inside the kernel topology is keyed by VertexId, HalfEdgeId and FaceId, never by object identity or coordinates (the 2017 shared-Point topology and FTG's coincident-intersection bug are the two failures, os-geometry.md §1.1, FTG 153121107).

No record outside the kernel stores arena slots, and no entity record stores a vertex's position — except a building's wing rings, its stored stage-3 composition's and plan's rings and points, and its tower centres (§2.6), whose boundary points are footprint vertices re-read by §2.6's wing-carrying rule after every footprint change so they cannot go stale.

Otherwise vertex positions live only in log events (with a VertexSig), view state, label placements and StretchRef ends; a point that is not a vertex (a river's control knot, a pin's or decoration's point, a tree override, a point light's point, an access point's ground point, a Works' kept rings and lines) is an ordinary attribute of its record (§2.3, §2.7, II.7.4, §7.4); one inside a building (a basement ring's point, a stored composition's or plan's point off the footprint boundary) is carried with its building by mean-value coordinates (§2.6 rule 2 (b)).

An entity reaches its geometry through the kernel role and owner tables, resolved on demand by resolve (§3.4): ChainRef('way', wayId) a way's spine; FaceRef(plotId, 3) a plot; VertexRef('junction', id); a bridge's deck ends VertexRef('deck_end', bridgeId, 0|1); a water gate's bank ends VertexRef('gate_end', gateId, 0|1); a castle's weld ends VertexRef('weld', castleId, 0|1); an open wall's end anchors VertexRef('anchor', enceinteId, 0|1); a reservation's attach points VertexRef('attach', reservationId, i); a plot bound's gate openings EdgeSetRef('gate_opening', boundId, i).

Roles survive topology changes: splits carry roles to both parts, merges union them, attraction merges them onto the surviving edge or vertex, promotion keeps them (except a prepared anchor contact name, which it strips, rule 7) and warp moves the vertex carrying them, so a stored reference cannot go stale — nothing to rewrite (GEO-5 (a)). How a warp treats kernel-pinned vertices and vertices of locked/pinned entities is §3.6's (GEO-5 (c)).

Stretches (J-K31): an operator that removes or hands over part of a chain (carve's cut stretch, pruned remainder, kept way's replaced stretch, moved river's old shore stretch, stretch between two bank anchors, way split, partial wallToWay) names it by StretchRef: the chain's edges between two of its vertices, in chain order for an open chain and, for a ring, from `from` counter-clockwise to `to` (orientation by orient2d at the lowest-leftmost vertex, §3.2 (6)), so a ring's two stretches differ without a stored direction.

Each StretchRef end names a chain vertex by a vertex role or by its lattice point (unique per lattice point, §3.10); a cut end not yet a vertex is placed first by splitThrough, which may give it a vertex role row; a StretchRef is resolved within its batch, never stored in an entity record; removeEdges and retypeEdges apply it as §3.4 states.

Chain attributes are knot profiles, never positional arrays (J-K10): a value varying along a chain (way width, wall base elevation, tunnel invert, shore bank kind and shore class) is a ChainProfile whose knots are vertices of the entity's own-level route carrying the registry's knot role with an ordinal (('width_knot', wayId, i)); between consecutive knots interpolated linearly by arc length along that route (linear) or held to the next knot (step, categorical); constant before the first and after the last knot of an open chain; a ring interpolates cyclically; a chain of several rings has at least one knot per ring and never interpolates across rings; a constant attribute is a scalar with no knots.

The creating stage places each knot on an existing vertex of its own level or inserts one by splitThrough at its own level; splitThrough, attraction, crossings, promotion and warp never change a profile (a split adds a vertex without a knot; a knot vertex moves with its chain).

kerb, bandUnion and every export sample the profile (§3.4, §3.7) and the digest hashes its values with the knot rows, so a T-junction S8 inserts into a spine cannot shift the width elsewhere along it.

Cutting a profiled chain (J-K23): a conversion handing part of a chain to another entity or opening a ring (way split, partial wallToWay, carve's cut) goes through retypeEdges with rekey (§3.4), which first gives each part a cut knot at every cut vertex: a knot row of that part's entity carrying the profile's sample there — linear: the arc-length interpolation kept as that exact double (the one kind of knot value that is not an authored value; computed with + - * / and Math.sqrt only, identical on every engine); step: the held value. A cut at a knot vertex copies that knot to the other part; a part wholly before the first or after the last knot takes the constant as a scalar.
Cut-knot bar: every part samples what it sampled before to within one interpolation's rounding (<= 6.8e-13 cm over 20,000 random ways, docs/validation/bench/fixall_kernel_r3_checks.out B).

Removing a stretch of a profiled chain first gives each remaining part a cut knot at the stretch's end on its side (same rule) before the stretch's rows and interior knot rows leave, so every remaining sample is unchanged (fixall_kernel_r4_checks.out C).

A join of two chains into one entity concatenates their knots in chain order and drops a knot at the join vertex only where the joined profile samples identically without it — value equals the interpolation between neighbouring knots within 1e-9 cm, decided in doubles (linear), or equals the previous knot's value (step); the two cut knots of an undone split carry one value and drop, restoring the original profile bit for bit (20,000 of 20,000, r3 file); two different values at the join stay on the one vertex as two ordinals, a step, as §3.6 step 1's merged knots are.

A log event addressing a vertex by position (moveVertex, §7.1) stores its LatticePoint and the vertex's VertexSig at edit time; the edit layer refuses a target with an empty signature (every editable vertex carries a structural or vertex role, §7.1's table).

On replay resolveVertexAt(key, at, sig) (§3.4) maps the signature's entity ids through carry-over (§6.3) and binds in order: (1) the vertex at `at` if its signature contains every recorded row; (2) else the nearest vertex whose signature does, within the rebind radius — attractCm for a vertex without vertex roles, else the §6.3 anchor radius of its vertex-role kind (junction and pin 1 m, gate and tower 2 m) — ties by lattice position (y, then x).
items.note: Anchor radii (junction and pin 1 m, gate and tower 2 m) restated from §6.3.

items.statement: resolveVertexAt step (3): else the event is orphaned and reported (§7.3 item 4). A vertex is never bound by distance alone, so an upgrade replay never moves an unrelated nearby vertex. A river's control knot is no arena vertex: moveCourseKnot binds by the knot's ordinal (§7.4).

Rule 6: refinement is a pure function L(n+1) = refine_n(level-n view, params, streams), streams keyed from the scope's lineage (§6.1). How an edit clears and re-derives finer content is §7.3 (2); what survives the clear (locked or pinned entities returned as conflicts to the dry run, and kept content treated as fixed obstacles) is §3.3's.

Rule 7: roles, not a single type. Each edge pair and vertex carries a small sorted set of (role, entity, level, ordinal) rows from the role registry (a versioned data table); an output reading a set in order (a digest §6.2, a contact name's entity) reads by the role's rank in the registry then the entity's address id, never by an interned handle (session-order dependent).

Edge roles: way, kerb, corridor_split, band, wall, wall_gate, shore, bank, border, margin, field_bound, district_bound, plot_line, party_wall, frontage, access, yard_part, claim, reserved (a reservation's boundary before growth, §4.2 S3), setback (L1 line bounding a wall strip, §4.8), deck, green_line (hedgerows on L3 field boundaries; avenue and street-tree rows are Greenery.along records, not edges, §2.7), treatment (a plot edge's fence, hedge, wall or railing as an attribute row), gate_opening (sub-edge of a treated plot edge left open for a gate, indexed per gate), tunnel, gallery (centreline of an underground system's gallery or an undercity walkway, own part; item 65), chamber_wall (chamber's closed outline chain; item 65), invisible.

Vertex roles: junction, tower, gate, entrance (one row per entrance of a building's entrance set, ('entrance', building id, i), §2.6, item 29), portal, attach, anchor, weld, deck_end, gate_end, composition (a stored stage-3 composition's boundary points, §2.6), access_point (an AccessPoint's vertex on its underground element — tunnel or gallery kerb, chamber wall, sewer dwelling's side or rear wall, II.7.4 — distinct from the access edge role), link_end (('link_end', link id, 0|1): an UndergroundLink's end, one vertex per part in both parts, §2.7; item 65), and one knot role per profiled attribute (width_knot, base_knot, invert_knot, bank_knot, shore_class_knot).
Indexed roles (rows carry an ordinal): entrance, attach, anchor, weld, deck_end, gate_end, composition, link_end, gate_opening and the knot roles.

Structural edge roles: way, wall, wall_gate, shore, bank, border, margin, reserved, setback, deck, tunnel, gallery, chamber_wall; all other edge roles are partition roles. A structural role is never removed by a sliver absorption or a face merge (§3.6); §5.3's crossing invariant finds deck edges by their role.
A vertex carrying any role row of a live entity is never dissolved.
Coincident features are one edge with several roles (street on a district boundary, quay on a shore, wall on a river bank, track on a field boundary), never two edges and never an overwrite.

A way's class, width profile and surface are attributes of the Way entity, not of its edges (FTG's 14 wire types generalised); a wall chain may be open, its ends anchored on typed vertices (shore, cliff, castle; Enceinte.anchors, §2.7).

The deck: a Bridge's deck span is the way's own L1 edge between the bridge's two deck_end bank vertices, carrying `deck` beside `way` (ChainRef('deck', bridgeId)); a site no way uses keeps its two bank vertices and no span (Bridge.state = 'site', §2.7). Which batch places a deck's bank vertices, at which level, before or after its water, is §4.2 S1 (5)'s; no L0 edge crosses water and no deck splits a water body's L0 faces (LC-7, J-I12).

Anchors, contact names and gate ends (J-K29): an anchor row marks the end of an open chain resting on a coarser feature (an open wall's two ends, ('anchor', enceinteId, 0|1)) or serves as a contact name — a bank point a coarse insertion's preparation batch places on a finer edge that is neither a kept way nor a re-traced wall run (a settlement-perimeter or other district-boundary stretch, a wall strip's setback or glacis line, the map's border; §3.3 rule 2), for the water's batch to name in KernelTx.prepared.

A contact name's entity is that of the first row of the edge's own birth level in the row order: on a district boundary the first district in id order among its district_bound rows; on the settlement perimeter the first in id order of the inner district and the hinterland pseudo-district; on a setback or glacis line its setback row's enceinte; on the map border the arena's Terrain entity. Its kernel-allocated ordinal and life until the promotion that strips it are §3.3 rules 2-3's; no record references it.

A water gate's two bank vertices carry ('gate_end', gateId, 0|1) — on a re-traced run from the preparation batch on, under a fresh Gate address as a re-sited deck's bank vertices are under a fresh Bridge (§6.3, §7.3 (b) 3) — and persist because Gate.banks names them (§2.7); the wall's edge between them lies across the water as a deck span does. Where generated and edited water gates' bank vertices stand is §4.4 S5a's; both are held under a warp unless fromLevel = 0, as a deck's bank vertices are (§3.6; J-K35).
Rule 8: every committed batch validates its declared invariants at their scopes, writes a report record and a CommitRecord; a failed batch leaves the arena at the previous version (§3.3, §3.10).

Arena size at CITY: ≈ 80 k vertices, ≈ 240 k half-edges, role rows (2-byte ordinal) and five face tables (1-byte stage rank) ≈ 10 MB typed arrays, plus ≈ 2 MB for the two lookup tables at load <= 0.5 (≈ 1.5 MB role heads for ≈ 60,000 role keys at 12 B a slot; ≈ 0.5 MB owner heads over five levels at 8 B a slot) — ≈ 12 MB (PLAUSIBLE until M0), against ≈ 20-29 MB for five per-level DCELs (SCL-11).

Spatial index adds 38.4 B per item (packed partition: double-precision box and 32-bit index per node, one inner node per 16 below; fixall_kernel_r4_bench.out A) over one item per vertex, route edge and face: ≈ 190,000-230,000 items, ≈ 7-8.5 MB at a finished CITY (PLAUSIBLE until M1); indexHome 2 B per vertex, edge-pair and face slot adds ≈ 0.5 MB; the generation worker's arena with index ≈ 19.5-21 MB. A pool worker's frozen copy and its size are §3.3 pool step 1's.
Knot rows are few: a constant-width way has none; a wall's base profile has one knot per trace vertex (tens to a few hundred per enceinte).

Rebuilding lookup tables as Maps would cost each pool worker ≈ 10 ms (60,000 keys) to ≈ 20 ms (100,000 keys) at CITY and ≈ 62 ms at METROPOLIS before its first query (fixall_kernel_r3_bench.out B); typed tables travel inside the frozen copy, one memory copy costing ≈ 1.1 ms at 12 MB, ≈ 1.5 ms at 15 MB, ≈ 2 ms at 20 MB (fixall_kernel_r4_bench.out A).

Terrain { id; key (the ground, or one sky island's own terrain); cellCm, cols, rows, originX, originY (the height raster over frame + margin, §3.2 (9)); datumCm; heightCm: Int32Array above datum; reliefLimitCm = 1,000,000 (10 km, the declared range every write is checked against); hydro: HydroGrid; flowDir (Uint8 on hydro: D8, defined on every land cell of frame and margin, flats included); flatRank (Uint32 on hydro: flat-resolution order, 0 off flats); flowAccum (Uint32 on hydro); outfalls: Outfall[]; seaLevelCm (datum frame); wind {bearingCdeg, strength}; features: SiteFeature[] (hill, spur, valley, terrace, cliff, ravine); geology }.
datumCm: the elevation that height 0 represents, relative to mean sea level; one per document (per island for sky terrain); set by S1 (§4.2).

geology ∈ {'ordinary','soluble','volcanic'} (item 65): the site's rock under the frame, written by S1 (§4.2) with the resources or overridden by setAttr (§7.1 terrain row), read only by II.7.6's cavern rule (soluble or volcanic rock holds caverns); 'ordinary' on a sky island's terrain.
HydroGrid { cellCm: TOWN 1,600, CITY 2,500, METROPOLIS 3,200 (table values at creation, kept through frame growth, §3.2 (9)); cols; rows; originX; originY — same extent as the height raster }.
TerrainSampler { heightAt(p): Cm — bilinear on the height raster, the 2.5 m refinement computed on demand, never stored; slopeAt(p); flowAt(p): {dir, accum} — the hydro cell containing p }.
read_by: slope queries in the built extent

items.statement: WaterBody { id; kind; face: FaceRef (L0); shore: ChainRef ('shore', id) its ring(s); course? (rivers: the reach's centreline downstream, kept in step with the shores); controls? {ordinal, at: PointCm}[] (rivers: S1's control knots in course order, §4.2 S1 (3) — recorded inputs, not arena vertices); nextControl?; widthProfile?: CmArray; depthCm?: Int16Array (per course vertex — the course is the entity's own derived polyline no kernel op re-vertexes); flowFrom?; flowTo?; bankKinds?: ChainProfile<beach|rock|cliff|quay|marsh> (step, on the shore chain, G-R5); shoreClass?: ChainProfile<bay|headland|straight> (step); lifecycle }.
WaterBody.kind ∈ {sea, lake, river, tributary, distributary, islet_channel, pond, moat, estuary, harbour_basin, canal, ditch}; ditch = a drainage cut that drains reclaimed ground (item 25; §4.11).

A river control knot the user moved is the edited path 'controls/<ordinal>', implicitly pinned (§7.1 moveCourseKnot, §7.4); nextControl is the next free knot ordinal: a re-trace or re-sampling gives new knots fresh ordinals, so an ordinal never names two knots.

Terrain is a raster in metres with resolution set at creation by size class (TOWN 5 m, CITY 8 m, METROPOLIS 10 m — so VG's 128² fixed grid is never the constraint) over the frame and its context margin; cols x rows follow the arena's width x height (§3.2 (9)).

The resolution is kept when an epoch grows the frame: every raster of §2.3 extends by whole cells on its own grid keeping its cellCm (§3.2 (9); J-A81.31); a re-grid at the new rung's cell is only that rule's pre-decided fallback.
Point queries go through a TerrainSampler (bilinear), which is how slope queries inside the built extent and S11's ground datum read a 2.5 m refinement without storing one.

The hydrology grid (J-K12): flow direction, flat rank and accumulation live on their own raster `hydro` over the same extent (frame and margin) at 16 m (TOWN), 25 m (CITY), 32 m (METROPOLIS): 200², 320², 400² cells at the rungs' target populations, the counts §12.4's S1 budget assumes (1.6 x the cell of a frame-only raster with the same counts, 10/16/20 m). A hydro cell's height is the height raster's bilinear sample at the cell centre rounded to the centimetre, so the flood runs on integers.

Hydrology timings (bucket-queue flood, two-gradient flats, D8, accumulation; fixall_kernel_r2_hydro.out): CITY 15.9-17.2 ms, METROPOLIS 25.3-26.5 ms, TOWN 6.2-7.0 ms, every cell with defined D8 on both 60 m and 3,000 m relief (frame-only raster of the same counts 15.3-16.4 and 25.6-26.8 ms; frame and margin at frame-only cells 41-44 and 67-69 ms).

flowAt(p) returns the hydro cell containing p, so a hinterland plot's upstream (§2.5), a water mill's reach and the sewer hook read defined flow everywhere on the map; O1 (b)'s "every terrain cell has a defined flow path to an outfall" holds on this grid over frame and margin (§13.1).
How S1 traces and carves the river course on this grid and keeps stored flow in step with carved terrain is §4.2 S1 (3)'s; the grid's pre-decided coarsening is §12.4's M0 site-and-fields fallback.
Heights are Int32 centimetres relative to the per-document datum datumCm (§4.2 S1), so stored values stay small and a 3,000 m relief is ordinary.

Every write to a height or depth raster (S1, terrain brush, site primitive) goes through a range check against its declared limit that clamps and reports (W_HEIGHT_CLAMPED with the cell count in the generation report) and never wraps (an Int16Array stores 40,000 as -25,536, executed in GEO-15). The mountainous round-trip fixture is §13.1's.

Flats (GEO-15): sinks are filled by §4.2 S1 (3)'s priority flood, keeping exact flat surfaces; flow across every flat (filled depressions and genuinely level ground) is resolved by the two-gradient flat-resolution method (a BFS gradient away from higher terrain and one towards lower terrain, combined into flatRank) in its own array, so stored heights are untouched, D8 is defined on every land cell and each flat drains to its spill point.
D8 ties break in the fixed neighbour order E, NE, N, NW, W, SW, S, SE, so flow is identical on every engine.

where: §2.3 Terrain is not in the plat
items.statement: Terrain is not in the plat: water faces and their shore and bank edges enter L0 from S1 (§4.2); contour lines are not model geometry — extracted per render tile and per export and clipped to the land faces (§4.2 S1 (2), §8, §11).

where: §2.3 Terrain is not in the plat
items.statement: Drainage lines are raster queries, not plat edges (as L0 edges they would be antennae every L1-L4 line would have to end on or avoid, §3.6); a line that must be visible as water is a tributary water body with its own L0 face (§2.2 rule 1; GEO-1, GEO-6).

where: §2.3 Terrain is not in the plat
items.statement: Drainage (flow direction, flat rank, accumulation, outfalls) is queryable per hydro cell — the sewer hook's query surface.

where: §2.3 Terrain is not in the plat
items.statement: A sky island's terrain is its own Terrain with its own key, datum, frame and hydro grid (§4.2, II.1).
items.note: The II.1 citation resolves (II.1's input carries layer sky with optional own terrain); the island hooks proper are II.6.

items.statement: A shore's bank kind and shore class are step ChainProfiles on the water body's shore chain (§2.2 rule 5): a knot where the class changes, so a street end, bridgehead or quay inserted later never shifts which stretch is beach and which quay.

The river course and its width and depth arrays are S1's centreline of the reach, recomputed by S1's water operator whenever a batch moves or re-vertexes the reach's shores; moveCourseKnot is the one edit that changes the course directly (both §7.3 (b) 1), so a warp never leaves the course behind.

Slow change of terrain and water (item 25; kinds, rarity rows and rates §4.11's, local repair §7.3 (b)'s): terrain and water are the slowest layer, not an immutable one. siltReach on a reach or basin: widthProfile and depthCm fall by the row's share and S1's water operator re-buffers shores from the unchanged course (a basin below the harbour's draught loses its harbour role, §4.11).

reclaim of a marsh or foreshore: the water face's L0 ring retreats (a moved shore, §7.3 (b)) or the marsh LandUse face is re-typed; the new ground is an L3 land-use face marked `reclaimed` (§2.7) drained to the nearest outfall by a ditch water body cut like a canal (§4.11 carve).

shiftCourse: the reach is re-traced between two control knots with fresh ordinals (nextControl), the old shores' vertices demoted as §2.2 rule 3 states and the old bed left as a marsh land-use trace. digCanal is §4.11's carve of kind canal.
Each slow-change conversion is a lifecycle event on the water body or land-use face with cause convert:<kind> (§2.8), undone from the chain's replaced scope (§7.4).
A building's basement decision (§2.6, item 29) reads ContextVector.terrainClass (§2.5) and the nearest water surface's elevation and the hydro grid's accumulation.
Emulation note: neither reference has time; MFCG's warp and FTG's water drawing already let a user reshape water, kept as edits (§7.1); the design adds only slow change over epochs (item 23).
WayClass ∈ {through, primary, secondary, lane, alley, cul_de_sac, track, path, quay, pier, bridge, ford}.

Way { id; class; spine: ChainRef ('way', id) the L1 chain resolved by the kernel; width: Cm | ChainProfile<Cm> (width_knot on the spine; constant-width stores a scalar); surface ∈ {paved, cobble, dirt, planks}; name?: NameRef; from, to: NodeRef (gate, plaza, bridge, harbour, junction, external bearing); growthStage; epoch; provisional; bridge?; slopeP95?; flowToward?; corridor?: FaceRef (L2 view); lifecycle }.
An external bearing names the trade partner it leads to by the partner's key (§7.7's TradePartner, item 77); the settlement's derived TradeFlow weighs it (§4.3).
provisional: an S5-grown spine beyond a stage boundary: the only ways the inter-stage trim may cut (§4.4).
Way.flowToward ∈ {'from','to'}: sewer hook — drainage direction along the way; slopeP95? recorded.
Junction { id; vertex: VertexRef ('junction', id); arms: Id[]; kind ∈ {T, X, Y, end, gate, bridgehead, square}; wedges?: FaceRef (L2 view) }.
items.note: Junction has no lifecycle field listed, although §2.4 says every record embeds Identity and Lifecycle (§2.8); see conflicts.

items.statement: Every record of §2.4-§2.7 and PART II reaches geometry only through FaceRef, ChainRef, EdgeSetRef or VertexRef, never an arena slot, and holds a vertex position only where §2.2 rule 5 allows.
Every record embeds the Identity and Lifecycle of §2.8 (the id and lifecycle fields); no record stores a seed or a stream key: streams derive from the entity's lineage on demand (§6.1).

No passage way class (item 30): a passage through a building is an L3 face of kind passage under the front building's wing (§2.5 Passage, cut by S10 on §4.6's reach; J-A30.31 — no nesting exception, no new operation), reached as an access face and drawn with an arch glyph (§8.3); WayClass unchanged; the underground carries tunnel and gallery chains (undercity walkways among them), never ways (§2.2 rule 1).

District { id; kind; quarter (label-level grouping, §9.1); faces: FaceRef (L1 coarse faces, before and after infill); boundary: TypedBoundary; seams: Id[] (its Seam records, II.1, one per boundary run, shared with the neighbour; the SeamContract is the view assembled from them — from milestone 1); character; venueMix; prosperity {mean, band}; growthStage; identity?; bandRange; pressure; nameHistory?; parent?; outskirts?; fabric; fabricParams; buildingScale; materialOverride?; allocation; subDistricts; description?; namingFeature?; name?; lifecycle } — labels are LabelEntity (§9.1).

DistrictKind is feature-named and data-defined, never a social class: central, market (one per market of either rank, item 24), docks, gate, riverbank, castle, temple, park, craft, sprawl, suburb, shanty, hinterland, underground (the owner-staged layer's pseudo-district, II.7.3), undercity (one neighbourhood of the undercity in its void's part, II.7.5; item 65), ...
District.seams: its Seam records (II.1), one per boundary run, shared with the neighbour across it; the district's SeamContract is the view assembled from them, from milestone 1.

District.character: CharacterVector (item 72 (a)) — what the district has become; written by S12c and each epoch's character step (§4.5 (2)); derived: recomputed on load, outside the model digest (§6.2).

District.identity? { row (the §10.2 row it took: quarter-identity row, a family's or sector's dominant row, or a plain row by band); source ∈ {dossier, emergent, dominant, plain}; sinceWeek (§4.11's week) } — item 72 (d′) quarter identity (§4.5 (4)); model data in the digest; written by S12c, by an epoch's character step past its hysteresis and by a dossier kind (district-defining institution, matched naming claim, §7.7); a setAttr overrides an identity the dossier did not set (§2.8 fact tiers).

District.bandRange: [floor, ceiling] band ids (FieldBands.bands) of what any building in it may be — derived by S10a from its prosperity value through §10.2's bandRanges rows (§4.5 (5)), recomputed on load, outside the model digest.
District.pressure: the leaky sum of the excess the dials would push past the range (§4.5 (8)); model data in the digest, written only by epochs; 0 with none.
District.nameHistory?: NameRef[] — the names a rename replaced, oldest first; §6.3's epoch rename and a dossier rename keep the old name here (§10.4).

District.parent? (item 65): an undercity neighbourhood's surface district, the one it shadows (II.7.5); District.outskirts? (item 65): an undercity neighbourhood's sewer-front blocks in part 0 (II.7.3) — a link across parts, never a second key (J-A65.31).
District.fabric: FabricStrategyId — 'bent-cut' in the base; ring / square / street at stage 2; fabricParams: Record<string, number>.
District.buildingScale: 0.5-2, default 1 — FTG's "smaller / bigger" knob as a continuous multiplier on footprint targets (§4.7 S11).

District.materialOverride?: Partial<MaterialRow> (§2.6); allocation: Id (the district's Allocation record, §4.5 S7b); subDistricts: Id[]; description?: TextRef (a generated one-line summary of the mix and features, §10.4, regenerated when the mix changes, editable); namingFeature?; name?: NameRef.

CharacterVector (item 72 (a); J-A72.41 — the one meaning of "character"; the per-district input is §7.7's DistrictIntent): a district's derived five-component profile computed by S12c and each epoch's character step (§4.5 (2)), draw-free, every share significance-weighted (§4.5 (1)): (1) mix — each class family's share of what was placed (§10.2 families), sum 1; (2) powers — each power's share (PowerStanding key, §7.7) by partition weights (§4.5 (7)); (3) trade 0-1 — trade-weighted frontage over the busiest district's (§4.3 TradeFlow), tradeBearingCdeg? — weighted mean bearing of gates whose routes cross it; (4) sectors — weighted presence per sector over the settlement-wide total (§10.2 sectors); (5) mainRoad — share of frontage on through and primary ways, and anchors {institution, weight}[] — significant institutions near it and its contributions.
Character = the district's derived CharacterVector (the one meaning, J-A72.41); distinct from the per-district input DistrictIntent (§7.7) and from the ContextVector.
Quarters are §9.1's QuarterNode merge tree, built by S6 (§4.5); its city cut is the city-LOD label unit (§9.4).
SubDistrict { id; district; blocks: Id[]; cluster (roster cluster tag, e.g. a trade group) } — FTG's sub-district: a contiguous block group a cluster is placed into (§4.7 S10a).

Reservation { id; kind ∈ {castle, plaza, market, precinct, institution, park, harbour_basin, moat, canal}; rank?; face: FaceRef (L1 barrier face(s); water kinds L0 faces); areaBandM2 [min, max]; compactnessMin?; owner? (castle, institution, commons); attach: VertexRef[] (('attach', id, i): perimeter vertices arterials end at (plaza) or the wall welds through (castle on the enceinte)); stage: StageId (S3, S7 gate plazas, or S7b); lifecycle }.

Reservation.rank? ∈ {principal, secondary}, market kinds only (item 24): the principal market (the plaza when it wins S3 (12)'s trade score, else a flanking site) or one of S7b's secondary markets (§4.2, §4.5); setAttr-editable.

Allocation { id; level ∈ {town, district, block}; target (town, district, block, hinterland pseudo-district, sky pseudo-district (II.6), underground pseudo-district (II.7.3) or undercity neighbourhood (II.7.5)); rows [{cls; band; count; claim? (Reservation for items larger than a block); subDistrict?; near? (hinterland rows only: the district an edge orchard serves, §4.9); areaM2? (area-sized rows: edge orchards, sky capacity)}]; lifecycle } — persisted; the eager content decision every lazy or per-district stage honours (§4.1 laziness contract); stores no stream key (§2.4).

FieldBands { field ∈ {prosperity, density, greenery}; cuts: ascending on the field's [0,1] value; hysteresis default 0.02; bands: the band set's ids in order, cuts.length + 1 of them, from §4.5's prosperity.bands table (item 27) — every band-keyed row key is one of them; middle: the settlement's middle band (holding its median household under the roster's wealth shares, designated at S6 with the cuts, §4.5; J-A27.42) — the band §4.11's geometry floor bounds a plot's manifested geometry to (item 31) and the row §2.6's interior ladder reads as its middle (item 28 (f)); source ∈ {roster-shares, table, edit}; epoch } — computed once per town at S6, changed only by an explicit edit or an epoch (§4.5).
Block { id; face: FaceRef (L2 built block(s)); district; subDistrict?; frontages: Frontage[]; depthClass; interior; reach; due?; reservation? }.

Block.interior ∈ {plots, court, back_lane, through_alley, rear_plots, green, landmark, reserved, wall_strip, empty}: the deep-interior treatment decided in S8 (§4.6); wall_strip = an enceinte's band, setback and glacis block, never plotted (§4.8).

Block.reach ∈ {open, passage, gated} (item 30): how a court or rear-row interior is reached from the public way, drawn with the treatment in S8 (§4.6); 'open' for every other interior and in the parity presets.

Block.due? {band; since (epoch of the crossing); epochs (spent in that band since)} (item 31): the block's value crossed a cut past the hysteresis at an epoch and its stock has not yet met the new band; written and cleared by §4.11's wealth ladder, never by a brush.
Frontage { id; way; edges: EdgeSetRef ('frontage', frontage id) — the L2 kerb edges of this block on this way; class: WayClass; lengthCm }.
items.note: The 'frontage' role is keyed both by frontage id (Frontage.edges) and by plot id (Plot.frontage); see conflicts (ambiguity).

items.statement: Plot { id; face: FaceRef (L3); block; district; frontage: EdgeSetRef ('frontage', plot id); access: EdgeSetRef ('access', plot id); depthCm; frontageCm; exposure; knownTo; tenure; partyWalls; bounds; owner?; use: PlotUse; sitePlan; buildings: Id[] (0..n footprints); yard: YardPart[]; builtBand; builtProsperity; fieldBand; ctx: ContextVector; derivedFrom: DerivationRecord (§2.8); assignment?: AssignmentRef; members? (joined plots — EVO; item 31's fusion, §7.1); lifecycle }.
Plot.access: ('access', plot id), >= 1 edge always (§5.2 F-PLOT); an access edge lying on a sealed Passage face is a sealed access edge.

Plot.exposure ∈ {street, lane, alley, court, hidden, sealed} (item 30): derived at §4.6 from the block's interior access graph when S10 types the access edges (by adjacency and reach depth, never a sight line, J-A30.42); hidden = every reach to a public kerb passes a passage, a gated opening or two or more interior faces; sealed = every reach passes a sealed passage.

Plot.knownTo ∈ {public, local, secret} (item 30): defaults from exposure (hidden -> local, sealed -> secret — item 30 (e)'s lost place, J-A30.24 — else public), otherwise a dossier fact (§7.7) or a setAttr; read by §9.2's label policy and the reader (§11.2), never by geometry.

Plot.tenure ∈ {owned, rented, common, informal} (item 70 (a)): who holds the ground — derived by §4.7's rule (Informal clusters (1)), written with the plot by S10b and S11 and re-derived by every event that changes its inputs; a setAttr overrides it, kept as an edited path (§7.2); a persisted attribute column, in the leaf digest (§6.2) and the snapshot.

Plot.partyWalls: EdgeSetRef ('party_wall', plot id), one shared edge per wall, the neighbour being the owner of the face across; Plot.bounds: PlotBound[] — the boundary treatment of every non-party-wall edge (VIS-8).
Plot.owner? (household | business | institution); use: PlotUse; sitePlan: SitePlan; buildings: 0..n footprint ids; yard: typed YardParts.

Plot.builtBand and builtProsperity (item 31): the band and field value on [0,1] the plot's present stock was built for — persisted attribute columns, in schema order in the leaf digest (§6.2) and the snapshot (§2.9), never recomputed from the field (J-DET-12); written by generation and the paths J-A31.44 lists (§4.11) and by no bare setAttr (§7.1); geometryFloor is derived from it at read.

Plot.fieldBand (item 28 (f)): the occupants' band — the plot's prosperity band by §4.5's rule with its hysteresis read against this column, so the band's memory moves with the band (J-A28.29); set by every derivation that reads the current field (= its ctx.prosperityBand, banded against this column; by the cuts alone at the plot's first derivation; a field brush's re-derivation past τ among them, §7.2); Regenerate (keep settings) reading recorded inputs keeps it as it keeps builtBand; re-banded after S6 at every epoch (§4.11); persisted attribute column in the leaf digest and snapshot; derived — no setAttr (§7.1); read by §2.6's interior ladder, ClassRules.pick and the plan rung's recorded inputs (§2.8).
Plot.ctx: ContextVector; derivedFrom: DerivationRecord (§2.8); assignment?: AssignmentRef; members?: joined plots (EVO; item 31's fusion, §7.1).

PlotBound { id; edges: EdgeSetRef ('treatment', bound id) the treated sub-edges — a gate opening is the sub-edge carrying the indexed gate_opening role instead of treatment (splitThrough at the gate ends); side ∈ {frontage, side, rear}; treatment ∈ {none, fence, hedge, wall, railing}; heightCm; gates [{opening: EdgeSetRef ('gate_opening', bound id, i); widthCm}] — every access edge with a treatment has >= 1; ownedBy (one owner per shared edge) }.

YardPart { id; kind (data-defined — named by designation templates' yard rows §10.2 DesignationTemplateRow.yard: yard, garden, court, orchard, midden, pen, vacant, formal_garden, forecourt, churchyard, shore, footpath (item 70: a cluster plot's internal path narrower than an alley onto which every structure's door opens, §4.7 S11), ...); face: FaceRef (L4 yard sub-area bounded by yard_part edges, made by S11's yard partition, §4.7 S11, §4.9); lifecycle } — the lineage unit of its address is the plot (§6.3).
DerivationRecord (what S10-S12b read last time; Regenerate (keep) re-reads it, §4.5, §4.11) is defined once, in §2.8.

SitePlan { arrangement ∈ {row, compound, detached, hovel, tents, institution, cluster (item 70: informal structures packed along footpaths, each with its own door, §4.7 S11), none} — tents stays FTG's row for the parity presets; coverage; slots: BuildingSlot[]; frontJitterCm (the drawn front-line recession h, §4.7 S11, item 43: 0 or in [jitter.minM, jitter.maxM]); ruleRow }.

Passage { id; face: FaceRef (the L3 face of kind passage: a covered alley-as-face cut along one side line of the front plot from the kerb to the court or rear row it serves, §4.6, §4.7 S10 (9); J-A30.31); block; frontPlot; frontBuilding? (the building whose wing spans it — written by S11 with BaseWing.spans, cleared as §2.6's BaseWing.spans states); widthCm; headroomCm; sealed; lifecycle } — in the entity registry (§2.8).

Passage.headroomCm: the clear height (the ground storey it takes, storeys above keeping the frontage continuous) — derived, written by S11 whenever it writes the spanning wings' BaseWing.spans (every re-fit) and re-derived in every other event changing a spanning wing's heights (setAttr of heights §7.1 or its undo §7.4), which holds the passage in its effective scope (§7.3 item 1), as the least ground-storey height (eaveCm / floors, rounded down to the cm) over the base wings that span it; kept as it stands and read by no reader while none spans (front building made a footprint trace or tombstone), until S11 writes it with a successor's spans.

S11 gives every spanning wing at least two floors (raising its class row's floors to two where they would be one), so each spanning wing's eave stands above the headroom (§8.5 (2), §8.4, §11.1); a heights edit that would leave a spanning wing below two floors is refused (F-EDIT, §5.2).
Passage.sealed (item 30 (e)): a bricked arch — sealPassage / openPassage (§4.11, §7.1), no geometry change; the one stored bit behind "a sealed access edge" and a plot's exposure 'sealed' (§4.6).
BuildingSlot { role (house, hall, stables, workshop, chapel, barn, kitchen, brewhouse, tent, ...); entranceOn; frontage?; unhoused? } — persisted, no polygon.

BuildingSlot.entranceOn: EdgeSetRef ('access', plot id) — the access edges the slot's main entrance faces; it stands on the footprint side facing them (§2.6 entrance rule 1): the frontage for a front slot, the court or the path from the plot's street gate for a set-back one (item 29); a hidden plot's door faces its passage or court, a cluster structure's the footpath reaching these edges (items 30, 70); side, rear and yard doors read the plot's other access edges and yard parts.
BuildingSlot.frontage? ∈ {none, lean_to, stall, shopfront, arcade, gate, wall}: the designation template's frontage treatment for the main slot (§4.7 S11, item 19), persisted with the slot.

BuildingSlot.unhoused?: true (item 28 (f)) — only on a residential slot of a workplace's or institution's plot (its main slot or one within a required structure's least count) for which §4.7's generation fill found no household of its band or drift, which S11 built as a slot without houses; every reader of a slot's houses (§4.7 S11, §2.6 capacity, §13.2 T19-4) reads it as without; written by every run of that fill; cleared by the designation mutator (§4.7), whose undo restores it with the former parts.

SlotPlan extends BuildingSlot { hint: Polygon — S11's working shape, transient, never stored; a later outline() or compose() call gets the building's current footprint ring resolved from its FaceRef at the call (§2.6) }.

ContextVector — the per-plot vector every rule table reads (owner hook; O7/O17/O18/O19): areaM2; shape {obbW: M, obbD: M, compactness, reflex, corner, wedge}; frontageM; roadClass: WayClass; roadWidthM; districtKind; quarter; venueMix (the district's mix, read through the district, never copied per plot, SCL-5); prosperity, prosperityBand, density, greenery (continuous values plus banded class, O18, as sampled at the plot's derivation); dist {centre, plaza, market (nearest market of either rank, item 24), gate, wall, water, shore, harbour?} in M; upstream (0 upstream .. 1 downstream along drainage); slope; aspect: Cdeg; upwind; baseCm; terrainClass; growthStage; epoch; buildingScale; arena; rosterAssignment?; assignment?.
read_by: every rule table (§10.2 ClassRules, designation templates, granularity table)

items.statement: Context vector: the one per-plot record (ContextVector, Plot.ctx) of the plot model, prosperity field, granularity and greenery that every rule table reads; distinct from the district's CharacterVector and from §7.7's DistrictIntent.
ContextVector's field values are as sampled at the plot's derivation; after it a building's interior reads the current sample and the plot's fieldBand — §2.6's occupants' band (J-A28.29).
ContextVector.terrainClass ∈ {high, mid, low, damp, flood, rock}.

ContextVector.arena ∈ {ground, underground} (item 12): keys the arena-specific rows of the granularity table and of the designation templates' arrangement (II.7.3); every underground part reads 'underground', a system's own rows being its rule's (II.7.5, II.7.6).
items.note: Sky arena not an option of ContextVector.arena although sky pseudo-districts receive allocations (II.6); see conflicts.

items.statement: The context vector is stored as struct-of-arrays columns per district partition (one typed column per field), not as an object per plot (SCL-5).

A plot is the parcel (the owner's stage-3 wording and the references' code say lot for the same thing; the document says plot except when quoting); building means only a footprint with heights standing on a plot.
Rendering never draws a plot outline as a building (a cadastral outline group is an optional toggle).
A plot's coverage, arrangement, separation and boundary treatment come from S11's designation templates (§4.7).

A slot's shape is S11's working data, never a stored polygon: after S11 the building's footprint face and its wings (§2.6) are the slot's geometry, so no plot record holds a world position a warp would leave behind (§2.2 rule 5; J-P50).

Districts are feature-named, never class-named (J-P1, refined by item 72): kind names feature or function (the typing stages read, §4.5); identity is what it has become (religious, craftsmen's, merchants' quarter, or a plain residential identity by band), naming and describing it (§10.4) without zoning by class; an identity row may re-type the kind at an epoch (§4.5 (9)). "Rich quarter"/"poor quarter" stay descriptions derived from the prosperity field for naming and the description line only; wealth varies continuously through the prosperity field (MFP-7).

CharacterVector is derived and recomputed on load, never an input (the input is §7.7's DistrictIntent); identity and pressure are model data that generation and the epochs write; bandRange is a derived bound S10a writes from the district's prosperity value; nameHistory keeps replaced names. The significance weights, partition, identity rows, three dials and pressure's law are §4.5's, stated once there.

Reservations are the large claims made before the streets (§4.2 S3) or before the lanes (§4.5 S7b): castle bailey, main plaza, market, church or cathedral precinct, large institutions, parks, and the water kinds (harbour basin, moat, canal) carved into L0 before any way is routed; a reservation is a barrier to growth and infill; the claimed entity is built inside it.

Allocations are the persisted content decision: which classes and how many, in which wealth band, go to each district, sub-district and block — and for outside classes and edge orchards to the hinterland pseudo-district, and with the owner-staged island toggle on to the sky pseudo-districts (II.6); computed eagerly for the whole town (§4.1), read by every per-district stage, so content never depends on the order districts are derived or viewed (LC-2).
An allocation stores no stream key — S7b and S10a draw from lineage-derived streams (§6.1) — so a district's New random re-draws its own block allocation and nothing else.

DerivationRecord is a plot's, block's or building's memory of its derivation inputs (§2.8). Regenerate (keep settings) re-derives from recorded inputs (faithful, byte-identical); re-deriving with current inputs is Adjust; a field brush compares each plot's current sample with the recorded one and re-derives only what §7.2's τ rule selects (τ = 0.01 of the field range, same τ on replay; LC-6) — an authorial re-derivation that sets builtBand in its scope (J-A31.44).
An epoch never re-derives plots by τ: it acts on survivors only through §4.11's wealth ladder, at due blocks, bounded by the geometry floor (item 31; LC-12).

PlotBound gives every plot edge a treatment (none, fence, hedge, wall, railing) with gate openings on access edges, chosen by the designation template (§4.7 S11); it draws a walled manor compound, a fenced garden, a hedged field edge and exports as VTT walls and GeoJSON lines (VIS-8; NG 1.2.2 draws none; FTG's fences, COV-FTG-F23).

A plot in transition (item 67 (g)) keeps the rings its event gave it; a boundary line the event removed is drawn from its Works' kept lines until the clearing stage, and a new one as stakes first (Works.before, §2.7; §4.11's Works).

geometryFloor is derived at read, never stored, from builtBand and FieldBands.middle by §4.11's floor rule, so a changed middle designation needs no migration; that rule, the manifested band a plot's geometry reads and what writes builtBand are stated once in §4.11 (J-A31.43, J-A31.44); a block's due mark is that ladder's trigger; with no epoch the manifested band is the field band everywhere (item 23).

Exposure names how a plot is reached (derived at §4.6 by S10 from the block's interior access graph and reach); a Passage is the covered way under a front building that a passage reach cuts; its sealed bit is the one stored fact behind a sealed access edge and exposure sealed (its plots then enter §4.11's ladder as vacant, §2.8); knownTo is knowledge, not geometry — the place is always on the map, only its name and purpose withheld (§9.2, §11.2).

A hidden plot keeps the access guarantee: >= 1 access edge and a chain of access faces to a public kerb (§5.2 F-PLOT, §5.3); an informal cluster (item 70) carries it down to each structure: every structure's main entrance opens on a footpath yard part that reaches an access edge of its plot (§4.7 S11 Informal clusters).

Tenure values: owned; rented (let out beyond what its buildings were built for); common (ground no one owns — commons, greens); informal (no single owner — squatted or customary); derived by §4.7's rule and editable by setAttr; the cluster arrangement and §4.11's decline and formalisation paths read it.
Seams (II.1), FieldBands (§4.5) and vacant frontage runs — ordinary plots with use = 'vacant' or a yard part joined to the neighbour (§4.7 S10 (8); COV-VG-VN-170) — are stated at their homes.

Heights { baseCm (ground datum: floor level in terrain cm); floors; floorsBelow? (derived, never set on its own: on Building.heights the basement's Basement.floors, item 29; 0 or absent without one; absent from every other entity's heights); eaveCm; ridgeCm; towerCm? (eave, ridge, tower above baseCm) } — owner HEIGHT ruling: always populated.

BaseWing { kind ∈ {rect, quad, polygon}; ring: Polygon (world lattice points, counter-clockwise — a derived shape record the wing-carrying rule keeps on the footprint); corners?; ridgeAxis; spans?; heights; roof: RoofSpec }.

BaseWing.kind: rect = a rectangle, its four corners and on its sides the footprint's and the building's other wings' vertices lying there; quad = a row footprint clipped to its plot (§4.7 S11), four sides in ring order from corners[0], sides 1 and 3 the party-wall chains (straight, or with the lot cut's one bend, §4.7 S10 (4)), sides 2 and 4 the front and rear chains which may be bent or curved — or a rect the carry turned into a quad (rule 3); polygon = a template part (apse, octagon, star point).

BaseWing.corners? [0, i, j, k] (rect and quad): ring indices at which sides 1-4 begin (ring starts at the first corner); recorded by S11 when it clips a row or when a rect's sides carry other vertices, re-indexed by every carry; absent on a rect whose ring is its four corners ([0,1,2,3]).

BaseWing.ridgeAxis 0|1: rect — along side 1 (0) or side 2 (1); quad — 0 = the ridge joins the arc-length midpoints of sides 1 and 3 (party-wall chains, eaves to the street), 1 = joins midpoints of sides 2 and 4 (front and rear chains, gable to the street); polygon — unused (pyramid, cone or dome).

BaseWing.spans?: FaceRef (item 30) — the Passage face this wing spans, on each base wing whose ring runs along the passage's edge (a stepped front building's quads each); written only by S11 with Passage.frontBuilding, cleared by S11 when it builds or re-fits the passage's front building or the passage goes (§4.6, §4.7 S10 (9); drawPassage, a block's reach changed to or from passage (J-A30.72), densify ... back_court's new passage and the rung-3 re-cut removing a sealed passage with its rear row (amalgamate) reach it through that re-fit, §7.1, §4.11; sealPassage, openPassage and thin ... back_court's sealing change no geometry and leave it); absent on every other wing.

BaseWing.spans is also cleared, with Passage.frontBuilding, inside the event that makes the front building a footprint trace (§2.8 cleared: robStone or clear, which zero its heights) or a tombstone (demolish); each such event holds the passage in its effective scope (§7.3 item 1) and its undo restores what it cleared (§7.4); the passage is then open above — face, sealed bit and plots' access unchanged, no span mark, span caster or arch glyph drawn — until S11 raises a successor over it (reuse ... build, build). Its span ring and extent above ground are as Wing.spans, so the capacity, the building's leaf digest and §8.5's span mark read them before any composition exists, and a composition inherits them.

Building { id; plot; slot; footprint: FaceRef (L4); wings: BaseWing[]; class; use?; formerUses; concealed?; dwelling?; households; entrances; nextEntrance; basement?; heights; roof; material; condition; knownTo; predecessor?; reusedAs?; works?; description?; openingHours?; subLocations; composition?; assignment?; drift?; lifecycle } — no occupants list (J-A28.29): the housed are households (with a workplace's live-in dwelling); those who work there are §10's Posting records.

Building.wings >= 1; the footprint is their union exactly, kept so through every move by the wing-carrying rule (rectangle 1, L 2, T 2-3, templates n; a clipped row house 1 quad, or stepped quads on a slope).

BuildingClass (data-defined): hovel, cottage, house, row_house, hall, inn, workshop, warehouse, chapel, church, temple, manor, keep, tower, mill, tent, shack, lean_to_shelter (item 70's cluster structures, named apart from the lean_to frontage treatment), ...

Building.use?: the current Use record (§2.7): the roster class it houses, its specialisation and assignment; absent = vacant (item 17). formerUses: Use records that occupied it before, newest last — the traces item 17 (c) keeps (a former inn, a guildhall turned tenement).

Building.concealed?: Id[] (item 63): the concealed Use records it houses behind its front (use), each with Use.concealment not 'none' and Use.front naming use; their knowledge is theirs (§2.7; §4.7 Concealed institutions); absent = none.

Building.dwelling?: the household living in a workplace (live-in), §4.7 S10b — one of its households; cleared by every event taking that household out of the building (its relocation §10.3: a use's move, a relet, §4.7's overflow pass, the capacity re-homing; or its leaving at an epoch, epoch step (c) §4.11) and by one that leaves the building no live-in use (the household staying as an ordinary one of households — §10.3's use that moves without it; a liveIn table edit, §7.6).

Building.households: the Household records housed (§2.7), the reverse of Household.building, kept by the writer that sets it — generation fill (S10b's placement, written by S11 once wings exist, clamped into [1, capacity] for a residential building and empty for every other, §4.7), §4.11's relet, item 17's relocation (§10.3); its length is the count the plan rung houses and the interior ladder reads (item 28 (f)), never above the capacity.

Building.entrances: Entrance[] >= 1 (item 29): exactly one of role main, on the footprint side facing the plot's frontage access edge (its street, the court or path from the plot's street gate, a hidden plot's passage or court, a cluster structure's footpath — Entrances rule 1) plus the side, rear, yard and service doors the entrance rules allow; replaces the single entrance vertex.

Building.nextEntrance: the next free entrance ordinal (the i of Entrance.vertex), written only by deriveEntrances and setEntrance, never decreasing, so a removed entrance's ordinal is never re-used (as WaterBody.nextControl).
Building.basement?: Basement — the selective basement decision (item 29 (b)); absent = none.
Building.heights = the building's max over its wings; Building.roof: RoofSpec — the model's default roof construction; a style sheet may override the construction, never the heights (§8.2).

Building.material {walls, roof}: from MaterialRow, setAttr-overridable, a rendering attribute only; condition ∈ {kept, worn, neglected} (item 31 rung 1): the fabric's wear — a rendering-class driver like material (§8.2: wear, patched roofs), never a shape input and not an existence state (§2.8); stepped down by §4.11's ladder, restored by renovation.

Building.knownTo ∈ {public, local, secret} (item 30): defaults from its plot's exposure and knownTo; a dossier fact for a dossier-backed institution's buildings (§7.7); read by §9.2 and the reader, never by geometry.

Building.predecessor? (item 8): the cleared trace or ruin this building was raised on (§4.11 reuse ... build; the trace's address passes by succession, §6.3); reusedAs? ∈ {garden, orchard, field} (item 8): what a reused trace became (existence reused, §2.8) — the trace keeps its L4 face and is drawn as that kind (§8.2); written only by §4.11's reuse conversion or its convert by hand (§7.1); absent on every other building (J-A8.22).
Building.works? (item 67): the Works (§2.7) running on it; its stage at a week is derived by §4.11, never stored; cleared when the Works finishes, is cancelled or is retired.
Building.description?: TextRef; openingHours?: OpeningRow[]; subLocations: SubLocation ids from the class table.

Building.composition? (stage 3): lazily generated rung by rung (the elaboration record and cache, §2.8, §2.9), stored only when edited — the first composition or plan edit stores it (§7.1); its streams derive from the building's lineage with each rung's own reroll (§6.1).

RoofSpec { kind ∈ {gable, hip, flat, pyramid, cone, dome, skeleton, tent, plain (the F-SKELETON downgrade: no ridge or hip lines, §3.8), none (the roofless state the decline ladder's decay sets — derelict, kept through ruin, §2.8 decline hooks)}; pitch? (a ratio, not an angle); material? }.

MaterialRow { key {era; stage? (FTG per-stage default: the growth stage of the building's plot); districtKind?; cls? — overrides, most specific winning: class (temples and churches stone by row), then district kind, then the stage default; band? — only in the optional regional-shift rows, absent from every default row, so the default never keys a material by wealth (item 19)}; walls; roof; weight; extension? 'regionalShift' (§7.6's marker: a row of our optional regional shift, off by default, items 19, 23) } — a rule table (§7.6), our own rows.

OpeningRow { dayType; openH; closeH }; SubLocation { id; building; name; tags (table, counter, stage, bed, bath, pickup, deliver, ... data-defined); capacities {leisure, tempResidential, guestWorker, studying, working}; relax? } — from the class table; rooms at stage 3 refine, never replace.
