Composition { lod: subset of the four rungs of the building ladder outline -> wings -> rooms -> plan (item 28); wings: Wing[]; towers: ComposedTower[]; courts: Polygon[]; rooms?: Room[] (the rooms rung: principal rooms a Fantasy-Manor-class composer emits with its wings — a hall, a tower's round room — each with its storey; the plan rung takes them as fixed rings, each less a stair bay or chimney stack it holds; optional, absent from the base's outline builder); plan?: Plan }.

Wing { footprint: Polygon (the wing's ground ring); heights; roof; dormers? (a free count while the plan rung is absent; once a plan exists derived from the plan's roofed rooms with exterior demand); porch? (at the main entrance's side and offset, item 29, so porch and plan front door coincide by construction; re-read after every carry, rule 3); spans? }.

Wing.spans?: FaceRef (item 30): a composed wing whose ground ring follows the edge of a passage a base wing spans takes that BaseWing.spans — every such composed wing and no other — so a composition inherits the span and never decides it. Its span ring (the part of the face under the wing: the face's ring cut by lines continuing across it the end segments of the two wing-ring sides meeting the passage's edge — a row quad's front and rear chains — a boolean on the arrangement, §3.7, or the whole ring where the wing covers it all) is derived at read, never stored. The wing's ground ring ends at the passage's edge; every storey above extends over the span ring (extent at level >= 1 = ring ∪ span ring); at the ground storey the plan rung adds the span ring as a seed ring passed as a fixed ring — the passage room (role passage, scope circulation), never cut, its two end walls carrying the passage openings (J-A30.23); read on the base wing by the capacity, §8.5's span mark (§8.4's span caster) and the 3-D export (§11.1), and on the base or composed wing by the plan rung.

ComposedTower { centre: Point; radiusCm; heights; roof } — a composition's tower; for the plan rung a round wing: one round room per storey and the spiral stair core of the wing it joins; the wall tower entity is §2.7's Tower.

items.owner: model (plan-rung interface; built by V03; V03 §2 extends)
items.statement: Room { id (room:<building id>/<level>/<i> — an address carried by its anchor, the room's centroid within its wing, §6.3); ring: Polygon (world lattice points inside its wing's extent at its storey — spans on base or composed wing; the passage room is a span ring — a value read back from the rung's transient arena, never a plat face, §3.4; J-A28.31); wing (index into Composition.wings; a tower's round room names its ComposedTower by wings.length + tower index; the passage room names the wing spanning it); storey (Storey.level); role: RoomRole; scope ∈ {unit, shared, service, circulation} (§10.2 RoomRuleRow.scope); unit? (item 28 (f): the Household whose dwelling unit it belongs to — present exactly when scope is unit; edited by setRoomUnit §7.1); program? (index into Plan.program; absent for a generic room); subLocation? (rooms refine sub-locations, never replace); hearth? {wall, at, chimney}; lit (a light at the room's spine summit, §8.5, §11.1; J-A28.32; corridors unlit); concealed? (item 63: a room of a concealed use's programme, plan rung steps 2 and 5, entered only by a service, yard or concealed door; drawn and read only for a viewer whose knowledge admits the concealed use, §9.2) }.

items.owner: model (plan-rung interface; V03 extends with heads)
items.statement: Plan { storeys: Storey[]; program: ProgramRoom[] (the programme as sized and allocated, plan rung steps 2-3: what the plan owed — read by the report, §13.2's bars and the re-cut); units [{household; form: UnitForm; entry (the Opening that is the unit's own door, onto circulation or the street)}] (item 28 (f): one per household housed); cores: StairCore[]; chimneys: Chimney[]; pattern: per storey level LayoutPattern; slices: SliceRef[] (programme, pattern, furniture and interior-ladder rows consulted, §2.8) }.

Storey { level (-k..-1 basement storeys, 0 ground, 1..n above); wings (the wings whose floors — or the basement ring — reach this level); rooms; walls; openings; windows }. ProgramRoom { rule (index into the programme row's rooms, §10.2 RoomRuleRow); role; scope; unit?; areaM2 [min, target, max] = the row's values x the interior ladder row's size factor interpolated along the occupants' value; storey; wing; concealed? (item 63: §10.2 RoomRuleRow.concealed); anchor? ({entrance: ordinal — its entrance room, one per entrance, step 3} | 'core' | 'hearth' | 'passage' — the span ring, step 1) }.

Wall { id; a, b: PointCm; kind ∈ {exterior, party, partition, court}; left, right: Id | 'outside' } — exterior and court walls lie on the edges of the storey's extents (wing rings, and a span ring: the passage room's walls, J-A30.23), a party wall on the plot's party-wall edge (stage-3 contract's fourth rung). Opening { id; wall; at (from a); widthCm; kind ∈ {door, arch, open, entrance, passage, trapdoor}; entrance? (the entrance's ordinal, the stable i of Entrance.vertex, item 29: every entrance opens here; the passage room's two arch openings are of kind passage and name no entrance, item 30, J-A30.23) }. WindowRec { id; wall; at; widthCm }.

StairCore { id; wing; tower? (index into Composition.towers: a spiral in a round wing); bay: Polygon (the same bay on every storey it serves); levels [from, to]; kind ∈ {straight, dogleg, winder, spiral, ladder, trapdoor} }. Chimney { id; wing; column: PointCm; levels } — derived from a hearth column (a small fixed ring on the transient arena, §3.4); the roof construction draws it (§8.6).

RoomRole = string, data-defined by §10.2's room-programme rows (our names: hall, chamber, solar, parlour, kitchen, buttery, common room, cooking place, staff chamber, stair hall, forge, shop, store, undercroft, nave, passage ...). LayoutPattern ∈ {bisect, follow, spine, hall_and_parlour, cross_passage, enfilade, nave} — the cut patterns, rows not code. UnitForm ∈ {house, dwelling, lodging, apartment, room} (item 28 (f): the interior ladder's unit forms, richest first).

InteriorLadderRow (item 28 (f)) — one row of the interiorLadder table of roomProgram.json (§7.6, §14), defaults in the table below: band (a FieldBands.bands id, one row per band of the set, §4.5); form: UnitForm (one household's unit); households [lo, hi | 'capacity'] (range a shell of this row houses, clamped into [1, capacity]: bounds relet and the canonical chain's row steps, never the as-built count); unitRooms (scope unit); shared (scope shared, where the class's programme row allows); staff {count {n; law 'const'|'perPrincipalChambers'}; sizeShare (of the owners' principal chamber's target); placement (attic|basement|service, preferred first)} | null; circulation {roles (stair hall, corridor); patterns (preferred first)}; sizeFactor (x the programme rows' room areas).

Entrance { vertex: VertexRef ('entrance', building id, i) — a vertex on the footprint edge, indexed (§2.2 rule 7); i a stable ordinal kept by a re-derived entrance §6.3 re-matches, Building.nextEntrance for a new one, never re-used after removal — named by Opening.entrance and ProgramRoom.anchor; role ∈ {main, side, rear, yard, service}; faces ∈ {street, lane, alley, yard, court, passage (item 30 passage face), footpath (item 70 cluster path)}; concealed? (item 63: a concealed use's own door — service or yard entrance where rule 2's access edge presents itself, never the main one; its knowledge the concealed use's) ... }.
Entrance.wing; side (the wing ring's side, as Porch.side); offsetCm (along that side); side and offset re-read from the vertex after every carry (rule 3). The rules are "Entrances" below.

Basement { floors (storeys below ground, >= 1 — the one stored count Heights.floorsBelow reads; 0 for a crawl space, which is no storey); kind ∈ {full, half, walkout, crawl} (crawl: item 66's requested form — a void under a raised ground storey reached by a hatch); ring: Polygon (inside the ground storey's wings and smaller than their union; world lattice points carried with the wings by rule 2 (b)'s mean-value coordinates, CarriedShapes.basement; rule 4 checks it); access ∈ {core, trapdoor, external} (how the plan rung joins it — the stair core, where no bay of the core fits inside the ring a trapdoor core the plan reports (step 3), a trapdoor, or an outside stair; step 3's reported trapdoor core where no side of Basement.ring is long enough for its door; derived with the basement, a shell fact) }.
items.note: Basement.floors ">= 1" versus "0 for a crawl space": the field's range statement contradicts itself within one comment; see conflicts.

items.statement: Porch { side (the side of its wing's footprint ring it stands on, by ring index); offsetCm (from that side's first vertex along it); widthCm; depthCm (outward) } — relative to its wing, no world point, so it moves with the wing; side and offset are the main entrance's, re-read after every carry (rule 3).

BuildingInput { lot: Polygon; access: Segment[]; slot: SlotPlan (at S11 the site plan's working hint; at a later outline()/compose() the building's current footprint ring resolved at the call); ctx: ContextVector; cls; assignment?; drift: DriftBounds; seed: StreamKey (derived from the building's lineage for this call, never stored); terrain: TerrainSampler; fixedWings? (the row arrangement's clipped quads, §4.7 S11: outline() returns them with heights and roofs, never re-fits them); building? (Pick of households, entrances, basement, subLocations, use, assignment, concealed — the plan rung's content inputs, item 28, resolved at the call); accesses? (item 64: the AccessPoints that open in its basement, II.7.3's Basement accesses declared in II.7.4 — anchors of the plan, step 3); stage?: WorksStage (item 67: its running Works' stage at the drawn week, §4.11, which the plan's drawing shows) }.

items.owner: model (stage-3 hook; implementers: base OutlineBuildingGenerator, V02, V03)
items.statement: BuildingGenerator — the stage-3 hook split by cost (SCL-13): outline(input, k): KernelResult<{wings}> (every LOD, exports, shadows: cheap and deterministic); compose(input, outline, lod 'wings'|'rooms', k): KernelResult<Composition> (lazy, per visible tile); plan(input, composition, k, prior?): KernelResult<Plan> (the fourth rung, item 28: lazy under §4.1's contract, on the click's request, on a transient arena per storey, §3.4; prior = the canonical prior a re-cut mutates, never the cache).

ClassRules.pick(ctx, bands {field {band, value} — the occupants' band (plot's fieldBand) and current field value: specialisation and room programme; manifested {band, value} — from Plot.builtBand and FieldBands.middle by §4.11's floor rule: the geometry columns}, assignment?) -> {cls; specialisation?; heights (without baseCm); roof; template?} — a data table, not code: the class row and its designation template (§4.7 S11, item 19); geometry columns read at the manifested band, specialisation and room programme at the field band (J-A19.43, J-A28.29).

Replaceability and class change (item 31): how soon a band change may replace a building's stock is its designation template row's replaceability at the plot's builtBand (§10.2), read by §4.11's ladder; a class change at rung 2 (mansion to tenement, inn, workshop or chapel) is item 18's mutation and keeps the shell (§4.7 S11).

The wing-carrying rule is pure, + - * / and sqrt only (§6.5). CarriedShapes { wings; basement? (item 29 (b): carried by rule 2 (b), checked by rule 4); composition? (only when stored — an edited stage-3 composition: wing, court and room rings and tower centres, and with a stored plan every storey's room rings, walls' end points, stair-core bays and chimney columns; rule 2 (b); J-P48) }. carryWings(shapes, before rings (outer first), after rings, moved(p) -> new position or null (dissolved) of a footprint vertex — with spanned, of a span ring's vertex too, pairing? 'tiled'|'overlapping' (rule 4's verdict found once per edit from vertex identities and reused by every halving of one step; computed when absent), spanned? (item 30: per span ring, the rings of footprint face ∪ span ring before and after — where a stored point inside the span ring takes its mean-value coordinates, J-P48 (2))) -> KernelResult<CarriedShapes>; E_INVARIANT when rule 4's check fails.

The base ships OutlineBuildingGenerator: the site plan's rectangle; an L or T of 2-3 rectangular wings (MFCG Complex mode, FTG Dense/Gaps looks); a row's fixedWings passed through unchanged; and for institution classes (keep, temple, church, manor, hall, farmstead) two further constructions behind the same outline(): footprint templates and the axis-locked composer.

Footprint templates (COV-FTG-F16): data rows of normalised shapes fitted to the claim — cruciform church (nave, transept, apse), cruciform keep with corner projections, octagon, n-gon (a 9-gon theatre), 6- and 7-pointed star temples, U-court, ring cloister around a court; fitting = an affine map into the claim's lir then a boolean intersection with the claim; each template stored as constituent rectangles and wedges so the wing rule holds.

Axis-locked composer (COV-MFCG-G05, our own construction): take the claim's OBB axes; cut the axis-aligned rectangle on the axis more perpendicular to the current longest edge at a ratio from U(0.4, 0.6); recurse until cells reach the class's minimum cell (minCell = baseCell * 2^(2*size - 1), a table row); keep each cell with the class's fill probability, keeping the cell nearest the main entrance and rejecting any drop that disconnects the kept set; retry <= 3 times on the .../attempt=n stream, then the full rectangle (reported). U, H, comb, cross and ring footprints emerge.

Every footprint is stored as wings (VIS-10; J-P17) of the three BaseWing kinds — rect for the outline builder's rectangles and its L/T compositions, quad for a row house, polygon for a template part with a pyramid/cone/dome roof; each wing carries its ridge axis (the wing's long axis, or the short axis in a table share of wings — NG measures ≈ 36 %), its heights and roof; the footprint is the wings' union, so the footprint hash at city LOD does not depend on the wing split.

The roof construction the renderer draws (plain, skeleton-hip, skeleton-gable, fake gable per wing) is a style-sheet parameter over the stored wings (§8.2); the model's roof.kind is the default the 3-D export uses, so presets change the picture without changing the model.

Row footprints are quads (J-P31, J-P39): S11's row arrangement builds each row house's footprint by the boolean plot ∩ frontage band (§4.7 S11, GEO-26), so two neighbours share one party-wall edge even on a bent or curved frontage; stored as one quad wing — side chains = the plot's party walls (straight, or bent once where the lot cut's bend falls inside the row depth, §4.7 S10 (4)), front and rear = the clipped chains; S11 records the four corners and hands it to outline() as fixedWings; outline() adds heights and roof, never re-fits it.
On a slope beyond skirtMaxCm S11 first splits a row quad along the contour into stepped quads, each a wing with its own corners.

The quad's model ridge joins the arc-length midpoints of the two chains its ridgeAxis names, so every row house has a ridge without a skeleton, and a bent party-wall chain has one well-defined midpoint (on whichever of its two segments half its length falls); the drawn roof is chosen wing by wing by §3.8 (exact OBB roof for a wing passing its convex near-rectangle test, else the validated skeleton with its plain-roof downgrade); the per-wing fake-gable construction draws the stored ridge directly; no reader asserts a party-wall side is straight.
The union rule, O17 (i)'s identical footprint hash at every LOD and the stage-3 contract hold for attached rows on curved frontages exactly as for rectangles (the curved-street fixtures of §13.2).

Wings follow their footprint — the wing-carrying rule (J-P42): wing rings store world lattice points, some footprint vertex positions (with a stored stage-3 composition and plan, the only entity records that do, §2.2 rule 5; a basement ring's points, all inside the footprint, carried with them), so one pure function carryWings keeps every building's wings on its footprint face through every change of its rings: a warp or moveVertex moving a vertex of the face (the commit record's moved list, §3.3); a batch adding a vertex to one of its rings (a neighbouring plot re-fitted with a corner on a shared party wall; II.1 (3)'s neighbour step splitting a kerb a row footprint fronts; S12b's formal-garden grid line or orchard-part edge ending on a house wall, §4.9) or taking one out (a dissolution or that step's reversal); and S11's own insertion of the footprint, the first carry.

When carryWings runs is stage-agnostic (J-P47): after every committed batch (generation or edit; derivation pool, hinterland unit or generation worker) whose commit record lists a footprint face among the L4 faces it changed, a vertex of one among the vertices it moved, or — for a building whose stored composition has a wing spanning a passage — that passage's face among the L3 faces it changed or one of its vertices among those moved (§3.3), the batch's writer runs carryWings for that building before its next batch (a passage and its front building lie in one block, §2.5; an edit changing the passage face takes the building into its effective scope, as J-P48 (1)'s split faces are, §7.3 item 1); the building's own S11 batch ends with the first carry; a warp or moveVertex runs it inside the step's whole-step validation (rule 4; §3.6, §7.4).

The carry writes only the building's wings (and its basement ring and stored composition), which belong to the writer's own faces — a district's S12b changes only its own footprints (§4.1 laziness contract), an edit only those of its effective scope and seam exception (§7.3 item 1) — so generation, a pool of any size, a replay and Regenerate (keep settings) run the same carries on the same rings and store the same bytes (O9 (c)).

Rule 1 boundary runs are footprint runs: the parts of a wing's ring on the footprint's boundary (boundary runs) are runs of the footprint's rings vertex for vertex, so a wing vertex on the boundary is a footprint vertex identified by its lattice point (§3.10). S11 establishes this at the first carry: it inserts the footprint's rings through every wing vertex on the wings' union boundary (a collinear one included, as a shape vertex that never dissolves, §2.2 rule 3), then carries the wings from the inserted ring to the committed face, each input vertex matched to the vertex its insertion placed (ChainInsert.placed, §3.4; a row's quad already is its committed ring). Inside the footprint, a vertex one wing has on another wing's side (an L's joint, a T's stem corner on its bar) is a vertex of both rings (a rect records it between its corners); every later carry keeps both properties.

Rule 2 carry: (a) each boundary run is re-read from the rings after the change between its two end vertices, in the direction keeping the footprint's interior on its left, matched by identity (an end keeps its vertex wherever it stands), so an added boundary vertex joins every wing ring running along it, a dissolved one leaves it, a moved one moves; a wing wholly on the boundary (one-wing house, row quad) is re-read whole from its first corner's vertex; (b) every other wing vertex (a joint inside the footprint, the hidden corner of an overlapping wing) takes its mean-value coordinates w.r.t. the footprint's rings (outer and holes) before the change, applied to the rings after with + - * / and sqrt only (§6.5), rounded to the lattice, so a shared joint maps to one point for both. Basement ring points (CarriedShapes.basement, item 29 (b)) are carried the same way in the same call (J-A29.23).

Rule 3 kinds: a rect's and quad's corners name the same corner vertices after the carry and are re-indexed; a rect whose carried ring fails §3.8's convex near-rectangle test becomes a quad with its four corners recorded and ridgeAxis swapped (rect axis 0 along side 1 = quad axis 1, the line joining midpoints of sides 2 and 4), keeping the ridge direction, the roof path re-chosen on the carried ring (§3.8, §8.6); quad and polygon keep their kinds. After every carry each entrance's side and offsetCm are re-read from its vertex (the side of its wing's ring the vertex lies on and its arc length from that side's first vertex), and a stored composition's porch takes the main entrance's, re-read on its composed wing's ring, so stored numbers never disagree with the door (§6.3's re-match reads them; J-A29.23).

Rule 4 check (J-P49): every carried ring is simple and counter-clockwise, and the union of the building's wings equals its footprint face (integer equality after snapping — the stage-3 contract), decided exactly at least cost by the building's pairing: whether every directed edge of its wing rings, keyed by vertex identity, is an edge of the footprint's rings (each used once) or the reverse of exactly one other wing's edge. The pairing depends on identities only, so is found once per edit and holds through every halving of a step; a batch adding or removing a vertex recomputes it.

Rule 4 cases: (i) a building whose every wing is re-read whole by rule 2 (a) (one-wing house, row quad) needs no union — its ring is the footprint's, kept simple by the step's validation (§3.6); only rule 3's test runs, on a rect; (ii) pairing holds (tiled wings: L, T, cross, U of abutting rects, a template of tiles) — needs only every carried ring simple and counter-clockwise (winding numbers sum to the face's); (iii) pairing fails (overlapping wings, e.g. a T whose stem runs into its bar) — checked by the kernel's boolean union on the arrangement (§3.7) against the face.

For a warp or moveVertex the check is part of the step's whole-step validation, which halves the step when it fails (§3.6; the edit layer's record check, as for a held pin, §7.4); it runs after the kernel's own checks pass and stops at the first failing building in address order. After any other batch a building whose check fails is re-derived by S11 on its plot (F-REDERIVE, reported); by rule 1 that cannot happen on the boundary, and a joint moves only by the sub-centimetre route changes such a batch makes (§2.2 rule 3).

The basement ring is checked in the same pass (simple, counter-clockwise, inside the footprint face, exact orient2d tests): an unedited basement whose carried ring fails is re-derived by the basement decision inside the step with no halving; an edited one fails the step's validation as a held pin does (§7.4), and after any other batch its edit is orphaned (§7.3 item 4) as a stored composition's is (J-P48), the basement being re-derived until the user re-attaches or discards the edit (J-A29.23).

carryWings cost per building per validation pass (carry and rule 3 included; Node 24; fixall_pipeline_r5_wingcost.mjs -> .out): ≈ 0.06 µs row quad; ≈ 0.4 µs one-wing rect; ≈ 0.9-2.7 µs tiled L, T, cross, U and inner-joint compositions (check 0.15-0.4 µs of it); ≈ 0.3-0.9 µs once per edit for the pairing; an overlapping composition adds its union, bounded by S11's compound geometry share (<= 25 µs, §12.4 S11 row; PLAUSIBLE). Core mix 55 % row quads, 25 % one-wing, 18 % tiled, 2 % overlapping — 450 buildings (§12.6's district ceiling; ≈ a 150 m brush, ≈ 7 ha, in a dense CITY core) cost ≈ 0.4 ms per pass and ≈ 3.6 ms worst case of a step and eight halvings, inside §12.6's warp Apply budget which counts it; M3a's measurement on that brush and its pre-decided fallback are §12.6's.

Rule 5 undo, replay, moveFootprint: the edit's undo record keeps the former rings (§7.4); a replay performs the same carry on the same geometry and gets the same rings; moveFootprint applies its rigid move to the wing rings and S11 re-fits the plot with them as fixedWings (the first-carry path).

A stored composition is carried with its wings (J-P48): a stage-3 Composition is derived lazily and stores no position until an edit stores it (Building.composition; the edit kinds that do so are stage 3's and the plan events of §7.1; a hand-built one is stored by §2.6's test); from then on its world geometry (each composed Wing.footprint, court, room ring — rooms rung's and, with a stored plan, every storey's — Wall end points, StairCore.bay, Chimney.column, ComposedTower centre) is carried in the same carryWings call as the base wings by the same rules; a porch takes the main entrance's side and offset after every carry (rule 3).

A designation mutation (item 18) re-matches a stored composition's and plan's rings to the target template by role inside its event (§4.7 S11) and re-cuts a stored plan by the re-cut rule (the interior ladder).

J-P48 (1): the edit that stores a composition establishes rule 1 in the same batch: every ring point, wall end, bay, column and tower centre on the footprint face's boundary becomes a vertex of the footprint rings (on an L4 edge by a same-level L4 split; on a plot line (L3) or kerb (L2) by an L4 Steiner vertex placed by splitThrough, the point re-read at the placed vertex) and carries a ('composition', buildingId, i) vertex role row while stored, so no dissolution removes it; the row leaves with the composition on undo or orphaning. Base wings gain each vertex by rule 2 (a); a point one composed ring has on another's side is made a vertex of both (a data step). Every face sharing a split edge (own yard parts, a row neighbour's footprint across a party wall, a neighbouring plot's L4 face) gains the vertex and is in the storing edit's effective scope with a row neighbour's wing rings; each ring equals its prior ring with those vertices removed (§3.3 same-level-split rule; §7.3 item 7 (ii) check).

J-P48 (2): boundary runs re-read by identity; every other point takes mean-value coordinates in the footprint's rings before the change — a stored room's point in a spanned passage's span ring (the plan's passage room's or a room above it) in the rings of footprint face ∪ span ring (carryWings' spanned; J-A30.23) — applied after and rounded, so a point shared by a wing, a court and a room maps to one point; a boundary tower centre moves with its footprint vertex; each composed wing and tower is then re-based by deriveBase on the ground it now stands on, as base wings are (§7.4).

J-P48 (3) a composed Wing has no kind to lose — its roof construction is re-chosen on the carried ring (§8.6); (4) the check adds every carried composition ring simple and counter-clockwise, composed wings uniting to the footprint face (by rule 4's tiers), every room ring inside the union of the face and the span rings of the passages the building spans (J-A30.23), a stored plan's rooms tiling each storey's extent (the contract's fourth rung, by §3.10's seed-tiling test) and every tower centre inside or on the face (exact orient2d); (5) the undo record keeps the former composition with the former wing rings (§7.4).

A composition carry failure inside a warp or moveVertex halves the step as for the wings; after any other batch the stored composition is orphaned (§7.3 item 4): the dry run lists it, the edit that stored it stays in the log and the document's orphan table, the record is dropped and the building composes lazily from its carried wings until the user re-attaches or discards the edit — never silently.

Wherever the document names a building's wing rings as carried, re-based, excepted from locality or restored (§2.2 rule 5, §4.6 step 7, §5.3, §7.3 (a) 4 and items 1 and 7 (ii), §7.4, II.1 (3), II.4), a stored composition's rings, wings and tower centres and a stored plan's points are included by this rule, and the basement ring by rule 2 (b).

§2.6's test is the B-EDIT fixture exercising the wing-carrying rule (warps and vertex moves over L, overlapping T, curved-row and holed footprints and a hand-built stored composition; generation equal to regeneration on a compound whose garden edges end on the house wall), stated in §13.2 (and §7.3 item 7 (vi)); receipts for the carry under 0.25-8 m displacement fields: fixall_pipeline_r4_wings.py -> .out; cost and pairing's agreement with the full edge test: fixall_pipeline_r5_wingcost.mjs -> .out.

where: §2.6 heights and ground datum (owner HEIGHT ruling
items.statement: Every building, wing, tower, keep, wall run, gate and bridge carries heights; eave, ridge and tower heights are measured above baseCm, the floor level in terrain centimetres.

One per-entity function deriveBase(entity, sampler) computes every ground datum; S11, S7, S1's terrain operator (§7.3 (a)) and the edit layer after a warp or vertex move (§7.4) all call it: a wing's baseCm from the terrain sampler (bilinear on the refined 2.5 m raster at the wing's vertices and centroid) = max(samples) + plinthCm (table, default 30 cm) — over a requested crawl space also half the class's cellar depth (Basements) — so no floor is buried.
The fall under a wing (max - min) is a foundation skirt the 3-D export extrudes down to the terrain and the shadow pass includes.

Where the fall across a row footprint would exceed skirtMaxCm (table, default 300 cm) the footprint is split along the contour into stepped wings, each within the limit — terraces step down a hill instead of floating.

Walls store their base as a knot profile along the trace (§2.2 rule 5); gates and towers their own base from samples under their footprints; bridges and pier decks a deck height from the two bank elevations plus a clearance row. Shadows and the 3-D export (§11.1) read the same numbers, so they agree on any terrain.

The lighting model and its shadows (cast by the sun and placed lights over the height field, defaults and budgets) are §8.4's (item 68; §12); the base populates every height and keeps the display list's shadow hook (§8.1).

A building under Works (item 67) keeps its finished heights in the record; its heights at a week are derived by §4.11's heightsAt (walls rising storey by storey, no roof before ROOF FRAMED); a framed roof (rafters without covering) is a drawn state, never a RoofSpec.kind. The heights acceptance bar is §13.2's.

A material is a rendering attribute only (owner, 2026-09-26: materials only change texture or colour, nothing to do with shape): it changes the texture and colour roles the style sheet maps it to (§8.2), never a footprint, wing, storey, height or roof form; shape is decided by the designation template and prosperity alone (§4.7 S11).

MaterialRow is a rule table read by S11 whose default rows reproduce FTG's model (item 23): one default material per growth stage (key.stage), overridden per district kind and per building class (temples and churches stone by row); wealth shown through the lifestyle-banded building pools (§10.2) and the roof-colour role by band in the style sheet (§8.2), never by a material keyed to the prosperity band.

The optional regional shift — rows marked extension: 'regionalShift', off by default, a preset row (D-2) — may shift materials with the prosperity band within what the region builds with, never as a universal ladder.

A district's materialOverride and a building's setAttr override the material rows; enceintes carry their own wall material (§2.7). Wear (Building.condition, item 31) is a rendering class over the same geometry (§8.2); a roof is lost only in the decline ladder's derelict state (decay, RoofSpec.kind 'none', §2.8).
Test: a material change leaves the geometry subtree of the digest unchanged (§13.2).

A building's description is generated by the naming engine (§10.4) from its class, use, owner and district, persisted per entity and editable; opening hours come from the class table and are what the simulation module reads; SubLocation records (named parts with tags and capacities for leisure, temporary residence, guest workers, study and work) are filled from the class table when the building is created; stage-3 rooms refine them (a Room may host a sub-location) and never replace their ids.

The stage-3 hook and its cost contract (owner-staged; DEF-17, SCL-13): stage 3 replaces OutlineBuildingGenerator with a lot-driven Fantasy-Manor-class generator (manor.md §3.3, §9 via the proposals: a lot-derived path of wings, orientation fixed by the frontage, the lot polygon in the collision set, a class picker per plot from the same ClassRules table).

Fantasy Manor's model (build 890, v1.0.0) needs no input but a path of wings and their breadth; its five layout families — closed rings of four, five, six or eight equal sides; stars of four to six points; open arcs of two to seven equal segments; rectangles; self-avoiding paths on a four-by-four grid — become stage 3's path-shape rows (PathShapeRow; provenance ref:Fantasy Manor build 890 layout families (code), P21); a hip block stays distinct from a square tower's pyramid (RoofSpec hip != pyramid).

Ours adds what Fantasy Manor lacks (J-A59.21): wings join the collision set so no tower or block stands through a wing; porch options restricted so every building's main door faces its street (Entrances — that model guarantees none: about 14 % of its buildings have no entrance, D4); the scale is metric.

PathShapeRow (item 59): stage 3's path-shape rows — the path of wings a lot-driven composer lays inside the plot; a data table (§7.6) read at the class's designation row; our rows, families from Fantasy Manor build 890 (P21): family ∈ {ring, star, arc, rect, snake}; sides? (ring side counts; star point counts); chords? [least, most] (arc segments); gridCells? (snake grid cells per side); cls? (classes that may take it; absent: every composed class); weight (equal across the five families in the parity row); provenance.

The interface is split so the city view never waits for a manor: outline(input) returns the wings every LOD, export and the shadow hook use (a row's fixedWings unchanged, heights and roofs added); compose(input, outline, lod) returns wings with roofs, dormers, porches, towers, courts and rooms, lazily per visible tile at district LOD and finer (a tile draws the outline until its compositions arrive). Budgets (base outline() inside S11's geometry share, a stage-3 outline()'s admission bound and the re-declaration of S11's §12.4 row by the measured difference, compose() per building and per tile) are §12.7's.

The stage-3 contract: the union of the composed wings equals the outline's union exactly (integer equality after snapping), so O17 (i)'s identical footprint hash at every LOD holds by construction (test §13.2).

A composition's wings — generated or stored, and after every composition edit — reach every storey its base wings reach, with at least their area at each storey, so the households the capacity admits always fit its plan (F-PLAN tier 6, §5.2).

The contract reads the wings' ground rings: a wing spanning a passage (spans on base or composed wing, item 30) contributes its ground ring, its span ring lying outside the union at the ground and inside the wing's extent above.

The plan's seed rings (base or composed, clipped to tile, plan rung step 4) stand at least attractCm apart except where they share a joint, so the plan rung's transient arena inserts them unmoved (§3.4 seed contract).

The seed clip (§3.4 tileRings) gets the wings reaching a storey in the clip order: wing order, except that a wing whose extent there lies wholly inside another's is taken after that container (two identical extents keep wing order), so a contained wing has no piece at that storey (its floor is its container's; every anchor or fixed ring the plan rung places in that wing there lies in the container's piece) and no piece has a hole, which the clip refuses.

Composed towers (each a round wing to the plan rung) join the clip order at every storey they reach: a tower whose ring lies wholly inside a wing's extent and overlaps no wing taken before the first such wing (its container) is taken directly after that container, towers sharing a container in Composition.towers order; every other tower is taken before all the wings in Composition.towers order; no tower's ring lies wholly inside another tower's at a storey both reach (a stair inside a tower is its spiral core, StairCore.tower). Each tower's round room is its ring less the earlier towers it overlaps — its own piece when it precedes the wings, each wing's piece taking the arcs; a tower wholly inside a wing that overlaps a wing taken before that container is taken before the wings too (the earlier wing carries the tower's cut to the container's edge); a tower following its container has no piece there and its round room lies inside the container's piece.

where: §2.6 bays and stacks in composer rooms (F-PLAN tier 2)
items.statement: A stair core's bay or chimney stack that step 3 places inside a composer's room (a spiral core's bay inside its tower's round room, a stair or hearth stack inside a hall) stands against that room's wall, meeting its sides along one run and nowhere else, or fills the room (a stair turret); step 3 filters candidates to those staying out of every composer's room or standing in one so, leaving each composer's room less every bay and stack in one piece the transient arena accepts (§3.4: minEdge, clearance, simplicity); a refusal naming a vertex a bay or stack gives the room belongs to that bay or stack (F-PLAN tier 2, §5.2), so a refused composer's room stays the composer's bug. At each storey where such a bay or stack lies, the plan rung passes the room less it, and no room where it fills the room (§3.4 transientArena).

Every composer's room (Composition.rooms), a tower's round room included, lies inside one seed piece at its storey (the composer emits it inside its own wing's or tower's extent less the extents before it in the clip order, or inside its container's piece where the clip order leaves it none), so every fixed ring the plan rung passes lies inside one seed piece (§3.4 transientArena), and F-PLAN's abort on a refused composer's room (§5.2) marks a composer's bug.

Fourth rung (item 28): per storey the union of the plan's rooms equals the union of the extents of the wings reaching the storey (a wing's extent is its ring and, above the ground, its ring ∪ the span ring of the passage it spans), and at the ground storey also the span ring of each passage a wing of the building spans, which the plan reserves before any cut as one room of role passage, scope circulation, its two end edges exterior walls carrying the passage's arch openings (§3.10 seed-tiling row; J-A30.23).

Stage-3 intake measures the generator's outline() time per building class on B-CITY METROPOLIS seeds; above §12.7's 10 µs median, outline() runs the generator's own massing step only (wing rectangles without roofs or rooms); if still above budget, the base OutlineBuildingGenerator keeps producing the outline and stage-3 compose() is constrained to it (its wings must union to the base outline).

Diversity "from a giant manor to a small hovel" stays a property of ClassRules (data keyed by the context vector), not of the generator; the intake also runs §2.6's test with every fixture building's composition stored (§13.2), so a stage-3 generator is admitted only with compositions the base can carry and that keep the storey rule.

Entrances (owner 2026-09-26: larger buildings may have more than one entrance; always a street-facing entrance; back or side entrances where an alley presents itself optional or random but limited; back entrances recommended with a larger court or yard; item 29 (a); J-A29.21): a building's doors are a set Building.entrances, each a named footprint vertex (('entrance', building id, i), indexed, §2.2 rule 7) on the wing facing its way, carried through every footprint change by the wing-carrying rule.

deriveEntrances(building, plot, template row): one per-entity function called by S11 (§4.7), the designation mutator (item 18, §4.7 S11 — a house that becomes a shop gains its street door; a shop that closes keeps the door as a house door) and the edit layer (setEntrance, §7.1, §7.4), as deriveBase is; its draws are the siteplan.entrance concern (§6.1), so re-deriving doors disturbs no site-plan draw.

The entrance rules are defaults; the rows are the designation template's entrances columns (§10.2; item 23: the parity presets give one street entrance per building with side and rear probabilities 0 — the owner's rule (item 29) as their default, provenance owner — since neither the FTG client of the 25 September 2026 capture nor MFCG 12710731 models a door, the latter by inference; what each carries is §13.5's entrance rows; J-A50.01, J-A50.21).

Entrances rule 1 — one main entrance, always street-facing: exactly one entrance has role main, on the footprint side facing the plot's frontage access edge (wherever the site plan set the front line, §4.7 S11 recession; flush for a row), facing the street; where along that side is deriveEntrances' draw (J-A50.21). A set-back building on a multi-building plot puts its main entrance on the court or path from the plot's street gate (PlotBound.gates on the frontage: the plot itself always has a street-facing gate or door); a hidden plot's main entrance faces its access face (court or passage, item 30, §4.6); a cluster structure's faces the footpath it fronts (item 70; §4.7 S11), read the same way (J-A70.44).

Entrances rule 2 — side and rear doors only where an access edge presents itself: a side or rear entrance is drawn only where the plot has an access edge beyond its frontage (a lane, through-alley, back lane or passage face — S8's interior treatments and S10's alley rung, §4.6, §4.7), with the row's probability by class x size x band and capped by the row (capSide, capRear: one side and one rear door for ordinary classes; hovels and row houses ≈ never; ...).

Entrances rule 2 (cont.): shops and inns often on a corner; workshops and warehouses toward the lane; service entrances for institution classes, one per court side the row allows. A concealed use (item 63) adds one service or yard door flagged concealed where such an access edge onto an alley or passage presents itself — never the main door; with none its concealed rooms are reached from the front's service side (§4.7 Concealed institutions (4)).

Entrances rule 3 — a yard door is recommended: when the plot's yard parts behind or beside the building reach the row's yardDoorMinM2, a yard entrance opens onto the yard or court by default — a kitchen or service door, never a public entrance.

Entrances rule 4 — every entrance is an addressable vertex: add, move and remove are building edits (setEntrance); the main entrance moves only along the footprint side rule 1 puts it on and is never removed; entrances are re-derived when the designation mutates and kept where an edit fixed them (§7.2); ordinal i stable — a re-derived entrance re-matched by §6.3's anchor keeps it, a new one takes Building.nextEntrance, a removed one's is never re-used (J-A29.23).

Entrances rule 5 — the plan opens a door at every entrance and roots its circulation at the main one; side, rear, yard and service doors are secondary roots (a plan may have more than one way in); the passage room's two arch openings are the passage's own ways through (kind passage, no entrance); a door from the building onto the passage is a side entrance facing passage (rule 2; item 30, J-A30.23).

§5.3 rows: exactly one main entrance per building, facing its street, court or passage, or footpath (rule 1); no side or rear entrance without an access edge beyond the frontage. Test: §13.2's entrance bars on B-CITY-lite.

Building.basement is derived by "the same function" (the text does not name it: see MC-06), never rolled alone, from the class row's cellar columns (§10.2: base probability by class — cellars for inns, taverns, breweries, storehouses, manors, keeps and temples by row, none for hovels, tents, sheds, shacks and lean-to shelters; the kind weights; slope threshold slopeCm; the rock cost; cellar depth depthCm default 220 cm; ring inset insetCm default 60; for a building carrying a concealed use the higher probability of its front's and concealed class's rows, §4.7 Concealed institutions (4), item 63), raised within the class band by the prosperity value and by size and storeys (larger and taller more likely), and gated by the terrain from §2.3's facts and the context vector — no new raster.
items.note: "derived by the same function" — the referent (deriveEntrances vs deriveBase) is implicit; see conflicts (ambiguity).

items.statement: Water table: the nearest water body's surface elevation (its shore's terrain sample) plus freeboard freeboardCm (default 50) for a plot within waterTableM (default 40 m) of a shore; elsewhere the height of the drainage line: the hydro cell nearest the footprint's centroid whose flowAccum reaches drainageAccumCells (ties by cell index; where no cell reaches it, no water table limits the cellar).

Basement terrain gate (the three values freeboardCm, waterTableM, drainageAccumCells are §10.2's basement-gate row): no cellar where terrainClass is damp or flood, or where even a half-cellar's floor (wing baseCm less half the cellar depth) would lie below the water table; half-cellar where the full cellar's floor (baseCm less the depth) would lie below it and the half-cellar's would not, or where terrainClass is low; walk-out where the fall under the footprint exceeds the row's slopeCm (the same samples deriveBase reads); rock lowers the probability by the row's cost.

The basement lies inside the ground storey's wings and smaller than their union (Basement.ring, inset by cellar.insetCm), has its own storeys (Basement.floors, read by Heights.floorsBelow; its floor = baseCm less the depth per storey).

Basement.access is derived with it: external for a walk-out, else the class's programme row's basementAccess read at the plot's builtBand (§10.2) — a shell fact that never moves with the occupants and is edited with the basement (setAttr(basement)); the plan rung reads it (step 3).

The basement ring follows every footprint change by the wing-carrying rule (rule 2 (b); rule 4 on a ring that no longer fits; J-A29.23); editable (setAttr(basement), §7.1; an edited basement is kept through terrain changes, §7.3 (a)); re-derived when its terrain gate changes.

A cellar never joins a sewer as a room (item 12: underground neighbourhoods front sewer tunnels only; J-A12.42): a way down from a basement to an underground element (stair, ladder, hatch, or a door through the basement wall into an adjacent sewer dwelling) is an AccessPoint record (II.7.4, source basement), made by II.7.3's Basement accesses: a probability by class x band x age x concealment, gated by the basement's reach to an underground element (item 64).

Emulation note: MFCG and FTG have no cellars; Dwellings' basement share n / (n + 1) (n = storeys over the ground; Dwellings itch 17195045's code, replay-confirmed, D2) is a descriptive baseline, never a gate (§13.5); the terrain gate and the prosperity term are our extensions (item 23).
§5.3 rows: no cellar under the flood band (a requested crawl space, which is no storey, excepted); every basement inside its ground-storey footprint and smaller than it.

A requested basement (item 66; J-A66.21): when an edit's closure needs a basement the building lacks (addUndergroundAccess, §7.3 item 9; II.7.6's pieces) the decision runs as a request overriding the class probability, never the terrain gate, and takes the richest lawful form in fixed order: (1) a full cellar; (2) a half cellar where the full cellar's floor would lie below the water table, or a walk-out where the fall passes slopeCm; (3) a crawl space where the plot is damp or flood or even the half cellar's floor would lie under the water table — the ground storey raised by cellar.depthCm / 2 above deriveBase's datum, a void beneath it inside the inset ring, reached by a hatch (kind crawl, floors 0, access trapdoor) — lawful where the lowest terrain sample under the footprint lies above the water table, a damp or flood plot included.

Requested basement (4): otherwise a refusal naming the gate each form failed (F-EDIT, §5.2), never a silent substitute. The closure records the basement it created (§7.3 item 9 (c)): it reverts to the derived decision once nothing that needed it remains, unless the user edited it; the plan rung reserves the access's stair, ladder or hatch (step 3) and is marked stale (§2.8).

items.owner: model (base carries interface; built by V03 interiors, M6-P)
items.statement: The plan rung — fourth rung of the building ladder (owner 2026-09-26: a coherent floor plan tailored to building type and function; item 28; J-A28.21; the Dwellings synthesis, research/findings/dwellings-synthesis.md, ideas only): ladder outline -> wings -> rooms -> plan (Composition.lod); the plan is the building's floor plan per storey, derived by BuildingGenerator.plan from the composed exterior and the building's content, never from a shape of its own; staged with the Fantasy-Manor buildings in the owner's order; runs function first (the reverse of the reference's partition-then-label).

The base carries for the plan rung: the records, the step's signature, the streams (§6.1), the events (§7.1), the elaboration record and cache (§2.8, §2.9), the trigger policy (§4.1), the draw, export and budget rows (§8.5, §11.1, §12.7), F-PLAN (§5.2) and §13.2's bars; adding the rung later is a registration.

Plan step 1 inputs — nothing is rolled: the wings reaching each storey (BaseWing.ring or composed Wing.footprint, with their spans at level >= 1 and at the ground storey the spanned passage's span ring), each wing's Heights.floors, the basement (ring, floors), the entrance set, composed towers, courts and porch, the class and its designation template's programme row (§10.2, read at the occupants' band — the plot's fieldBand, J-A19.43), the use, assignment and sub-locations (one room each), the concealed uses (item 63), the basement's accesses (item 64), the running Works' stage (item 67), the households housed, and each spanned passage (span ring = seed ring and fixed ring, the passage room, J-A30.23). A plan is a pure function of the building's committed state and its own streams (§4.1 contract, §6.2).

Plan step 2 programme: from the programme row and interior ladder, a ProgramRoom list — each household's unit at its ladder row's form, the shared, service and staff rooms the row allows, the class's own rooms (a smithy's forge, an inn's common room, a chapel's nave), one room per sub-location, each concealed use's programme rows (§10.2 RoomRuleRow.concealed, flagged concealed; item 63) — each sized in m² (row triple x ladder size factor, interpolated along the occupants' value) with its storey rule, exterior demand, opening kind, adjacencies, hearth and priority; counts by the row's law (const, perStorey, perHousehold, perCapacity, perSubLocation; a fractional count drawn on plan.program).

Plan step 3 allocation: each storey's capacity = the area of the extents of the wings reaching it (passage room excluded) less the row's circulation share; hard rooms go by their storey rule, soft rooms by priority until capacity is met, household units first (F-PLAN tier 0, §5.2: a unit falls to the next poorer form before anything is dropped; no tier drops a unit).

where: §2.6 plan rung step 3 stair core and basement access (J-A29.25
items.statement: Plan step 3 stair core: StairCore (a bay of the wing the row's stair.placement names, or the composed tower as a spiral — standing against the wall of any composer's room it lies in) placed before any cut, serving every storey of its wing and the basement as Basement.access says: core — takes a bay inside Basement.ring and inside its wing's seed piece at every storey served (candidates filtered by exact containment as §3.4 requires of a fixed ring; the container's piece where the clip order leaves the wing none); trapdoor, or the fallback where no candidate fits the ring (core stopping at the ground storey) — a core of kind trapdoor serving basement storeys and the ground storey, its bay inside the ring and one ground-storey seed, from the same filtered candidates — fallback reported, writing no building record (Basement.access stays as derived; a click changes no digest, §6.2); where not even that bay fits the basement is unreachable, which F-PLAN takes (§5.2 tier 1; J-A29.25).

Plan step 3 external (walk-out's outside stair): core stops at the ground storey; a door (Opening kind door) opens the basement in the side of Basement.ring among those at least two of step 4's wing-local modules long (a door's width) whose midpoint samples lowest on the terrain (deriveBase's sampler; ties by ring index); where no side is that long the basement is joined by the trapdoor fallback, reported.

Plan step 3 anchors: the entrance rooms (one per entrance) and hearth rooms are anchors fixed in their wing and side before any cut; each access into the basement (item 64: an AccessPoint of source basement, II.7.3) is a fixed anchor of the basement storey — its stair, ladder, trapdoor or door placed before any cut, a crawl space's hatch an opening of kind trapdoor in the ground storey — and the passage room is its span ring fixed whole (step 1), so stairs are stacked by construction.

Plan step 4 partition to targets: each wing of each storey is cut on the rung's transient arena (§3.4; J-A28.31) — seed rings = the extents of the wings reaching the storey clipped to tile (overlaps: each extent less the union of those before it in the clip order, by §3.4 tileRings) and at the ground storey each span ring; fixed rings = the stair core's bay, the chimney stacks, the passage room (span ring, both seed and fixed) and the composer's rooms each less a bay or stack it holds — by the storey's layout pattern, with remaining rooms' target areas as the stop rule and pieces assigned to programme rooms as they are cut (no room waits for a label).

Layout patterns (a weighted row per storey class in the programme row): bisect — recursive cuts across the region's short axis from a re-entrant corner where one exists; follow — cuts parallel to the long sides (a gallery on the court or street side); spine — a corridor along the wing's axis with rooms off it (lodging house's and inn's upper floors); hall_and_parlour — one cross cut with the hearth room larger; cross_passage — a through passage at the entrance with rooms either side; enfilade — rooms in a row with aligned doors; nave — one room.
Cuts are planned on a wing-local module — a table row, default 50 cm, in the wing's OBB frame; the planner's grid, never a second lattice.
Cuts are written back as world lattice points (Room.ring), so walls are exact centimetre polylines, never cells; slivers and one-bay strips merge into circulation.

where: §2.6 plan rung step 5 circulation and openings (D3)
items.statement: Plan step 5 circulation and openings: the room graph is built as a spanning tree first (priced by the programme, the pattern's hub — spine, hall, stair hall — preferred, a bedroom's or store's degree capped by its row), loops added by rule, never by chance (a kitchen to the yard door; a hall to the parlour and the stair; an enfilade's doors) — Dwellings itch 17195045 keeps half its non-redundant extra doors at random, a loop baseline describing the reference (D3) that binds nothing; a door at every entrance rooted at the main one (side, rear, yard, service secondary roots, item 29 (5)); a walk-out basement's outside door (external) the root of the basement's storeys; stair-core doors on every storey served; each unit's own entry door (the ladder); a passage opening in each end wall of the passage room (item 30). Openings and windows are records on wall segments.

A concealed room (item 63) is joined only to other concealed rooms, to service rooms and to the room behind a concealed or service door, never to the public hub the main entrance roots, so the concealed programme is entered only by a service, yard or concealed door (§5.3's row).

Plan step 6 exterior coherence: per storey the rooms tile the wing extents reaching it (fourth rung; a wing of fewer floors is roof at that level; a basement's outline is Basement.ring); chimneys derived from hearth columns rising to the roof (Chimney, drawn by §8.6); dormers placed from the top storey's roofed rooms with exterior demand (Wing.dormers becomes derived, one per such room's façade bay, capped by the eave length); the porch sits at the main entrance; a composed tower is a round room per storey with the spiral inside (radialSplit for two), its bay against the room's wall; windows follow each room's exterior demand, one per façade bay of its exterior wall, aligned across storeys where a wall stacks; furniture is abstract shapes by role from the row's furnish columns, never blocking an opening or the stair bay; materials stay texture only.

where: §2.6 plan rung step 7 streams and re-rolls
items.statement: Plan step 7 streams and re-rolls: four concerns plan.program, plan.layout, plan.roles, plan.furnish, keyed with the rung's own reroll (§6.1); New random on plan.layout (regenerate with rung, §7.1) re-partitions and keeps the wings, entrances and stair core; on plan.roles re-assigns roles and what hangs off them (windows, door kinds, furniture), moving no wall.

Plan edits: room roles, walls, openings, windows, the stair core and a room's unit are events scoped to the building (§7.1: setRoomRole, moveWall, splitRoom, mergeRooms, setOpening, setWindow, moveStairCore, setRoomUnit; a room lockable on its path); the first plan edit stores the composition with its plan, whose rings and points carryWings carries (J-P48).

where: §2.6 plan rung step 7 failure, values, cost
items.statement: A programme that does not fit is F-PLAN's (§5.2), per building, never whole-house. Rooms are values, never L4 faces, so a click changes no plat and no digest (§6.2). Cost: one plan per click within §12.7's row; the room graph is exported in our own schema (§11.1).

where: §2.6 plan rung under Works and decline (item 67 (h), (j))
items.statement: A building whose running Works stands before FINISHED shows its plan as walls without doors, windows or furniture up to the storey its stage has raised; a decayed or ruined building its fallen walls and open rooms — a drawing of the same plan, nothing stored; the stage counts among the rung's recorded inputs (§2.8), so a stage change marks the plan stale (item 67 (h), (j)).

where: §2.6 elaboration by click and rung states (item 28 (b)-(c)
items.statement: Elaboration by click (owner: once generated it is saved until something changes from the simulator; item 28 (b)-(c); J-A28.22): when a rung is derived is the viewer's elaborate key (§2.9; click — the owner's default — or view within §12's budgets; §4.1 states the policy); what it derives is fixed. Per building and per lazy rung an elaboration record (§2.8) holds state absent / current / stale / edited with the digest of the rung's recorded inputs; a batch changing one marks the rung stale, the cached result stays on view with a change marker at every zoom (§8.5), and the next click re-derives it as a mutation from its canonical prior (the stored plan where one exists, else the as-built plan carried along the interior ladder) — never from the cache and never by a re-roll (§7.3); viewing never re-derives a current rung.
Pre-assigned plots are the eager content decision of §2.5 and §4.1: assigned at the city level, "just not generated" until the click.

The interior ladder — the interior has no floor (owner 2026-09-27: the geometry floor on prosperity does not bind the interior; same building geometry but not the interior): item 31's geometry floor bounds what is BUILT (a shell never reads poorer than its geometryFloor by wealth change alone, §4.11); the interior reads WHO IS THERE — the plan's programme is written for the occupants' band (the plot's current prosperity field value at its sample point, the one §7.2's brush compares, banded by §4.5's rule = Plot.fieldBand, kept until the value crosses a cut by more than the hysteresis and re-banded at every epoch; = ContextVector.prosperity/prosperityBand at derivation, following the field after it without re-deriving the plot; J-A19.43, J-A31.43, J-A28.29), never the manifested band and never geometryFloor — and for the household count (Building.households); the plan is re-cut inside the unchanged shell as they change.

So a mansion district growing poor keeps its big shells while their interiors fill with families; the poor of a developed town live in re-cut interiors behind grand fronts (this rule), in back courts behind them (item 30, §4.11 rung 2) and in the cheap stock of the edge (item 27's shanty rule, §4.5).

The interior ladder is one table keyed by the band names of §4.5's band set (FieldBands.bands; its middle row is the band FieldBands.middle names, so the shell's floor and the interior's middle agree per settlement), read at the occupants' band and interpolated along the value inside a row.

The per-class programme rows (§10.2) follow the interior ladder and add what a class needs; its rows are InteriorLadderRows, the interiorLadder table of roomProgram.json (§7.6); the default rows are our own, calibratable (§13.9), tendencies changeable per region and era (item 23 — no reference has interiors that follow their occupants); with no epoch every residential building houses what §4.7's generation fill gives it (at least one household, never above capacity), so the static baseline is unchanged.

Interior ladder default rows (band: form; households per shell clamped into [1, capacity]; unit rooms; shared rooms; staff rooms count, size share, placement; circulation; size factor): rich — house (whole shell); [1,1]; hall, parlours, chambers, a solar, kitchen with hearth, buttery and stores; none; staff chambers one per two principal chambers, 0.35, in attic, basement or service wing, never beside the owners' rooms on a storey that has them; few corridors: a stair hall, enfilade or hall_and_parlour; 1.25. prosperous — house; [1,1]; hall or parlour, chambers, kitchen with hearth, a store; none; one staff chamber, 0.40, service side or attic; a stair hall; 1.10. comfortable (the middle) — dwelling (kitchen with hearth, parlour, chambers); [1,2]; kitchen, parlour, chambers; none (two households divide the shell by storey or wing, each with own door off the stair hall); none; a stair hall; 1.00. modest (lodging house) — lodging (chamber and parlour); [2, capacity]; chamber, parlour; a shared kitchen with hearth on the ground storey by the stair core, a common room where the class row allows; none; a corridor or stair hall so every unit has its own door (spine upper storeys); 0.85. poor (tenement) — apartment (bedroom and small cooking place); [3, capacity]; bedroom, cooking place (hearth where the class row allows); shared facilities where the class row says; none; a double-loaded corridor (spine) on every storey, the stair core its hub; 0.65. squalid (destitute) — room (single room off the corridor); [4, capacity]; one room, no cooking place; shared facilities or none; none; spine; 0.50.

The dwelling unit (J-A28.25): every room of scope unit belongs to exactly one household (Room.unit); Plan.units lists each household's form and entry door; a household's unit is the rooms of its building's plan carrying its id (§2.7). Unit-door rule: each unit has its own entry door onto circulation (corridor, stair hall or landing) or onto the street (an entrance), never through another unit's room (§5.3's row; a setRoomUnit or plan edit that would break it is refused, F-EDIT, §5.2); shared and service rooms open onto circulation; units given to households in address order by default; setRoomUnit overrides.

capacity(b) = min(households.max of the designation template at the plot's builtBand (§10.2), floor(Σ over storeys s at or above the ground of A(s) x (den - num) / (2 * den * minRoomCm2))); A(s) = exact integer twice-area (area2, §3.2 (6)) of the union of the extents of the building's base wings (Building.wings with their spans) reaching storey s — never a composition's wings, stored or derived, so neither a click nor a stored composition moves it (§6.2): at the ground the footprint face's area2 (passage room excluded); above it the sum of the extents' area2 where the pairing holds (tiled; a span ring lies outside every wing ring) and the kernel's boolean union (§3.7) where it fails; num/den = circulation share (RoomProgramRow.circulation, integer fraction, §10.2); minRoomCm2 = minimum area of the room form's one room (RoomRuleRow.area[0], cm²), both read from the class's programme at the band set's first, poorest band (FieldBands.bands[0]) — a property of the shell alone; basement storeys excluded.

A building S11 builds for a slot without houses (§10.2, §4.7) has capacity 0 — the slot's typing, like the template row, a fact of what the shell was built as, never of its occupants. Every host computes the same integer. The generation fill (§4.7: S10b places the households on the plot; S11 creates the building and wings and writes each residential building's households clamped into [1, capacity]), §4.11's relet and F-PLAN (§5.2) read this one function, so solver and plan never disagree.

where: §2.6 capacity bound holds through every change (§4.7 overflow pass)
items.statement: A committed change lowering a building's capacity below its households count — S11's operator (§4.7), a rewrite of the plot's builtBand (J-A31.44 paths), a change of its wings' extents (carry after warp/moveVertex, or a moved face of a passage it spans, moving span rings), a setAttr of its heights or class, or a §7.6 edit of a table the function reads (designation template households.max or a structure's houses cell, the class's liveIn, the circulation share or the least room-form area in the class's programme row at the first band, or the band set) — re-homes the households past the capacity (the last in address order, passing over a locked or pinned one, which keeps its building, §7.2) by §4.7's overflow pass inside the causing event, each move a lifecycle event (relocate, §2.8); a hand edit lists the moves among its dry-run fates (§7.3 item 4), takes receiving buildings into its effective scope (§7.3 item 1), and its undo restores them (§7.4).

No capacity-lowering change is refused for it, except a hand edit whose excess cannot be re-homed — its locked and pinned households alone above the new capacity, or, without a dossier, a household no residential building of the district has room for (on a dossier-bound map every household fills the dossier's population and is re-housed by §4.7's re-provision) — which returns F-EDIT naming them, as a hand relet above the capacity does; S11's operator and an epoch's step leave a building whose locked or pinned households alone would exceed its new capacity unchanged (as a lock stops a rung-3 re-cut, §4.11; any locked entity is a fixed input, §7.2); a household no building of the district can take in a generation run or an epoch is F-SITING's (§5.2, J-A28.46).

The capacity is the owner's "the more rooms for more occupying families the richer a building gets", read on the building: a shell built richer has more rooms to let (its households.max rises with builtBand) while the households actually housed follow the occupants' band.

Never omit a household: the count the plan must house is bounded by the capacity computed with the smallest form, so the room form always fits; a unit falls to the next poorer form (house -> dwelling -> lodging -> apartment -> room) before any room is dropped, and no tier of F-PLAN omits a unit (§5.2, J-A28.51); a hand relet above the capacity is refused (F-EDIT).

The re-cut (J-A28.26): a change of the occupants' band or household count re-cuts the plan as item 18's mutation applied to rooms. FIXED (each in the form the transient arena takes it, §3.4; J-A28.33): the shell — each storey's seed rings (wing extents clipped to tile as step 4 passes them; at the ground each span ring; below ground Basement.ring) opened again unchanged; every entrance and its door and the hearths (anchors before any cut, step 3); and as fixed rings the stair core's bay, chimney stacks, passage room, composer's rooms (each less a bay or stack) and the rooms the least-disruption rule keeps. RE-DERIVED: partition walls, corridors, doors, roles and units.

Least disruption: a room whose seed ring (its wing's extent at that storey clipped to tile, or Basement.ring) is unchanged and whose ring fits a role of the new programme (area inside the role's [min, max], storey rule met) keeps its ring and address even when its role or unit changes; a shell mutation by item 18 keeps nothing in a wing whose clipped seed changed — which re-cuts a wing's rooms too wherever a change to an overlapping wing earlier or later in the clip order alters that wing's clipped seed (the clip's crossing vertices included, §3.4). Re-uniting households removes what the subdivision added — exactly for an unstored plan (its canonical chain returns the earlier plan); a stored plan's re-cut keeps by least disruption the subdivided rooms still fitting a role, its rings keeping the composition-role vertices its re-cuts added (J-P48 (1)), which the shell's identity reads without; its undo restores it exactly (§7.4).

The canonical chain: the plan for (band row r, count n) is derived from the as-built plan (the class's programme at the plot's builtBand row with the template's households.built clamped into [1, capacity], whatever that row's household range) by a fixed order of least-disruption steps, each a re-cut from the previous as its prior: first the ROWS, one band at a time from the built row toward r along FieldBands.bands, the count at each step clamped into that row's household range; then the HOUSEHOLDS, one at a time from the clamped count to n. The result depends on (r, n) alone — never on when a click, epoch or relet reached it (§6.2, §6.5 (9); each step's draws keyed by its target, §6.1; the cache memoises steps, §2.9); a return to the as-built row and count is the as-built plan exactly.

A STORED plan is re-cut inside the event that changes its inputs, around its edited and locked rooms, with the inverse recorded (§7.3, §7.4; J-A28.72); that re-cut establishes J-P48 (1) for its new walls in the same event (a same-level split moving nothing), so the shell's identity across a re-cut is read on its rings with the composition-role vertices removed, as §7.3 item 7 (ii) reads them (§5.3, T28-14). Each step is one open, cut and read-back of the transient arena, counted by §12.7's plan row.

Staff rooms are dwarfed beside the owners' (size a share of the owners' principal chamber's target, the row's column) and sit where a house keeps its service: the attic, basement or service wing before a storey the owners' rooms occupy; a lodging house's shared kitchen or common room sits on the ground storey by the stair core, the circulation hub; both are programme rows (scope service and shared), so a class or culture may keep a common kitchen down to the poor row or drop it earlier.
A room's unit (setRoomUnit), its role and walls (the plan events) and the household count by hand (relet, a convert on the building, §7.1) are events; the ladder's rows are §7.6 tables.
Interior ladder bars: §13.2's T28-13 - T28-18.

[{end 0|1; on ∈ {shore, bank, cliff, enceinte}; vertex ('anchor', id, end)}] (typed end anchors of an open chain); waterfront; placement; strips; band; glacis? {inner?, outer}; thicknessCm; walkCm; heightCm; base; setbackCm {inner, outer} (both faces unbuildable); intervallum? (the lane inside the wall when the era row asks); material; supersededBy?; gates; towers; moat?; stage; lifecycle }.

Enceinte.waterfront ∈ {open, quay_wall, sea_wall} — a preset row: open (MFCG's default and FTG's captured open chain: no wall along quays and beaches), quay_wall (a wall along the waterfront) or sea_wall (a full wall); where their water gates stand is §4.4 S5a's.
Enceinte.placement ∈ {aroundAll, aroundStage}: aroundStage walls only a stage's new ring, anchored on the previous enceinte (FTG's "around stage lots").

Enceinte.strips {inner, outer}: the two L1 wall-strip faces S7 cuts beside the trace (§4.8): inside band + inner setback (bounded by the setback line or the intervallum); outside band + outer setback + glacis, or the berm up to a moat; S8 never cuts them and lanes end on them (§4.6). band {inner, outer}: L3 half-bands on each side of the L1 wall chain built by bandUnion inside the strips by S10's step (0) (§4.7); nesting holds. glacis? {inner?, outer}.
Enceinte.base: ChainProfile (base_knot on the trace): the wall's base elevation, one knot per trace vertex S7 places, linear between (§2.2 rule 5).
Enceinte.supersededBy? (item 8): the shorter inner ring that replaced this one (§4.11 contractWall); the old ring's record stays live and its line persists as a trace.

[VertexRef, VertexRef] (a water gate: ('gate_end', id, 0|1), its two bank vertices on the trace; the wall's edge between them lies across the water, §2.2 rule 7; held under a warp unless fromLevel = 0, as a Bridge's deck ends are, §3.6) }.

Labels are the model records LabelEntity and QuarterNode of §9.1.

Institution { id; kind; plots; buildings; faction? (the module's materialised Faction when it exists, §10.1); roster: RosterRef; name: NameRef; reservation?; knownTo? (item 30: a dossier fact (§7.7) or an edit, defaulting from its plots' exposure; a local or secret institution prefers hidden plots (§4.7 S10b) and underground a cellar stair (II.7.3)); concealment? ∈ {none, front, hidden, underground} (item 63: the dossier's fact or the mode its concealed use resolved, §4.7 Concealed institutions (1); absent none); powers? [{power (PowerStanding key, §7.7 layer 2); weight}] (item 79: the powers it answers to, weights sum 1 — absent: its class's rows apply, §10.2; present: the dossier's override or an edit) }.

items.statement: Use { id (the address: moves with the use when it relocates, §6.3; a building keeps its own); cls (the roster class, §10.2 BuildingClassRow.id); specialisation? (the designation template's discrete row at the band, §4.7 S11, item 19); plot; buildings (several for a compound or joined plot); assignment?; owner? (household | business | institution); pinned (item 17 (d): stays under an epoch, the town adapts around it, §7.7); concealment?; concealmentSource?; front?; knownTo?; opened {epoch, seq}; closed? {epoch, seq}; lifecycle } — item 17: a use is separate from the building housing it; it opens, closes and relocates (§4.11's use step; §7.1 openUse / closeUse / relocateUse) while the building persists, vacant or re-let; Building.use points at it (§2.6).

Use.concealment? ∈ {none, front, hidden, underground} (item 63): a concealed use's mode, resolved when first placed (§4.7 Concealed institutions (1)) and re-resolved only when a dossier event withdraws the dossier's mode. concealmentSource? ∈ {assignment, class, edit}: the map-side origin of a mode the dossier did not set — written with the mode by §4.7's placement rule and by setAttr(concealment) (edit); absent while the dossier sets it. A dossier event setting the mode clears it (an edit it displaces is reported and orphaned, §7.7 item 5; J-A20.73); one withdrawing the dossier's mode re-resolves it from the map-side sources and re-places the use (J-A63.22). Whether the mode is a dossier fact is factTier's (§2.8); a mode the dossier set is dossier-owned, so a map setAttr of it is refused (§7.7 items 7, 11; J-A20.77, J-A63.22). Read by §11.2's why on the use's concealment under the caller's key.

Use.front? (item 63): the front's Use — the working business whose building (Building.use) it hides in; absent for a bare hidden or underground use. Use.knownTo? (item 63): a concealed use's own knowledge, secret by default; absent on an open use, which the reader reads through its building and institution (§9.2).

(the build or repair it fed)}] } (item 8 (d)): one per document, changed only by §4.11's salvage events, so inside the model digest; its only effect on the map is to weight clearance toward nearby building (§4.11).
