LightSource { id; kind (a light-rule row's kind: torch, lantern, lamp post, brazier, fire pit, campfire, magical orb, shrine lamp ... data, §4.7 LightRule); source ∈ {fire, magic}; point (moves with its host under a warp or vertex move, §7.4); host (the building, way, square, gate, bridge, castle, pin, decoration (a wayside shrine), tunnel, gallery, chamber or access point it belongs to — for a hand-placed light the entity placeLight names or finds under its point, §7.1; its arena is its Identity.key's); entrance? (a door light: its building's entrance ordinal); heightCm (above the host's surface); intensityCd (candela); radiusCm (the smooth cutoff of §8.4's falloff); sizeCm (flame's or orb's own radius, setting §8.4's penumbra — written at placement from its kind's light-table row, §4.7); colour (sRGB: fire warm, magic cool — its row's, written at placement, the colour §8.4 (c) lights with; the vector rung's glyph and glow take §8.2's light and lights roles instead); flicker? (a fire light flickers — written at placement from its row; §8.4 (f) animates it as a pure function of its render key and view time, §6.1; J-A68.61, never drawn or stored; absent: steady); rule; lifecycle }.

Item 68: a point light placed by rule (§4.7 Light sources) or by hand (placeLight, §7.1); lit windows, the plan rung's room lights and light shafts are derived sources, never records (§8.4; J-A28.32); a light is unlit while its host is abandoned, decayed or under Works before FINISHED — a reading, never a stored state.

Dossier staged record (item 88; schema-complete, empty in the base; the port fills it at the SettlementForge stage, §7.7 item 8, §14): ConditionOverlay { id; key (its binding key cond:<id>, §7.7 item 12); archetype; severity 0-1; sinceWeek; untilWeek?; lifecycle } — a condition standing between epochs, no geometry: §8.2's thematic overlay, §4.11's Works share and the clerk read it.

DepositSite { id; key (res:<key>); family (ore, stone, clay, salt ... data); state ∈ {available, depleted, removed, discovered}; bearingCdeg (its bearing from the centre); landUse? (the quarry, mine or claypit LandUse it anchors, §4.9); lifecycle } — a state change converts the land use it anchors (§4.11).

PowerRelation { id; key (its two powers' binding keys joined in address order — a pair of existing keys, no key form of its own, §7.7 item 12); a, b (PowerStanding keys, §7.7 layer 2); kind (the dossier's pair type: alliance, rivalry, feud ... data); strength 0-1; lifecycle } — read by §4.5's typing as a soft adjacency row and by item 72 (a)(2)'s political component.

HistoryHint { ageYears (the settlement's age at creation — never advanced by the host's weeks, whose clock is §4.11's); scars [{type (fire, flood, siege, plague ... data); yearsAgo; severity 0-1}] } — Recipe.history (§2.9): a recipe input read by S2's growth-stage count (§4.2 S2), by II.7.6's catacomb age (ageYears) and, for a fire or flood scar, by II.7.6's buried old town (J-A88.42).
People are derived and never materialised in the document unless an explicit edit pins them (§10.3); which people a user has opened is per-user view state (§2.9), outside every digest.
Content references geometry by id and never the reverse, so the map can be regenerated without deleting content and content re-solved without moving the map.

Both faces of a wall are unbuildable (MFP-9): setbackCm.inner and setbackCm.outer are both unbuildable bands; the invariant "footprints ∩ (band ⊕ setback) = ∅ on both faces" is hard (§5.3), and ribbon plots start beyond the outer setback (§4.4).

How S5a lays open traces, waterfronts and stage rings is §4.4's; how S7 cuts wall strips and builds bands, towers, gatehouses and the castle is §4.8's; how bridges are sited, built and kept as sites is §4.2 S1 (5)'s and §4.8's (COV-FTG-G09, COV-FTG-G10, FTG-8).

Faction gains goals, named roles with member criteria and a secret flag (COV-FTG-B12) and the kinds military and arcane (item 79); Government is a blueprint circumstance whose offices force seats (COV-FTG-B13, §10.2); Religion carries a generated pantheon, practice share and clergy rate (COV-FTG-B14); Person carries a status and a carer (COV-FTG-C08); the relation store holds family units, relations, memberships and postings (FTG-9, COV-FTG-C04); SiteResources makes raw-resource availability a site property (COV-FTG-B09); LandUse carries crop and livestock (COV-NG-VS27); Greenery.species the species mix (COV-FTG-I11); Decoration the hinterland decoration table's output (COV-FTG-I12); Pin the complete furniture vocabulary — statue, monument, bandstand, market cross, campfire, fire pit, stall (COV-FTG-J02, COV-NG-XB23, COV-NG-CR23, COV-MFCG-I01, COV-FTG-J05, COV-FTG-E07) — and the notice post (item 82).
The content records' placement rules are in §4.7 S11 and §4.9; the point lights' are §4.7's Light sources, their lighting §8.4's (item 68).

The base types the settlement's powers as standings, never entities: each power is a PowerStanding of §7.7's circumstance slice (its key, kind, share of standing and the value the dials last applied); Faction stays the module's materialised record (§10.1, J-9). Institution.powers is the partition item 72 (d5) needs.

Absent, an institution answers to its class's powers (§10.2 BuildingClassRow.powers and RosterTables.powerLinks, item 72 (d″)(1)). Present, it is the dossier's override: the port writes it from the powers' controlled-institution lists (controlledInstitutions, resolved by §7.7 item 12's key law) and moves it only at an epoch past the dials' hysteresis (§4.11), two powers controlling one institution sharing it by relative standing (§4.5 (7)); the dossier's declared link lists would enter, were they ever present, before that partition — controls at full weight, funds 0.6, staffs 0.5, protects 0.4.

A powers the dossier set is a dossier fact (§2.8 fact tiers); otherwise setAttr overrides it (§7.1). An arcane power is a dossier fact or, standalone, exists only under the magic circumstance (§7.7 layer 2; D-3); a hidden power keeps its kind and sets secret — PowerStanding.secret in the base, Faction.secret when the module materialises it (§10.1; J-A79.23).

SkyIsland gives the owner-staged sky layer its data model now: an island exists only where prosperity supplies it (item 10; II.6's supply law — none without it; area from the carried districts' and the town's prosperity; altitude from the town's; only at CITY and METROPOLIS and never certain, items 13 and 15) for one of two reasons — a very prosperous neighbourhood or set of neighbourhoods, or a unique institution (a palace overlooking the land, a cathedral, a prison) — by rule or by assignment; may carry own terrain echoing the ground's (terrainEcho: a conjured river with the ground river's bearing); wanes, settles or falls as its supply fails (state, §4.11); no relation to the underground layer.

A tunnel records what it drains (serves), where it falls (invert profile), where it discharges (outfall), whether it is navigable and how it closed — the underground fades like the walls, caving in or being sealed, never demolished by the engine (item 11); underground neighbourhoods along navigable tunnels are ordinary blocks, plots and buildings in the sewer network's part (part 0; II.7.3; §2.1, §2.2 rule 1), reached through AccessPoint records (II.7.4).

The underground layer's other systems (item 65) are the same kind of hook — UndergroundSystem, Gallery, Chamber and UndergroundLink, each in its system's arena part, and the undercity's neighbourhoods as undercity districts (§2.5) — schema-complete and empty until the owner-staged stages run (II.7.5, II.7.6), a dug system included: the base carries the access edit addUndergroundAccess and its closure rule (§7.3 item 9 (d)), whose underground pieces (a dug system among them) run once the layer's stages exist (II.7.4; item 66); their rules are II.6's and II.7's.

ConditionOverlay, DepositSite, PowerRelation and HistoryHint (on the recipe, §2.9), with the dossier-backed Person, give every optional input of the dossier a home now, schema-complete and empty in the base: the port fills them at the SettlementForge stage (§7.7 item 8); their readers — §4.11's Works share and land-use conversions, §4.5's typing, item 72's political component, S2's stage count (§4.2 S2), II.7.6's catacomb age and buried old town — read nothing until then.

A dossier-backed Person is a notable the dossier names: pinned whole (never derived away by a re-roll), carrying Identity.dossier, housed by rule in the district of its institution or its power's seat, with a Posting at its named institution and a Membership in its named power; a successor re-binds to its record through the receipt §7.7 item 12 names.

Every entity record has five parts, and a kind with lazily derived rungs (a building, a stage-2 close-up) a sixth, its elaboration record (item 28): identity (what it is and where its random numbers come from — persisted, in the model digest); lifecycle (does it exist and what the user fixed — persisted, in the digest); attributes and geometry references (§2.2-§2.7 model content, geometry through the kernel's owner and role tables); derivation record (inputs of its derivation — persisted for kinds whose stage declares one, outside the model digest); provenance (how it was last derived — rebuilt by every derivation, never persisted, never in the model digest; LC-25).

An entity carrying a generated name also persists that name's naming record (the naming inputs of its last draw — outside the model digest). The persisted derivation and naming records form the snapshot's records digest (§6.2), checked at every in-window load and by the verification replay (§2.9 step 3).

@plat/model: Hash64 = [u32, u32]; Hash128 = 4 x u32 lanes; LineageHash = Hash64; PointCm = LatticePoint, Point = PointCm, VecCm = PointCm (one point shape, §2.2, three names); Polygon = PointCm[] (one ring); PolygonCm = PointCm[][] (outer ring then holes).
One point shape with three names: PointCm, Point, VecCm (all = LatticePoint).

M = number (metres: a derived or reported length, never an arena coordinate); Cdeg = number (i32 centidegrees); CmArray = Int32Array (integer centimetres per element) — the unit-branded types of §2.1.

Identity { id (address id, §6.3); kind; parent? (containment parent: a field, never parsed from the id); key: PlatKey (the arena — one per entity: every entity's geometry lies in one part, save an UndergroundLink whose two link_end vertices lie one in each part its ends name (§3.4), its address keyed on end a's part; a record joining parts names the other part's records by id, §3.4; J-A65.31); lineage: LineageHash (stream identity, §6.3); reroll (reroll count of this entity as a derivation unit, §6.1); dossier? }.

Identity.dossier? (item 20): the dossier element this entity exists for (§7.1's DossierRef, set by the host door, §11.4) — its element the binding key of §7.7 item 12 (item 74), its version the SettlementForge line the port read; the binding rows themselves are document data (Document.dossier, §2.9), never an entity; persisted identity in the model digest; carried by the entity the element is — its Use (§2.7), a dossier institution's Institution record, and for an element that is neither (a named feature: a bridge, well, gate, way, quay, pin — set by a named-feature claim, §7.7 item 16, item 82) the feature the assignment placed — and moved with it on every re-placement; a building or plot, which only houses a use, never carries it, a building-granularity assignment's placed member included (a rejectSite relocates the use, item 17; J-A20.22); an Assignment keeps its binding in its own Assignment.dossier (§7.7), while a District carries none — its dossier name and identity are reached through the assignment that targets it (factTier; J-A20.24); such an entity is never removed by a map edit, only rejected from a site (§7.7).

FactTier = 'dossier' | 'declared' | 'map' (item 20 (h) (i), item 101 (a)): who holds an attribute's value — the dossier, an author's declaration, or the rules the map derives it by; derived at read by factTier, never stored; the values §9.2's reader, §11's exports (plat:tier) and §11.2's tool API show.

factTier(entity, path): FactTier — pure: reads the entity's dossier ref (Identity.dossier, Assignment.dossier, or a district's through the dossier-backed assignments that target it), the registry's dossier paths, Document.dossier.carried and the lifecycle flags.
Existence ∈ {generated, built, altered, converted, abandoned, decayed, ruined, cleared, reused, demolished}; cleared and reused are item 8's traces (the decline hooks; J-A8.46).

LifecycleFlags { locked; pinned; edited; assigned; lockedPaths? (attribute-level locks, §7.2; absent = the whole entity); editedPaths? (attributes the user set; each implicitly pinned, §7.2) }. Lifecycle { existence; flags; since {epoch, seq} (the event that last changed existence) }.

LifecycleEvent { id; seq (the causing EditEvent's seq; 0 for the generation run); epoch; kind; cause: EditRef | RuleRef | 'generation' (an EditRef reaches its event's dossierChange, §7.1, §7.7 item 13; item 75, so a lifecycle entry and the disruption report say why); detail? {from?; to?; lineageFrom?; lineageTo?; path?; mutation? (index into the causing event's mutations, EditBase.mutations §7.1: the MutationRecord of §4.7 S11); works? {startWeek, durationWeeks} (item 67: the timetable of the Works that carried this change, kept here when the Works record retires, §4.11)} }.

LifecycleEvent.kind ∈ Existence ∪ {lock, unlock, pin, unpin, edit, assign, unassign, reparent, carry, supersede, resurrect, open, close, relocate (item 17: a Use opened, closed or relocated — and a Household moved to another building, §10.3 relocation: §4.7 overflow pass, §2.6 capacity bound, a re-letting; detail.from/to name the buildings), mutate (item 18: a designation mutation; detail.mutation names its record), reject, lapse, place (item 20: a placement rejection, its lapse, a positive placement, §7.7), relet (item 31 rung 1: the household count changed, §4.11; the plan rung goes stale)}.
Slow-change conversions are lifecycle events with cause convert:<kind> (§2.3, citing §2.8). (The typed cause of §2.8 has no such form: see MC-04.)
items.note: Restates MODEL-0152 for the conflict record MC-04.

items.statement: Tombstone { id; kind; lineage; supersededBy?; seq; last: Uint8Array (the compressed last record: orphan reports, resurrection, §6.3) }.

DerivationRecord — the one definition: persisted with plots, blocks and buildings (the kinds whose stage declares it); outside the model digest, inside the records digest (§6.2): { ctx: Hash64 (digest of the context vector read); fields? {prosperity?, density?, greenery?}; band? (the recorded band hysteresis reads — for a plot the band its derivation read; the plot's band memory after it is Plot.fieldBand); allocationRow? (the Allocation row the entity filled, §4.5 S7b); epoch (of the derivation that wrote it); params: Hash64 (digest of the effective parameters read); slices: SliceRef[] (table slices consulted) }.

NamingRecord — persisted with every generated name S13a draws; outside the model digest, inside the records digest (§6.2) and hashed with provenance; handed to a successor with the name (§6.3); dormant while the name is protected: { slices (the naming slices the last draw consulted: grammar rows and weight vectors of the effective naming table and, for every culture or ancestry row that chose a grammar or corpus for it (§10.4), one slice per field of that row the draw read — kind 'row', key '<rowKey>/<field>', hashed over the field's value and, for a corpus field, the named corpus's content hash, §7.6); salt (the naming salt the last draw used: the town salt, or the per-entity salt of the ids-scoped rerollLayer that drew it, §6.3); epoch }.
items.note: Checked: "hashed with provenance" means the provenance digest of §2.9 (provenance, derivation and naming records; locality audit only) — consistent, no conflict.

items.statement: Provenance — derived: rebuilt by every derivation and by replay; stored as columns; never persisted, never in the model digest: { run: StageRunRef (index into the stage-run table {stage, outputVersion, tablePins}, interned once per stage run); attempt (the ladder attempt that committed it, §5.1); rules: SliceRef[] (every table slice consulted, §7.4, §7.6); deps: Handle[] (u32 handles of the entities it read — the locality audit, §7.3) }.
SliceRef { table: TableId; version; kind ∈ {row, weights, bracket, thresholds, match}; key (a row key; '<rowKey>/<field>' for a slice that is one field of a row, §7.6); hash: Hash64 }.

Fact tiers: every attribute of every record is held by one of three tiers, factTier(entity, path) derived at read, never stored: dossier when three things hold — the entity carries a dossier ref (Identity.dossier; on an Assignment its own Assignment.dossier; on a District, for its name and identity, the ref of the dossier-backed neighbourhood assignment targeting it, a district-defining institution's or a naming claim matched to it, §7.7 item 16; J-A20.24), the path belongs to its kind's dossier paths (the registry), and the dossier supplies a value (the carried facts under that ref's binding key hold that field, Document.dossier §2.9; §7.7 item 12); declared when an author's declaration set it (the path is among flags.editedPaths, or it is the existence or position a declaring event that made, placed or shaped the entity pinned — §7.2's declared means held, other attributes re-derive; item 101's R13); map otherwise.

A dossier fact is immutable on the map and changes only by a dossier event; a declared value holds against generation and every re-roll until its author changes it; a map value is the map's to regenerate (§7.7 items 9-11). §7's edit rules refuse an edit of a dossier path as dossier-owned (§7.1); §9.2's reader, §11's exports and the tool API (§11.2) show each value's tier. The tier is not provenance: Provenance says how a value was last derived (never persisted); the tier says who holds it, following from what is persisted.

where: §2.8 no dossier tier without a dossier (item 101)
items.statement: A document with no dossier has no dossier tier: a user's roster, the dossier's stand-in, is declared (item 101's roster).

where: §2.8 one existence state plus orthogonal flags (LC-26)
items.statement: One existence state plus orthogonal flags (LC-26): a pin followed by an assignment leaves the entity both pinned and assigned; no code tests a single state value. Existence moves through: generated (made by the pipeline); built (created by a user or an epoch: build, drawFootprint, drawn features); altered (a structural edit or transformation: split, join, densify, a re-cut by F-REDERIVE); converted (retyped: wall -> ring road, gate -> junction); abandoned, decayed, ruined, cleared and reused (decline and its traces); demolished (removed; the record becomes a tombstone).

Decline and regrowth hooks (owner's decline instruction; item 8; COV-NG-XA36, COV-VG-VN-090 — STAGED-BY-OWNER): one existence state serves every kind; §4.11's ladders map plain names onto it per kind (J-A8.46, J-A8.21): buildings occupied -> vacant (abandoned) -> derelict (decayed, roofless: RoofSpec.kind 'none') -> ruin (ruined) -> robbed or cleared (cleared: a footprint trace — the face persists, heights zeroed in the record, material credited to the MaterialLedger) -> reused (reused: the trace keeps its face and is worked as a garden, orchard or field — Building.reusedAs, drawn as that kind, §8.2 — or a successor raised on the old foundations, Building.predecessor; J-A8.22); walls and gates in use -> neglected (abandoned) -> breached or partly dismantled (decayed) -> superseded by a shorter inner ring (Enceinte.supersededBy — a link, not a state); tunnels in use -> silted (abandoned) -> caved in (decayed) -> collapsed or sealed (ruined with Tunnel.closure; item 11 — condition reading and open column are II.6's); islands SkyIsland.state.

where: §2.8 decline hooks: conversions and live records (J-A8.42)
items.statement: Which conversion (ConversionOp, §4.11) moves which state is a data table, its inverse the undo record's (§7.4); every state exists in the base schema and can be applied by hand (§7.1); a cleared or reused building is a live record at its address until demolish or a successor takes it (J-A8.42), never a tombstone; a ruined building keeps its footprint and heights and draws with the ruin program (§8.2).

where: §2.8 decline hooks: condition, sealed passages, galleries, Works, ruins, lights
items.statement: Building.condition (kept, worn, neglected — item 31's wear) is not an existence state but an attribute of an occupied building; a sealed passage's plots (item 30) enter the ladder as vacant (§4.11); underground galleries and chambers (item 65) flood, collapse or are sealed (closure) through II.6's condition table as tunnels do; the stages a decay or repair Works draws (item 67) are this ladder's drawn stages, no new existence value (§4.11 Works; J-A8.46 stands); a dossier-listed ruin (item 80) is its assignment's state 'ruined' (§7.7) over a building whose existence is ruined — no field of its own on Use or Building; a light (item 68) follows its host: removed with a demolished host, unlit (a reading, never a state) on an abandoned or decayed one; when and where the evolution program applies the ladders is §4.11's.

ElaborationRecord — a sixth part per lazy rung, outside both digests: { entity (the building, or for closeup the district); rung ∈ {closeup, wings, rooms, plan}; state ∈ {absent, current, stale, edited}; inputs: Hash64 (digest of the rung's recorded inputs — for a building: its leaf digest (wings, heights, entrances, basement, class, use, assignment, sub-locations, the wings' spans), the leaf digest of each spanned Passage (its face's ring), the occupants' band (Plot.fieldBand) and value (at §7.2's τ), the accesses opening in its basement (item 64), its running Works' stage at the drawn week (item 67 (j)), the households housed in address order (item 28 (f)), and the slices); slices: SliceRef[] (programme, pattern, furniture and interior-ladder rows; §7.6 invalidates by slice); epoch; since {epoch, seq} } — no reroll here: a rung's reroll count is what the log's regenerate events with rung give it (§6.1, §7.1). A building carries one per lazily derived rung (wings, rooms, plan) and at stage 2 a district one for its close-up (closeup, II.4).

absent: never derived, or evicted — nothing lost, a rung is a pure function; current: the cached result's input digest equals the digest of the inputs now; stale: an input changed (a designation, an assignment, the band, the storeys, the wing rings or a spanned passage's face, the households, a concealed use, an access into its basement, its Works' stage, a slice, a dossier event of items 18, 22 or 31) — marked by the batch that changed it, with no derivation run; edited: a stored composition with plan events in the log. The state is recomputed from inputs against the current digest at load and after every batch touching the entity.

The elaboration record and the cached result live in the document's non-canonical blocks (§2.9) — outside the model digest and outside the records digest — because a click logs nothing and writes nothing a replay must reproduce (§6.2, §6.5 (9)); what a click derives enters a digest only when an edit stores it (§2.6).

History lives outside the entity (SCL-20): the document keeps one lifecycle event block keyed by id and ordered by seq (each entry's seq the causing event's; 0 for the generation run); an entity holds only its Lifecycle. The block is not append-only (J-DET-33): an undo removes the entries whose seq is its target's; a redo re-inserts them in seq order (the re-applied target's events cite the target's seq, §7.4); neither writes an entry of its own — so the block is always the block of the log with its undone pairs left out (the identity unshared-document truncation relies on, §7.4, §6.5 (9)).

Demolished and superseded entities move to the archive as tombstones: out of the working set, spatial indexes and display list; their ids and supersededBy links stay in the identity subtree of the model digest (§6.2) so an id is never minted twice (§6.3); a tombstone carries its causing event's seq, so an undo returns its target's tombstones to live and a redo archives them again.

where: §2.8 history growth budget and fallback (§13.2 M4 epoch test)
items.statement: Growth budget: the working set grows only with live entities; the document grows by at most the bytes of new or changed records plus 64 B per lifecycle event (M4 epoch test: §13.2). Pre-decided fallback: the archive and the lifecycle event block are held compressed in memory and decompressed only for an orphan report, a resurrection or an export — output-neutral.

Derivation records (LC-12): a plot, block or building persists its derivation inputs (context and parameter digests, field samples, band, table slices consulted) so Regenerate (keep settings) reproduces it from what it was made from across saves, epochs and field edits elsewhere (§7.3 item 5); excluded from the model digest (hashed with provenance and in the records digest); every derivation changing the entity's leaf digest (§6.2) rewrites it; a re-derivation reproducing the leaf digest exactly keeps the old record, as the dependency-graph route (which never touches it) does — so the record never depends on which route re-derived the entity (§7.3 items 6-7).

Three band memories, kept apart: DerivationRecord.band — the band the last derivation read, in the records digest, rewritten by every derivation changing the leaf; Plot.builtBand — the band the stock was built for, in the model digest, rewritten only by rung-3 events and the redevelopment-class edits J-A31.44 lists (§4.11); Plot.fieldBand — the band the plot's occupants live at, in the model digest, set by every derivation reading the current field and re-banded after S6 at every epoch, so the interior's hysteresis follows the field (J-A28.29).

A document written before these attributes existed gets builtBand and fieldBand from DerivationRecord.band and builtProsperity from the recorded sample (§7.5). A plot's record may also cite the designation-template and compatibility slices item 18's mutator read (slices).

Naming records: every time S13a draws a generated name it writes the name's NamingRecord (the naming slices consulted and the salt used); it travels with the name when the address passes to a successor (§6.3), is rewritten by every draw, and is what §6.3's draw case (4) and §7.6's invalidation by slice compare with current effective slices to find names whose naming inputs changed; persisted, like a derivation record and unlike provenance, so a rebased document (whose provenance no replay can rebuild) still knows which names drew from a changed grammar row or corpus (J-DET-41).

Naming records are stored as offsets into the deduplicated slice-reference pool: ≈ 4-8 slices per name, ≈ 20-40 B raw per name, ≈ 0.1 MB raw for the ≈ 3,500 names of a CITY before compression, counted in §2.9's per-building document budget.

A protected name keeps its record dormant (J-DET-46): while protected — a setAttr on it, a lock on its path (a whole-entity lock included) or an assignment that sets it (§7.7) — its record stays in place and no draw case reads, compares or rewrites it; it still travels with the address to a successor. The event ending the protection returns the name to unedited with the record of its last draw and runs §6.3's case (4), its undo record keeping the former name and record. An entity whose name was never drawn has no record and nothing to re-draw.

Provenance is compact and outside the digest (LC-25, SCL-5): version stamps live once in the stage-run table; rules are offsets into a deduplicated slice-reference pool; deps are u32 handles into a pool; all stored as struct-of-arrays columns per kind (target <= 64 B per entity at CITY, measured at M1 with §12's entity-memory test; pre-decided fallback: deps recorded per derivation unit — per block, per plot — instead of per entity, making the audit coarser, never unsound). Provenance, derivation records and naming records share the provenance digest, used only by the locality audit (§2.9 Canonical form and digests; §6.2).

Rules cite slices, not rows (LC-21): a derivation records every table slice consulted by the slice's hash — the whole weight vector for a weighted draw or deck, both bracketing rows for an interpolated rule, the threshold set for a band lookup, the row for a direct lookup (a naming draw: one slice per culture or ancestry field it read, §7.6), and the table's match predicate set for a rule selecting rows by predicate; §7.6 invalidates on slice-hash change.

The entity registry (@plat/model) declares per entity type: generator stage and lineage unit (§6.3); anchor encoding, hysteresis radius and class family (§6.3); digest encoding (§6.2); invariant scopes (§5.3); renderer symbols per LOD; export mapping per format; persistence encoding (§2.9), the naming record included for a named kind; pick behaviour; edit kinds with their undo path and lifecycle row (§7.1, §7.4); migration hooks (§7.5); dossier paths (item 20 (h)); and closure generators per edit kind — the pieces an edit's missing prerequisites need, in dependency order (§7.3 item 9; item 66). Its completeness test (a CI test fails when a type is missing from any of those paths) is §13.2's (O11 a; §7.1, owner amendment 5).

Registry additions (amendments of 2026-09-25): Use (§2.7; lineage unit the creating event or the epoch's use step, anchor the plot's address and role); Passage (§2.5); MaterialLedger (§2.7, one per document); Rejection (declared with its mechanism in §7.7: model data in the digest keyed by element and site, with its lapse and migration hook); AccessPoint (II.7.4); the underground plots' and buildings' fields (II.7.3); the plan's Room with its unit (§2.6; anchored by its centroid within its wing); a building's Entrance and Basement sub-records and its base wings' spans (§2.6); a site-plan slot's unhoused (§2.5); the plot's builtBand, builtProsperity and fieldBand with their migration hook (§7.5); the tunnel's navigable, headroomCm and closure (§2.7); the elaboration record's cache path (§2.9); each enters §13.2's path-completeness test, and every new attribute has its edit kind or is declared derived (§7.1).

Registry additions (items 63-88, 101): Works (lineage unit its target's lineage with its start week, §6.3; works draws keyed as §6.1; edit kinds startWorks, cancelWorks, setAttr on start and duration; retired by an epoch); LightSource (anchor its host's address, rule row and ordinal; placeLight, setAttr, delete, lock); UndergroundSystem, Gallery, Chamber, UndergroundLink (keyed in their system's part; drawTunnel with a system, drawChamber, addLink, setAttr, delete, the closure conversions; Document.nextUndergroundPart their part counter); staged ConditionOverlay, DepositSite, PowerRelation (anchor their binding key; dossier facts with no map edit kind; absent = empty); Use.concealment, front, knownTo and Institution.concealment, powers (setAttr, dossier-owned where the dossier set them); Use.concealmentSource (written with concealment; no edit kind); Building.concealed and works (derived links); Room.concealed and Entrance.concealed (each written by its own deriver: plan rung, deriveEntrances); Basement.kind crawl; Plot.tenure (derived, setAttr an override; a plot without it derives it at first load, §7.5); District.identity (setAttr an override), pressure and nameHistory (written by epochs and renames only), character and bandRange (derived, no edit kind), parent and outskirts (written by the undercity's stage); Pin.light and the notice pin; RegionGroup (§9.1: made by group, renamed by setAttr, removed by delete); LabelEntity.displayText (§9.1: setAttr, cleared by revert; the map's display over a name, never a dossier path); Faction.kind military and arcane; Terrain.geology (S1's; setAttr an override, §7.1 terrain row); AccessPoint state, knownTo, source (II.7.4; setAttr on the first two); item 101's sugar events (placeGate, quarter, roster, group, §7.1) listed with the kinds their expansions make, so the completeness test reaches them.

Dossier paths: the registry names per kind the attribute paths a dossier may own, each with the carried field that supplies it; no other path is ever dossier: Institution name, kind, knownTo, concealment, powers (the powers' controlled-institution lists, item 79); a dossier element's Use — cls (from the element's kind by the port's class rows, §7.7 item 12), concealment, front, knownTo; an Assignment's state, name, knownTo, concealment, front (§7.7; items 30, 63, 80); a District's name from a matched naming claim (item 82) and identity from a district-defining institution or a claim's kind (item 72), each under the ref of the assignment targeting the district; a named feature's name (bridge, well, gate, way, quay, pin; item 82); every attribute the port writes on the staged ConditionOverlay, DepositSite, PowerRelation and dossier-backed Person (item 88).
The settlement's own facts — its name, tier word and population — and the typed circumstance slices are carried in Document.dossier and Recipe.circumstances and read there (§7.7), on no entity.

A document is a base plus an ordered log: the base is either the canonical recipe (the town replays from its seed) or, after a rebase, a materialised state; the log is every event since creation in seq order. Everything else in the file is the canonical style state, input recorded for replay (setting-pack content, host outputs), a verified cache, or per-user state.
Document { docId; schemaVersion; outputVersion; base; log; nextSeq; nextUndergroundPart; packs; hostContent; dossier?; style; model?; view?; derived?; undo?; elaborations? }.
docId: Uuid minted at creation by @plat/api (outside the model packages); kept on save; re-minted on clone and save-as (§6.3).
schemaVersion: the file format (§7.5); outputVersion: the model packages whose output this document replays under (§6.4).
log: EditEvent[] — the single source of truth for every edit, lock, assignment, table edit, epoch, rebase, upgrade, undo and redo (§7.1, §7.4); a rebase never removes events.
nextSeq: the seq the next event takes; never decreases — also when an unshared document truncates an undone pair (§7.4).

nextUndergroundPart (item 65): the arena part the next underground system takes (II.7.6; 1 at creation, part 0 being the sewer's); never decreases, as nextSeq — an undone or truncated system's number stays spent, so no number is reused (§3.4); the system's record stores it (UndergroundSystem.part), as does its address's under<n>/ prefix, so an event creating a system after generation carries the number in the address it records (a closure's ClosureRecord.created, §7.3 item 9; a raiseGrade conversion's buried system, II.7.6) and a replay reads it there, never recomputes it; systems made at generation take theirs in II.7.6's stage order.

packs: PackData[] — the content of every non-shipped pack of the pack set and of every pack a truncated event held on a saved redo stack names (a selected user corpus is one) — canonical, outside the model digest.
hostContent: HostContent[] — outputs of host-registered providers keyed for replay (§6.5, §11.4) — canonical, outside the model digest.

dossier?: { binding: DossierBinding; carried: CarriedFacts } (items 20 (h) (v), 74, 87): the dossier block (types §7.7 item 12's) — canonical, outside the model digest like hostContent; absent without a dossier.
style: StyleState — sheet id@version (a non-shipped sheet's content included), style row operations, ground-cover regions — canonical, outside the model digest.
model?: Snapshot — the materialised model at the log head: a cache checked against its own model and records digests and verified by replay (load step 3); always written on save.
view?: ViewState — per-user and shared view keys, the stored authoring session included — never in a digest.

derived? { report: GenerationReport; stats: StatisticsRecord; epochs: EpochRecord[]; locks; orphans: OrphanRecord[]; features: Features (II.7.4: resolved feature set — sewers by tier; underground while any system exists, items 65-66 — recomputed on load with the report; every dependant reads it from the model, never from a layer's visibility, item 14); tradeFlow?: TradeFlow (item 77: derived trade flow, §4.3 — recomputed at creation, at each epoch and on load; never canonical); elaborations: ElaborationRecord[] (one per entity and lazy rung, derived from the cache against current digests, item 28) } — caches rebuilt from base + log; never canonical.

undo?: UndoRecord[] — the session's undo records carried across a reload (cap §7.4), with the truncated targets its redo stack holds; never canonical. elaborations?: ElaborationChunk[] — the elaboration cache kept across zoom-outs and sessions so "once generated it is saved" holds without storing derived rungs in the model (item 28); never canonical.

Base = {kind 'recipe'; recipe} (replay = G(outputVersion, recipe), then fold the log) | {kind 'rebased'; recipe; state: Snapshot; seq; reason: RebaseReason} (replay starts from state — checked against its root of record, load step 3 — and folds events after seq (= the rebase event's at, §7.1); a rebase event is a no-op in the fold of a client whose base it already is (a bridged client that holds another base installs it, load step 4); the town is not seed-reproducible before seq).
Seed = u32, 0 .. 2^32 - 1: records write it as its decimal string (§13.3), permalinks in base 36 (§6.4); the D-5 panel seeds are H32 values (§13.6 (2)).
Recipe.seed: for a dossier-bound document the port's one-way derivation from the dossier's own seed (§14; item 85) — never the host's seed itself.

Recipe — the canonical recipe: every model-affecting input and nothing else (§6.2; LC-15): { seed; rung: Rung; tablePins: Record<TableId, string>; packs [{id (a selected user corpus: 'user:<content hash, base 32>'); version; hash: Hash128 (of the pack's canonical JSON); shipped (informative only: a load resolves each pack by hash, the link rule reads the link's output version (§6.4), an upgrade to a version that stops shipping it copies its content into packs (§7.5 (2)); always false for a user corpus)}] (setting packs and selected user corpora, §7.6, §10.4); params: ParamDelta (the full effective delta over the pinned shipped defaults — pack, preset, user-global and document overrides folded in at creation, §7.6); presetId? (provenance only); intent: Intent (§7.7 layer 1's outcome targets); districtIntent: DistrictIntent[] (§7.7 layer 2: per-district intent — town-wide default and each district's override; the input a district is generated from, never item 72's derived CharacterVector, J-A72.21, J-A72.41); history?: HistoryHint (item 88; staged, absent in the base); circumstances?: CircumstanceTimeline (schedules epoch events the app proposes; never applied except through epoch events, §7.1); entryMode ∈ {contentFirst, layoutFirst} (S10b's entry point, §4.7 — a recipe field, not session state, LC-30); salts: Record<RerollableConcern, number> }.

Recipe.salts: initial salts of the rerollable concerns only (normally 0), keyed by §6.1's registry-generated type; the schema refuses any other key, so a geometry concern can never carry a salt; rerollLayer events in the log advance them (§6.1).

PackData { id; version; hash: Hash128; author; content: SettingPack (§10.4, schema-validated) }. HostContent { provider; version; inputHash: Hash128; output } — read on replay instead of calling the host (§11.4).

Snapshot { seq (the log head it materialises); chunks: ChunkRef[] (content-addressed); digest: Hash128 (the model's Merkle root, §6.2 — recomputed from the decoded state at every in-window load (step 3) under the model packages of the output version that recorded it, and compared); recordsDigest: Hash128 (root of the records tree over the persisted derivation and naming records, §6.2 — recomputed at every in-window load and by the verification replay, and compared) }.

ElaborationChunk { entity; rung; inputs: Hash64; hash: Hash128; bytes } (item 28 (c)): the elaboration cache — a derived Composition, Plan or close-up, or one memoised step of a re-cut chain (§2.6), keyed by (entity, rung, inputs digest); content-addressed and non-canonical: checked by hash, dropped on mismatch or eviction (§12.8), never a base, never in a digest (§6.2).

ChunkRef { block ∈ {geometry, entities, archive, history, fields}; partition (PlatKey and 'L0-1' (the level-<= 1 routes) or a static-index partition (§3.3) — or under the size fallback a block group — or 'town'); hash: Hash128 }.
ViewState { keys: Record<string, {value; lamport; session}> } — the keys of "View state", session included; each key last-writer-wins by (Lamport counter, session id).

EpochRecord { epoch; seq; inputs: EpochInputs; postDigest: Hash128 } — derived from the log's epoch events (§7.1); its week is inputs.week (§4.11). The document's current week is derived — the week of the last folded event that carries one (§4.11's clock) — never a stored counter; the week view key reads it.
RebaseReason ∈ {keptSnapshot, drawnConstraintsRebuilt, frozenImport}; keeping the old model at an upgrade needs no rebase: the document stays at its own output version (§7.5), so no reason names it.

UndoRecord { session; of (the seq of the event it undoes); record: Uint8Array (its §7.4 undo record, compressed); redo? (an unshared document's truncated target held on this session's redo stack, §7.4: the event itself with its original seq, so a redo after a reload re-appends it; every pack it names stays in packs while it is held) }.

One source of truth (LC-24): locks, assignments, table and preset edits (including host-supplied tables, arriving as editTable / editPreset / setStyle events whose content is copied into the log with provenance host), epochs, undo and redo exist only as log events; their current effect lives in the entity records (flags, attributes) and in derived caches rebuilt from the base and the log. The blueprint's own assignments and edits enter as the log's first events (§7.7).

Dossier events (items 20, 22 and 73-75) enter the log through the host door (§11.4) — produced by the dossier port (§14) — with author 'host', EditBase.dossier and EditBase.dossierChange set, in the host's order, so the log is the ordered dossier history the map is a function of (§6.2); every map edit lives in the log, never in the dossier; the module never writes the dossier (§11.3); the report, statistics and timings are §5.4's.
A rebase never deletes events: the events before it stay in the log as history and as the rebase's undo path (§7.4), and the fold skips them while the base is the rebased state.

Document.dossier holds what the map knows of its dossier: the binding rows (each dossier key bound to the address that carries its Identity.dossier), the facts carried under those keys, their hash, and every absorbed state's hash (DossierBinding, CarriedFacts, declared with their mechanism in §7.7 item 12). Canonical; the model digest never hashes it (as hostContent); the port writes it at creation and at each absorb; the fold rebuilds it from the log's dossier events; a load checks the stored block against that rebuild (§6.2, §7.5). It is what factTier reads, what an incoming dossier is diffed against (§7.7 item 1) and where a host's undo finds the earlier state it converges to (absorbed, §7.7 item 5); counted beside the host content, outside the per-building budget; a document with no dossier has none.

The skeleton file (item 101): a document's declared subset as a file of its own — the ordered declarations, the creation prefix's and every event whose entities factTier reads declared, with the recipe's seed, rung and pins — exported from any document and imported as a new document's creation prefix (§7.7's one path; its format §11.1's, its round trip §6.5 (9)'s).

Every setting pack is identified by id, version and content hash. The pack set is every pack the base recipe's packs names or that the value of any adjust of the pack list in the log (param 'packs', §7.6) names — an undone, superseded or deselected selection included (its event stays in the log and every replay folds it).

At creation, or when an adjust adds a pack (§7.6), the content of every pack of the pack set not in the output version's shipped set is copied into packs and stays while the base recipe or any event of the log names the pack, or a truncated event held on a saved redo stack (UndoRecord.redo, §7.4) does; it leaves packs at the next save only once none names it (a truncation removed the last logged event naming it, and the redo entry holding it was cleared by a new event from its session or left the undo cap). A pack a new output version stops shipping is copied into packs by the upgrade (§7.5 (2)).

A user-uploaded corpus is a pack like any other (§10.4): selecting it wherever a corpus is chosen is an adjust of the recipe's pack list (§7.6) entering {id 'user:<content hash, base 32>', version '1', hash, shipped false} with its content in packs — the corpus and the keyed row operation binding it to the chosen culture or ancestry row, so the binding is part of its content hash; deselecting it is a second adjust, and its content stays saved because the first still names it, so a replay always resolves it and a town that selected a user corpus can never emit a link that replays with other names (§6.4); an uploaded corpus outside the pack set is not a model input and is not saved. A host provider's outputs are copied into hostContent as produced (§11.4).

On load each pack of the pack set is resolved by hash, first from packs, then from the library's shipped packs; a missing pack or hash mismatch opens the document read-only with a message naming the pack, never a replay with other content — so a document replays on a machine having neither the pack nor the host.

Pack data and host content are counted outside the per-building budget and capped at 2 MB gzipped together: a pack (a user corpus included) that would pass the cap is refused when added, with a message; a host provider's output that would pass it is refused at the provider call (nothing recorded in hostContent) and the requesting edit returns an F-EDIT conflict (§5.2) naming the provider and the size — an ApplyResult conflict through the API and, for an edit over the bridge, doc.rejected {reason 'invalid', conflicts} (§11.2, §11.3) — so nothing is ever committed with content a replay could not read.

Load step 1: a schemaVersion newer than the library's opens read-only with a message (view and export only); a document whose canonical form fails its schema (a Recipe.salts key that is not a rerollable concern among them) opens read-only with a message naming the field, never replayed.

Load step 2: an outputVersion outside the retention window (§6.4) opens as a frozen view from model (view and export); the one edit offered is rebase (reason frozenImport), after which the document edits under the current version and records it is not seed-reproducible before the rebase. A frozen view is never checked against its recorded model root (J-DET-44) — that root was computed by its own output version's packages (leaf encoding, field drivers) the browser no longer holds; the view checks each chunk against its content hash (bytes alone) and is labelled "made with o<k>; not verified by this version" beside the CLI command that replays and checks it under its own output version (§6.4).

A chunk whose bytes miss their content hash is reported as damage ("part of the saved copy is damaged"), its partitions drawn marked, and the frozenImport rebase is refused (a damaged copy is never a base), with the same CLI command.

The frozenImport rebase decodes the state under the current version (fields recomputed from their drivers and the stroke list, never from the Uint8 display copy), checks its records root against model.recordsDigest (records' encoding is the file schema's, so any version can check it, §6.2; a mismatch refuses the rebase as damage), records the model root the current version computes as its stateDigest with version = the current output version (§7.1), and re-draws the names whose naming inputs changed as §7.4's rebase row states; it resolves the pack set as a load does, and a pack neither packs nor the current version's shipped packs hold refuses the rebase with a message naming the pack and the CLI command that installs the document's own output version, copies the pack's content into packs (the cap applies) and rebases.

where: §2.9 load step 2 no model outside window (§6.4)
items.statement: A document without model outside the window (only the CLI writes one) cannot be shown as a frozen view: the app says so and shows the CLI command that replays it under its own output version (§6.4), and offers to open its recipe under the current version as a new document with §6.4's notice.

Load step 3: otherwise the document's output version is the current one or a retained N-1 or N-2 (§6.4), and everything below runs under that version's model packages — its decoder, field drivers and digest leaf encoding, the ones that recorded the roots it checks.

Decode and check: the load decodes model — each chunk checked against its content hash, the arena rebuilt (§3.9), the entity columns decoded, the fields recomputed from their drivers and the stroke list — and displays it at once; before the decoded state accepts its first edit it recomputes its digest tree (every leaf and interior node of §6.2, one full recomputation within §6.2's bar) and compares its root with model.digest, and in the same pass builds the records tree over the decoded derivation and naming records and compares its root with model.recordsDigest; the trees built are the working state's maintained trees from then on (every edit updates them at commit, §6.2 Maintenance).

Corrupt cache: a model root or records root that differs, or a chunk whose bytes miss their content hash, is a corrupt cache: the report says so ("the saved copy of this town does not match its own fingerprint; it is being rebuilt from its recipe and edits"), the decoded picture stays on screen read-only and marked damaged, and the document loads by replay (step 5), the replay's state becoming the working state at the log head; a corrupt cache is never verified, never a base and never offered as the saved town.

A rebased document's base.state is checked when a replay starts from it: its records root against base.state.recordsDigest, and its model root (computed under the replay's packages) against its root of record for that output version — the stateDigest of the rebase that installed it when that event's version is the replay's, else the baseDigest of the later upgrade whose to is (every upgrade of a rebased document records one, §7.5 (2)). The document's output version is always its latest rebase's version or its latest upgrade's to, so an ordinary load always finds a root of record, and an upgrade's undo replaying under from finds the one recorded before it (a base kept under o5 and upgraded to o6 is checked under o6 against o6's root at the upgrade). A mismatch opens the document read-only with a message (no replay can rebuild a state that is not seed-reproducible).

On a matching root the decoded model is at once the working state: the user edits immediately, each edit dry-run, logged and applied as in a verified session at §12.6's edit cost — no edit waits. In parallel a verification replay folds (base, log) up to h0 (the log head model materialises, model.seq) in replay mode (every model stage at its event's log position exactly as in the session, S13a's scoped delta included; only view stages S14 and S13b suppressed, §7.3) and compares its model and records roots at h0 with model.digest and model.recordsDigest. It runs in a pool worker on its own arena with its per-district stages at pool size 0 on that worker (same overlay-and-merge path, identical digests by construction, §3.3 pool step 5; each freeze first rebuilding the partitions its folded edits left dirty, §3.3 pool step 1), so no copy is frozen while it runs and §12.8 counts the replay's model in place of the pool's frozen copies; every edit meanwhile runs its per-district stages (S10, S10b, S11, S12b) in the generation worker by the pool-size-0 path; an edit spanning several districts costs its single-worker figure (§12.4) until verification ends. With pool size 0 the replay runs in the generation worker on its own arena and yields to each user edit at its next batch boundary (J-I14).

Edits held for provenance: editTable and editPreset, whose invalidation reads recorded slices (§7.6), need provenance, which only the replay rebuilds: they are held until the replay reaches h0 and hands its provenance to the working state (for every entity the edits made meanwhile did not re-derive), and every event after a held one waits behind it, keeping log order. An Adjust made meanwhile uses tree scoping, which §7.3 items 6-7 prove output-identical to the dependency-graph route.

The working state is verified only when both model roots equal model.digest and both records roots equal model.recordsDigest — the decoded state's (checked before its first edit, or under §6.2 (iii)) and the replay's at h0; the edits made meanwhile are then verified with it, being applied to a state proven equal to the replay's at h0.

Records mismatch (J-DET-52): when the replay's model root at h0 equals model.digest while its records root does not (a writer stored a wrong derivation or naming record and hashed what it wrote), no model changes and nothing is asked: the replay's state at h0, records included, replaces the working state, and every event logged after h0 is re-applied in log order as "take the replayed town" does (step 4), since an edit made meanwhile may have read a wrong record (Regenerate (keep) reads derivation records; case (4) naming records and their salts, §6.3); fates and renames recomputed and differences reported; the report says "the saved copy's derivation or naming records differed from what its recipe gives and were rebuilt", and the working state is then verified.

The user may end the wait by choosing "trust the saved town", keeping the saved town as in step 4; offered only once the decoded state's own model and records roots have matched; when that is and what waits for the recomputation meanwhile is §6.2 (iii)'s.

Open-to-editable (from the file's bytes in memory to the working state accepting its first edit) <= the time §12.5's law gives to generate a town of the document's building count with the pool, T(B) (at CITY <= 60 ms + 60 µs x B: 330-420 ms at the default request), so opening a saved town is never slower than generating it; on the reference 300-edit CITY document with pool size >= 1, an edit made 100 ms after the state becomes editable applies within its §12.6 cost + 10 ms; with pool size 0 within its cost + the longest replay batch at the rung (reported); the picture is on screen before the state is editable (S14 from the decoded model). Measured at M2a (METROPOLIS at M2b).

Pre-decided fallbacks: if the digest recomputation passes §6.2's bar it leaves the edit path by §6.2 (iii); if open-to-editable still passes T(B), the kernel rebuilds each L2-L4 static index partition at the first query reading it instead of at load (§3.9) — output-neutral since every query result is sorted by its canonical key (§3.3) — and if the bar still fails it is restated at the measured value as a declared budget amendment in the release notes and judgment table, reported for the owner's veto, the picture still appearing at once; if the pool-size->=1 edit bar fails for CPU contention, the verification replay pauses while an edit is applied and while the user has edited within the last 2 s, then resumes — scheduling only, never a model change.
The load-verification fixtures (corrupt snapshots, a forced §6.2 (iii), an altered naming record) are §13.2's.

Load step 4: a mismatch is never silent and is resolved once by the user's choice (J-DET-38). Keep the saved town (offered only once the saved copy's own roots matched): the base becomes the rebased state model at h0 (Base.seq = h0) and a rebase event with at = h0, stateDigest = model.digest and version = the document's output version (reason keptSnapshot) is appended at the head (EditEngine.rebase(doc, 'keptSnapshot', h0), §14); edits made during verification stand. Take the replayed town: the replay's state at h0 (arena and entity columns transferred to the generation worker) replaces model, and every event after h0 is re-applied in log order through the ordinary fold; confirmed fates recomputed, differences reported (§7.3 item 4), undo records rebuilt. Either way the document is consistent, the next load does not report it again, and undo below a rebase uses the rebased state, never a replay from the seed.
A rebase fills in, from the rebased state, the derivation record of every entity of a kind that declares one (§2.8) and lacks it, so Regenerate (keep settings) stays defined for every such entity.

In a document attached to a host bridge (J-DET-42) the policy (which client may keep the saved town, what every other client does, reports, records and keeps meanwhile) is §11.3's (Bridged load verification); the install mechanics: a client receiving a rebase with reason keptSnapshot whose at lies behind its log head and whose stateDigest differs from its own root at at installs that base — decodes model from the doc.load bytes it kept (§11.3), checks it as in step 3, makes it the rebased base (Base.seq = at), re-applies every event after at through the ordinary fold (fates recomputed, differences reported §7.3 item 4, undo records rebuilt) and tells its user the owner kept the saved town. A client whose verification is still running stops it; a client whose root at at equals the stateDigest changes nothing; any other rebase whose at lies behind the head (possible only in a hand-built log) is a reported no-op identically everywhere.

A client loading a document whose log already holds a keptSnapshot rebase with at = model.seq and stateDigest = model.digest (the host kept serving bytes from before the owner's choice) takes model as that rebased base after step 3's check, without a verification replay and without asking (the owner has chosen); the next owner save writes the base in its rebased form — so every client of a bridged document reaches the owner's state, as §11.3's convergence rule requires.
The mismatch fixtures are §13.2's, and §11.3's convergence test includes a forced mismatch settled by an owner's keep.

Load step 5: a document without model inside the window loads by replay, as does a corrupt cache (step 3); model is a cache, never the only copy of anything. So does a document of the running output version written by M1's generated-town format before the records digest existed (§16): nothing recorded a records root, so the schema transform adding recordsDigest (§7.5) drops its model and the load regenerates the town from its recipe and empty log, never reporting it verified — a preview file (§13.3) loses nothing (J-I19). M1's reader never root-checks a document of another output version: it opens as step 2's frozen view (§16 M1).

Geometry is stored once: per arena (PlatKey) every boundary (shore, kerb, plot line, party wall) is written once with its birth level; faces, twins and parents are rebuilt on load (§3.9); every level is present, so a frozen view needs no pipeline code of its own version. Entities are stored as columns (identity, lifecycle, attributes, derivation records and naming records, §2.8); provenance is not stored — verification replays rebuild it.

The prosperity, density and greenery fields are not stored at full resolution: an editable document recomputes them from their drivers and the stroke list on load (§4.5, §7.2); the snapshot carries only a Uint8 copy of each field at 32 m (≈ 40 KB at CITY), used for thematic display if the document is ever opened as a frozen view. Neither digest tree is stored: the snapshot holds the two roots (digest, recordsDigest), and the load recomputes both trees (step 3).

Content-addressed chunks, one copy of a rebased state (J-DET-36, J-DET-19): a snapshot is serialised as chunks keyed by 128-bit content hash, written once in the container however many snapshots reference it. Geometry chunks — one per arena for its level-<= 1 routes and one per static-index partition (one per district plus one outside districts, §3.3; the same units as §7.4's copy-on-write checkpoints) — are laid out by §3.9 (what each holds, how a chunk names geometry another holds by lattice point, which edits rewrite which chunks). Entity columns are chunked per partition; archive, lifecycle history and field cache are town chunks. A rebased document's model shares every unchanged chunk with base.state: while the post-rebase log is empty model is only a chunk list naming base.state's chunks (same digest); after edits only the chunks those edits rewrote are stored twice.

Size budget: TOWN <= 0.6 MB, CITY <= 3 MB, METROPOLIS <= 8 MB gzipped, and <= 320 B per building at CITY, counted over the unique chunks plus the manifest; measured against FTG's 593 KB for 2,798 buildings with their population (≈ 212 B per building; PLAT also stores plots, yards, heights, lifecycle and naming records, and derives people); pack data, host content and the dossier block counted separately. This section holds the document budget (§12 carries memory, not the document).
Measurement: a document-size test per rung in B-CITY-lite at M1, and at M2a one on a CITY document rebased by keeping the saved town, after 20 edits (<= 1.25 x the unrebased document; §16).

Pre-decided fallback if CITY exceeds 320 B per building: the vertex stream switches to second-order (predictive) delta coding — each vertex stored as its difference from the straight-line continuation of the previous two along its first edge — with x and y in separate streams; lossless and output-neutral, no golden moves. If the rebased document exceeds 1.25 x: L2-L4 geometry and entity chunks are cut per block group instead of per district (a district's blocks grouped by the 200 m world-grid cell holding each block's lowest-leftmost vertex, so an edit rewrites only the groups it touched) and the test re-runs; if the ratio still exceeds 1.25 x, the bar is restated at the measured ratio as a declared budget amendment in the release notes and judgment table, reported for the owner's veto, while CITY <= 3 MB stays the hard bar for rebased documents too; both steps output-neutral (chunking changes bytes on disk, never the model or its digest).

Canonical format: a .plat container = a JSON manifest (schema-validated, human-diffable: versions, docId, nextSeq, base recipe, log, pack data, host content, style, the snapshot chunk lists) + binary blocks (the chunks by hash) as typed arrays.

Saving from the app or the API always writes model; only the CLI's --recipe-only export writes a document without it (test fixtures and files made from links), and it refuses a rebased base, whose state its recipe cannot rebuild.
The compact twin for embeds is §11.1's — the same schema in world coordinates, round-tripping exactly (O11 c); exports are views (§11) and carry address ids plus a supersedes table (§6.3).

The canonical document is docId, schemaVersion, outputVersion, nextSeq, nextUndergroundPart, base, log, packs, hostContent, dossier (when present), style and model (when present); view, derived and undo are never canonical.
items.note: elaborations (Document.elaborations) is not listed among canonical or non-canonical fields here although the code comment says "never canonical"; minor omission.

items.statement: Four digests: the model digest and the records digest (§6.2); the provenance digest (provenance, derivation records and naming records, §2.8 — the locality audit only); and the document digest (over the canonical bytes — save -> load -> save identity). The bridge's concurrency token logHead is §11.3's.

View state (FTG-12, LC-16): time, location, favourites, notes and public notes, view pins, layer choices, stylePreset (a per-viewer preset that never writes setStyle, §11.3), elaborate (click or view: when a lazy rung is derived, never what — §4.1, item 28; click by default), storey (the storey the building band draws; default §8.5's, J-A28.82), depthBand (the underground depth band the cut-away draws; default §8.4's, J-A12.81), plotsOnly (the cadastral plots-only view; §8.5, item 28), knowledge (item 30: {tier public|local|secret; places} — the viewer's tier and learned places, admitted by §9.2's table in the label policy, the reader §11.2 and every picture and interchange export §11.1; default by role and who may set it §11.3's, J-A30.82; every golden taken at tier public with no places), week (item 67: the week drawn — default the document's current week; a host sets its campaign week there, a user scrubs it, §4.11 Works (9)), light (item 68: day|night|time, default day; time follows the time key's hour through the path sun), sunMode (cursor|fixed|path, default cursor where a pointer exists), sunHeight (s >= 1, default 1: the cursor sun over the pointer at 1, receding toward a near-parallel sun as it rises, §8.4 (d)), handLantern (underground only; off by default), underlay (item 101: an image the viewer traces over — held by the viewer's app, never embedded in the canonical document; opacity 0-1 default 0.5; its frame a world-cm affine placement; never exported, never read by the model; §9.5 draws it), season, weather, frame, map rotation, compass, legend and emblem settings, exportAnchor (§11.1), and the people a user has opened — all in view, outside every digest.

The pointer's position is a transient input, never a view key, never stored, logged or shared (§8.4); the document's style stays canonical; each view key is last-writer-wins by (Lamport counter, session id), so a viewer never writes the model. The key session holds an unshared document's authoring session (§7.4 Sessions); a client attached to a host bridge takes its session from doc.load instead and never writes this key (§11.3).
Permalinks are §6.4; migrations §7.5; the edit log's replay semantics, undo and redo §7.4; the export -> import -> export round trip over the canonical form is a hard test (§13.2).

The plat: the cadastral plan of plots, the single spatial truth; stored as one vertex-and-half-edge arena per PlatKey (layer, part) — the ground, each underground part, each sky island; a part is PlatKey.part (underground 0 = sewer network; sky 1-3 = islands).
Address id (kind:token, arena-prefixed off the ground) — what everything points at; distinct from the lineage key (LineageHash, keying random streams) and from the in-memory interned u32 handle.

Kernel vocabulary of refinement: Steiner vertex (a level-n vertex splitThrough inserts on a coarser edge); promotion (a finer vertex's birth level lowered to a coarser batch's); demotion (levels following the rows after removals); dissolution (removing a degree-2 split vertex); split restoration; prepared contact (a vertex placed for a coarse insertion's contact, §3.3 rule 3); hot pixel (the route's placement tolerance, §3.6); contact name (an anchor row naming a bank point for a water batch).

Stretch (StretchRef: a chain's edges between two of its vertices), knot profile (ChainProfile: a value varying along a chain, knots on the chain's vertices), knot role (the registry role per profiled attribute) and cut knot (a knot row carrying the profile's sample at a cut vertex).
Role (a (role, entity, level, ordinal) row on an edge pair or vertex from the role registry); structural role vs partition role; indexed role (rows carry an ordinal).

Pseudo-district: a district record that is not a surface district of the settlement — the hinterland, the sky pseudo-districts (II.6), the underground pseudo-district (II.7.3) and each undercity neighbourhood (II.7.5).

Occupants' band = Plot.fieldBand: the plot's current prosperity-field band (with its own hysteresis memory), read by the interior; distinct from the manifested band (what the geometry reads, bounded by the geometry floor) and from builtBand (what the stock was built for) and DerivationRecord.band (what the last derivation read) — the three band memories.
Geometry floor: derived at read from builtBand and FieldBands.middle by §4.11's floor rule, never stored; bounds what is built (the shell), never the interior.

Plan-rung geometry vocabulary: extent (a wing's ring, and above the ground its ring ∪ its span ring); span ring (the part of a spanned passage's face under a wing, derived at read); seed ring (an extent clipped to tile, the transient arena's seed); fixed ring (a ring passed unmoved — stair bay, chimney stack, passage room, composer's rooms); clip order (the order the seed clip takes wings and towers); container (a wing whose extent wholly contains another's).

Boundary run (a part of a wing ring lying on the footprint boundary, a run of the footprint's rings vertex for vertex) and pairing (tiled vs overlapping: whether every directed wing edge is a footprint edge or the reverse of exactly one other wing's edge).

Canonical prior (the stored plan where one exists, else the as-built plan carried along the interior ladder) and canonical chain (the fixed order of least-disruption steps from the as-built plan to (r, n)); as-built plan (the class's programme at the plot's builtBand with households.built clamped).

Fact tier (dossier | declared | map: who holds an attribute's value), dossier ref (Identity.dossier / Assignment.dossier), dossier paths (per-kind attribute paths a dossier may own), binding key (§7.7 item 12's key of a dossier element).

Existence state (one per entity) vs lifecycle flags (orthogonal: locked, pinned, edited, assigned); tombstone (the archived record of a demolished or superseded entity); archive (where tombstones live, out of the working set).

Digests: model digest (Merkle root of the model); records digest (root over persisted derivation and naming records); provenance digest (provenance, derivation and naming records — the locality audit only); document digest (canonical bytes); leaf digest (an entity's leaf in the model tree); inputs digest (an elaboration record's recorded inputs).

Load vocabulary: working state (the decoded model accepting edits); verification replay (the parallel replay to h0 comparing roots); root of record (a rebased base's stateDigest or later upgrade's baseDigest for a version); frozen view (a document outside the retention window, view and export only); corrupt cache (a root or chunk-hash mismatch); keep the saved town / take the replayed town / trust the saved town (the user's choices).
Pack set (every pack the base recipe or any adjust of the pack list names) and skeleton file (a document's declared subset as its own file).

Wall vocabulary: trace (the wall's L1 chain), wall strip (the L1 face S7 cuts beside the trace), band (the L3 half-bands on each side of the wall chain), setback (unbuildable band beyond), glacis, berm, intervallum (the lane inside the wall).
Building ladder rungs: outline -> wings -> rooms -> plan (Composition.lod); a lazy rung is one derived on click with its own elaboration record; the plan rung is the fourth rung.

HOMONYM "rung": (a) a building-ladder rung (outline, wings, rooms, plan); (b) the settlement size rung (TOWN / CITY / METROPOLIS; Recipe.rung; "the rungs' target populations", "an epoch's upward rung crossing"); (c) a wealth-ladder rung of item 31 (rung 1 wear, rung 2 class change, rung 3 re-cut: "item 31 rung 1", "rung-3 re-cut"); (d) the failure ladder's attempt ("the ladder attempt", Provenance.attempt). Four concepts share one word; the text disambiguates only by context.

HOMONYM "trace": the wall's trace (Enceinte.trace, the L1 wall chain); a footprint trace (a cleared building, item 8); a superseded wall ring's persisting line; a reclaimed land face "a trace the style sheet may draw"; a drawn trace of Works.before.

where: §2.4 (every record embeds Identity and Lifecycle; "the id and lifecycle fields below are those")
conflicts.statement: §2.4 says every record of §2.4-§2.7 and PART II embeds the Identity and Lifecycle of §2.8, the id and lifecycle fields shown being those; yet these entity records show an id and no lifecycle: Terrain, Junction, SubDistrict, Block, Frontage, PlotBound, SubLocation, Gate, Tower, Castle, Bridge, LandUse, Institution, Household, Person, Faction, Religion, FamilyUnit, Membership, SkyIsland. The text elsewhere gives some of them lifecycle behaviour: slow-change conversions are lifecycle events on the land-use face (§2.3), a Household move is a relocate lifecycle event (§2.6, §2.8), gates follow the decline ladder (§2.8). Either the fields are implicit (then the sentence "the id and lifecycle fields below are those" is wrong) or they are missing.

Basement.floors is "storeys below ground, >= 1" and in the same comment "0 for a crawl space"; the requested crawl space sets floors: 0. The range statement contradicts itself (>= 1 versus 0 for crawl).

§2.3 gives each slow-change conversion "cause convert:<kind> (§2.8)", but §2.8 types LifecycleEvent.cause as EditRef | RuleRef | 'generation' with no convert:<kind> form (convert is not a cause value there; it may be a RuleRef or an EditRef's kind, which the text does not say).

ContextVector.arena is 'ground'|'underground' only, yet plots exist on sky islands (sky pseudo-districts receive allocations, II.6; the island is handed to the unit run, II.1) — the arena value a sky plot's context vector takes, and so which arena-specific granularity and designation rows it reads, is undefined.
"Building.basement is derived by the same function, never rolled alone" follows the Entrances paragraph (deriveEntrances) and echoes deriveBase; which function derives the basement is not named.

where: §2.2 rule 5 (no entity record stores a vertex position, with listed exceptions)
conflicts.statement: SkyIsland.outline stores a polygon of world points; rule 5 lists the only records that may hold vertex positions (building wing rings, stored compositions and plans, tower centres) and allows non-vertex points as attributes. Whether the outline is the island arena's own outer ring (then a stored vertex position outside the allowed list) or a non-vertex attribute (then how it stays in step with the island's arena ring under edits) is not stated.

Assignment references take three shapes (AssignmentRef, Id, Assignment) across Plot, Building, Use and BuildingInput, and ContextVector carries both rosterAssignment? and assignment? with no statement of how they differ.

where: §2.6 Building.households (clamped into [1, capacity] for a residential building)
§2.6 capacity (a slot without houses has capacity 0; floor(...) may be 0)
§2.6 interior ladder (every residential building houses at least one household)
conflicts.statement: A residential building is clamped into [1, capacity] and "every residential building houses ... at least one household", while capacity is 0 for a building S11 builds for a slot without houses (BuildingSlot.unhoused reads as such) and floor(Σ A(s)·(den−num)/(2·den·minRoomCm2)) can be 0 for a very small residential shell; the clamp interval [1, 0] and the at-least-one guarantee then conflict, and the outcome is not defined.
The canonical-form bullet lists view, derived and undo as never canonical but omits Document.elaborations (never canonical per its own comment); the list is incomplete.

§2 uses seven types that are declared only in a volume, never in the base: Rung (V07), TableId (V11), Outfall (V04), Segment (V10), TypedBoundary and FabricStrategyId (V01), DriftBounds (V02). A base record depending on a volume-declared type inverts principle (1) (the base owns what the base builds; Rung alone is used 24 times in the base).

where: §2.2 rule 1 underground levels (part 0 margin role on the underground pseudo-district's record)
